title: 摩根奇幻樂園（Morgan's Wonderland）
paras: Morgan’s Wonderland, located in San Antonio, Texas, is a theme park geared mainly toward mentally or physically disabled children. The park was built by Gordon Hartman, a former real estate developer. The creation of the park was inspired by his daughter, Morgan, who suffers from severe cognitive delay and physical challenges.

The world’s first ultra-accessible family fun park, Morgan’s Wonderland opened in the spring of 2010. Admission for guests with special needs is free, and fees for the general public are set at a much discounted price so that people of all ages and abilities can come together and play in a fun and safe environment.

Completely wheelchair-accessible, the park features 25 acres of attractions including rides, playgrounds, a catch-and-release fishing lake, and picnic areas throughout the park. The rides are custom-designed to accommodate wheelchair riders so that every family member can enjoy the fun. The adapted rides include the Off-Road Adventure, where guests can test their driving skills in sporty vehicles. Moreover, each visitor is offered the option to wear a GPS Adventure Band, which allows them to keep track of each other while in the park. The band also enables them to take part in electronic activities. For example, when the riders scan the band at the Off-Road Adventure, a photo will be taken and sent to their email.

In June 2017, Morgan’s Wonderland celebrated the opening of Morgan’s Inspiration Island. The new expansion is composed of five themed splash pads and a River Boat Adventure Ride. The wheelchair guests can transfer out of their chairs into unique, waterproof chairs and enjoy the splash park without risking damage to their personal wheelchairs.

“Morgan taught me that there’s more to life in many ways than what I saw before,” said Hartman. “The blessing that Morgan has brought is beyond anything that I ever could have imagined and could explain.”

outline: 介紹德州的摩根奇幻樂園，主要服務身心障礙兒童，創辦人 Hartman 的靈感來自女兒 Morgan。
2010 年開幕，是全球第一座無障礙家庭樂園，身障者免費入場。
園區完全無障礙，設施都能讓輪椅使用者遊玩，(Moreover) 還提供 GPS 手環，(For example) 掃描後會自動拍照寄出。
(In June 2017) 新開幕的戲水區提供防水輪椅。
Hartman 說 Morgan 帶給他的祝福超乎想像。

zh: 摩根奇幻樂園位在德州聖安東尼奧，是一座主要為身心障礙兒童設計的主題樂園。樂園由前房地產開發商 Gordon Hartman 興建，建園的靈感來自他的女兒 Morgan，Morgan 有嚴重的認知發展遲緩和肢體障礙。
摩根奇幻樂園是全世界第一座「超無障礙」的家庭遊樂園，2010 年春天開幕。有特殊需求的遊客免費入園，一般民眾的門票也大幅打折，讓各種年齡、各種能力的人都能聚在一起，在有趣又安全的環境裡玩樂。

樂園全區都能讓輪椅通行，25 英畝的園區裡有遊樂設施、遊戲場、釣了再放生的釣魚湖，四處還有野餐區。遊樂設施都經過特別設計，坐輪椅也能搭乘，讓每一位家人都能同樂。這些經過改造的設施包括「越野冒險」，遊客可以開著跑車造型的車子測試駕駛技術。此外，每位遊客都可以選擇戴上 GPS 冒險手環，在園區裡隨時掌握彼此的位置。手環也能讓遊客參加電子互動活動，例如在越野冒險掃描手環，就會拍下照片，寄到遊客的電子信箱。
2017 年 6 月，摩根奇幻樂園慶祝「摩根靈感島」開幕。這個新擴建的園區有五座主題戲水區和一項河船冒險設施。坐輪椅的遊客可以換坐特製的防水椅，盡情享受戲水樂園，不必擔心弄壞自己的輪椅。
Hartman 說：「Morgan 讓我明白，人生在許多方面，比我以前所看到的還要豐富。」「Morgan 帶給我的福氣，遠遠超過我所能想像，也超過我能解釋的。」

Completely wheelchair-accessible, the park features 25 acres of attractions including rides, playgrounds, a catch-and-release fishing lake, and picnic areas throughout the park.
In June 2017, Morgan’s Wonderland celebrated the opening of Morgan’s Inspiration Island.

title: 人字拖的歷史與影響（The History and Impact of Flip-flops）
paras: The flip-flop is the simplest shoe on the planet. It consists of a piece of rubber, plastic, leather, or woven material in the outline of a foot, with a strap holding the sandal to a wearer’s toes. The name comes from the sound the sandals make when they slap the walking feet.

The earliest record of people wearing the flip-flop comes from Egypt, but many ancient cultures had their own variants of the footwear. In the Greek version, the toe strap ran between the first and second toes, while Roman sandals had the strap between the second and third toes. The Mesopotamians wore the strap between the third and fourth toes. In India, “toe knob” sandals had a knob between the first and second toes.

Modern flip-flops derive from Japanese zōris, which were often worn with socks dividing the big toe from the rest, and were typically made of rice straw. During World War II, Japan seized much of Southeast Asia’s rubber. In 1945, devastated from the war, the country set about establishing a cheap industry that could rebuild its economy. The Japanese used their rubber reserves from the war to mass-produce the simplest Japanese footwear. Rubber thus replaced rice straw as the major material for the flip-flop.

In the 1950s, flip-flops became popular in the United States as soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home. The sandals have subsequently undergone redesign, often appearing in bright colors in line with Californian beach culture. They have remained popular due to their convenience, and are often worn with bathing suits or summer clothing. Some people also wear dressy versions for more formal occasions.

Despite their popularity, flip-flops provoke some questions. Their simple design is responsible for many foot injuries. Another issue is the suitability of exposing feet on the street and places other than the beach. But even more serious is their environmental impact: Millions of plastic discards end up in landfills or the ocean, releasing chemicals and at the same time taking centuries to decompose.

outline: 介紹人字拖是最簡單的鞋子，名稱來自走路時拍打腳底的聲音。
最早的紀錄來自埃及，(but) 許多古文明各有樣式，(while) 希臘、羅馬、美索不達米亞、印度的夾腳位置各不相同。
現代人字拖源自日本草鞋，(During World War II) 日本掌握大量橡膠，(In 1945) 戰後用橡膠量產，(thus) 橡膠取代了稻草。
(In the 1950s) 美軍把草鞋帶回美國，重新設計後流行至今。
(Despite their popularity) 人字拖也引發問題：容易受傷、場合是否合宜，(But even more serious) 更嚴重的是對環境的衝擊。

zh: 人字拖是世界上最簡單的鞋子，用一片橡膠、塑膠、皮革或編織材料做成腳的形狀，再用一條帶子把鞋固定在腳趾上。英文名稱 flip-flop 來自走路時鞋子拍打腳底的聲音。
最早有人穿人字拖的紀錄來自埃及，不過許多古文明都有自己的版本。希臘式的腳趾帶穿過大拇趾和第二趾之間，羅馬涼鞋的帶子則在第二趾和第三趾之間，美索不達米亞人的帶子在第三趾和第四趾之間。印度則有一種「趾鈕」涼鞋，大拇趾和第二趾之間有一個圓鈕。
現代的人字拖源自日本的草履。草履通常用稻草編成，常搭配把大拇趾和其他腳趾分開的襪子來穿。二次世界大戰期間，日本奪取了東南亞大部分的橡膠。1945 年，飽受戰爭摧殘的日本著手建立低成本的產業來重建經濟，用戰時囤積的橡膠大量生產這種最簡單的日本鞋子。於是橡膠取代稻草，成為人字拖的主要材料。
1950 年代，從美軍占領下的日本返國的士兵把草履帶回家，人字拖便在美國流行起來。此後這種涼鞋經過重新設計，常以鮮豔的顏色出現，和加州的海灘文化相互呼應。人字拖穿脫方便，所以一直很受歡迎，常搭配泳裝或夏季服裝；也有人在比較正式的場合穿講究一點的款式。
人字拖雖然受歡迎，也引發一些問題。人字拖的設計太簡單，許多腳傷都是這樣造成的。另一個問題是，在街上和海灘以外的地方露出雙腳是否合宜。不過更嚴重的是人字拖對環境的衝擊：數以百萬計的廢棄塑膠拖鞋最後進了垃圾掩埋場或海洋，不但釋放化學物質，還要好幾百年才能分解。

In the 1950s, flip-flops became popular in the United States as soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home.
Despite their popularity, flip-flops provoke some questions.

title: 引水人的專業（The Profession of Marine Pilot）
paras: Ships are the lifeline of trade among countries. Almost everything, from food to machinery, comes by way of the sea in huge ships piloted by captains. But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor. The task of bringing the ship into the harbor and anchoring it is taken up by a different captain. This captain is called a marine pilot.

A marine pilot is a boat pilot with specialized knowledge of a particular port or harbor. The pilot is needed to direct large ships into a port, where there are often deep water channels surrounded by shallower seabeds. Without the services of a marine pilot, docking ships would be hazardous. There would be a real chance of running aground and damaging the ship and the cargo, some of which might be dangerous if released into a water-based ecosystem.

In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port. During different tides, currents may change from one direction to the other. The same strategy for docking a vessel during an incoming tide may not work during an outgoing tide. Also, the wind can significantly alter the direction of the ship and how it reacts, adding to the difficulty of anchoring the ship.

Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking. Above all, it is about risk management. A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time and controls the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand. The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.

(In addition to) 除了淺灘，潮汐也讓入港更困難，(Also) 風會改變船的方向。
引水人需要高度專業與獨立快速的判斷，(Above all) 最重要的是風險管理。

zh: 船舶是國際貿易的命脈。從糧食到機械，幾乎所有東西都由船長駕駛的巨型船隻經海路運來。不過船長只負責把船開到港口、等候進港為止；把船帶進港內並下錨停泊的工作，則交給另一位船長，這位船長就叫做引水人（marine pilot），俗稱領港。
引水人是對某個港口有專門知識的船隻駕駛。港口常有深水航道，四周卻是比較淺的海床，所以需要引水人引導大型船隻進港。少了引水人，船隻靠岸會很危險，很可能擱淺，損壞船身和貨物；有些貨物一旦流進水域的生態系，還可能造成危害。
除了海床較淺，潮汐和風也讓船隻進港更加困難。漲潮和退潮時，海流的方向可能完全相反，漲潮時讓船靠岸的方法，退潮時不一定行得通。此外，風也會大幅改變船的方向和反應，讓停泊更加困難。
引水人這份工作需要高度的專業，也需要能迅速、獨立地思考。最重要的是，這份工作講究的是風險管理。引水人在關鍵時刻登船，根據自己對港口和當下狀況的了解來操控船隻。引水人不但要負責船的安全，也要保護港口和海洋環境。

In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port.
Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking.

title: 橄欖油的等級與保存（The Grades and Storage of Olive Oil）
paras: Probably the most widely used oil in cooking, olive oil is made by crushing olives with stone or steel blades to release the oil. Extra virgin oil, the finest grade, is made from the first pressing of the olives and has a very low acidity rate (under 1%). To be qualified as “extra virgin,” the oil must also pass both an official test in a laboratory and a sensory evaluation by a trained tasting panel. It must be free from impurity, while exhibiting some fruitiness and creating a pleasant bitter flavor along with a peppery sensation in the mouth. Second on the ranking is virgin olive oil. It is also a first pressing, but has a slightly higher acidity level (under 2%). Lastly, pure olive oil is the cheapest olive oil. It is refined to remove its impurities and blended to improve flavor, and is recommended for all-purpose cooking.

Packaging and storage also have an impact on the quality of olive oil. Olive oil spoils quickly when exposed to direct sunlight, so it should be stored in the dark at 16-18°C. Moisture and oxygen promote oxidation and therefore limit its shelf life. Plastic containers usually do not provide adequate protection from light, heat, or moisture; additionally, small particles in plastics can leak into the oil, which further reduces its quality.

Olive oil tasters have long adopted descriptive terms such as “pure” and “light” to evaluate the quality of olive oil. Recently, however, the International Olive Council (IOC) is seeking input on test methods to improve the transparency of the testing process and boost the accuracy of the results. A redefinition of the term “olive oil” is also proposed to make a clear distinction between virgin olive oil and pure olive oil. Industry members of the IOC hope to promote the trade of olive oil by initiating these changes.
accuracyRateSource: 大考中心 109 學年度學科能力測驗統計圖表：英文科答對率及鑑別度表

outline: 介紹橄欖油的製法：特級初榨等級最高，是第一道壓榨，酸度低於 1%，還得通過實驗室與品油小組檢驗。
(Second) 次一級是初榨橄欖油，酸度略高，(Lastly) 最便宜的是精製橄欖油，適合一般烹調。
包裝與保存也影響品質：要避光、存放在 16–18°C，濕氣和氧氣會 (therefore) 加速氧化。
塑膠容器擋不住光、熱、濕氣，(additionally) 塑膠微粒還可能滲入油中。
(however) 國際橄欖油理事會正尋求更透明、準確的檢驗方法，並重新定義名稱，以促進貿易。

zh: 橄欖油大概是烹飪時用得最廣的油，製作方式是用石頭或鋼製的刀片壓碎橄欖，讓油流出來。特級初榨橄欖油是最高等級，取自橄欖的第一道壓榨，酸度非常低（低於 1%）。要稱得上「特級初榨」，這種油還必須通過實驗室的官方檢驗，以及受過訓練的品油小組的感官評鑑。它不能有任何雜質，同時要帶點果香，入口有討喜的苦味和胡椒般的辛辣感。排名第二的是初榨橄欖油，同樣是第一道壓榨，但酸度略高（低於 2%）。最後是精製橄欖油，也就是最便宜的橄欖油；它經過精煉去除雜質，再調和改善風味，建議用在一般的烹調。
包裝和保存方式也會影響橄欖油的品質。橄欖油直接照到陽光很快就會變質，所以應該存放在 16 至 18°C 的陰暗處。濕氣和氧氣會促進氧化，因此縮短保存期限。塑膠容器通常無法充分阻隔光線、熱和濕氣；此外，塑膠裡的微粒可能滲入油中，讓品質進一步下降。
長久以來，品油師一直用「純」「淡」這類描述性的字眼來評定橄欖油的品質。不過，國際橄欖油理事會（IOC）最近正在徵詢對檢驗方法的意見，希望提高檢驗過程的透明度，並提升結果的準確性。理事會也提議重新定義「橄欖油」這個名稱，清楚區分初榨橄欖油和精製橄欖油。IOC 的業界成員希望藉由這些改變，促進橄欖油的貿易。

title: 用聲音驅趕鹿隻（Using Sound to Deter Deer）
paras: Researchers in Japan have installed on a train a speaker that barks like a dog and snorts like a deer in order to prevent collisions with animals on the tracks.

The country has been troubled by a problem with trains colliding with deer on its railways. According to Japan’s transport ministry, there were 613 cases of train services suspended or delayed for at least 30 minutes resulting from collisions with deer and other wild animals in 2016-17.

Deer are attracted to railway lines because of a need for iron in their diets. They lick the rails to pick up iron filings caused by the action of wheels against tracks. This dietary need has led to a constant battle to keep the deer separate from the unforgiving nature of tons of onrushing rolling stock. In the past, flashing red lights and even lion faces have been unsuccessfully trialed in an attempt to keep deer off the tracks.

This new device has been invented by a team at the country’s Railway Technical Research Institute (RTRI). RTRI officials explain that deer have a habit of repeatedly snorting short, shrill sounds to alert other deer when they perceive danger. The barking of the hound, which drives deer to panic, strengthens the effect of the warning noise, according to the RTRI. When the deer hear a combination of a 3-second-long recording of a deer’s snort and 20 seconds of a barking dog, they panic and flee rapidly.

RTRI researchers say late-night tests, at times when deer are most frequently seen by railway tracks, have resulted in a 45 percent reduction of deer sighting. Future plans include static barking sites where deer are commonly seen, but “the noises will not be blared in areas where people live beside the tracks.”

outline: 日本研究人員在火車上裝設會發出狗吠與鹿鳴聲的喇叭，防止撞到動物。
日本火車常撞鹿，2016–17 年有 613 次停駛或延誤。
(because) 鹿需要鐵質，會舔鐵軌上的鐵屑，(In the past) 閃爍紅燈、獅子臉都試過，沒有效果。
鐵道綜合技術研究所研發新裝置：鹿鳴警告加上狗吠，(When) 鹿聽到就會驚慌逃走。
夜間測試使鹿出沒減少 45%，(Future plans) 未來將在鹿常出沒處設固定裝置，住宅區除外。
structure.textNote: 這一篇的原文寫的是 the spraying of lion faeces on the track（在鐵軌上噴灑獅子糞便），試題改寫成 lion faces（獅子臉），第 54 題選項 (D) 也跟著寫成 Lion face paintings。大考中心在試題反映意見回覆中表示，本題沒有作答困難，未來改寫用字會以更嚴謹的方式處理。本題庫照試卷原樣收錄。

zh: 日本的研究人員在火車上裝了一個喇叭，可以發出狗吠聲和鹿鳴聲，用來防止火車撞上軌道上的動物。
火車在鐵路上撞到鹿，一直是日本頭痛的問題。根據日本國土交通省的資料，2016 至 2017 年間，因為撞上鹿和其他野生動物，火車停駛或延誤 30 分鐘以上的情形共有 613 起。
鹿之所以靠近鐵路，是因為飲食中需要鐵質。車輪和鐵軌摩擦會產生鐵屑，鹿就舔鐵軌來攝取這些鐵屑。這種飲食上的需求，讓人們不斷設法讓鹿遠離重達數噸、疾駛而來、毫不留情的列車。過去也曾經試過閃爍的紅燈，甚至獅子的臉，想讓鹿遠離鐵軌，但都沒有成功。
這個新裝置是日本鐵道綜合技術研究所（RTRI）的團隊發明的。RTRI 的人員說明，鹿察覺危險時，習慣重複發出短促尖銳的鳴聲，警告其他的鹿。RTRI 表示，狗吠聲會讓鹿陷入恐慌，可以加強警告聲的效果。鹿聽到 3 秒的鹿鳴錄音加上 20 秒的狗吠聲，就會驚慌失措，迅速逃開。
RTRI 的研究人員說，他們在鹿最常出現在鐵軌旁的深夜時段進行測試，結果看到鹿的次數減少了 45%。未來計畫在鹿經常出現的地點設置固定的狗吠裝置，不過「鐵軌旁有住家的地區不會播放這些聲音」。

title: 神仙魚的變性能力（The Gender-Changing Angelfish）
paras: Angelfish, often found in the warm seas and coral reefs, are among the most brightly colored fish of the ocean. Brilliant colors and stripes form amazing patterns on their body. These patterns actually help the fish to hide from danger among roots and plants. At night, when these fish become inactive, their colors may become pale. Often, the young ones are differently colored than the adults. Some scientists believe that the color difference between the young and the old indicates their different social positions.

Another interesting fact about angelfish is that they have an occupation in the fish world. Most of them act as cleaners for other fish and pick dead tissue from their bodies. This is not their food, though. Their diet consists mainly of sponge and algae.

One particular kind of angelfish, the blackspot angelfish, has a special capability that allows it to change gender from female to male. However, the change is not made at random; it happens for a specific reason. Angelfish live in groups, and each group has one male fish, which is blue in color, and four female fish, which are yellow. The male angelfish is the strongest and largest member of the group. He is the one who protects and looks after the females. When the male dies, the group needs a new “security guard.” This is when the largest female in the group begins to change in appearance. She begins to grow larger in size, and after a week, she starts changing color, from yellow to blue. Slowly, her behavior toward the other fish also changes. She begins behaving like a male. Two weeks later, black stripes appear on her body, indicating the gender change is complete. She is now completely male!

outline: 介紹神仙魚色彩鮮豔，(actually) 花紋其實能幫助躲避危險，夜間顏色變淡，幼魚與成魚顏色不同。
(Another) 神仙魚會替其他魚清除死皮，(though) 但那不是食物，主食是海綿和藻類。
黑斑神仙魚能從雌性變為雄性，(However) 這不是隨機發生，而是有特定原因。
每群有一條藍色雄魚和四條黃色雌魚，(When) 雄魚死後，群體需要新的守衛。
(This is when) 最大的雌魚先變大，一週後變色，(Slowly) 行為也改變，(Two weeks later) 出現黑色條紋，變性完成。

zh: 神仙魚常見於溫暖的海域和珊瑚礁，是海洋中色彩最鮮豔的魚類之一。亮麗的色彩和條紋在牠們身上形成令人驚嘆的花紋，這些花紋其實能幫助牠們躲在樹根和植物之間，避開危險。到了晚上，神仙魚不太活動，顏色可能會變淡。幼魚的顏色也常常和成魚不同，有些科學家認為，這種顏色上的差異代表牠們在群體中的地位不同。
神仙魚另一個有趣的地方，是牠們在魚類世界裡有一份「職業」。大部分的神仙魚替其他魚當清潔工，啄掉牠們身上的死皮。不過，這些死皮並不是牠們的食物，牠們主要吃的是海綿和藻類。

有一種神仙魚叫黑斑神仙魚，具有一種特殊的能力，可以從雌性變成雄性。不過，這種轉變不是隨機發生的，而是有特定的原因。神仙魚成群生活，每一群有一條藍色的雄魚和四條黃色的雌魚。雄魚是群體裡最強壯、體型最大的成員，負責保護和照顧雌魚。雄魚死掉之後，群體需要一位新的「守衛」，這時群體裡最大的雌魚就開始改變外觀。牠先是體型開始變大，一週之後，顏色從黃色變成藍色。接著，牠對其他魚的行為也慢慢改變，開始表現得像雄魚。兩週之後，牠身上出現黑色條紋，表示變性已經完成。牠現在完全是一條雄魚了！

title: 北美原住民的圖騰柱（Totem Poles in North America）
paras: Totem poles in North America are poles or posts carved with symbols or figures by Aboriginal peoples of the Northwest Coast. Carved from large, straight trees and painted vibrant colors, the totem poles are not just unique works of art. The coastal peoples have long passed on knowledge from generation to generation through oral traditions, and totem poles were the traditional way of telling the story of an individual family or clan.

The totem pole can be grouped into specific categories, depending on its location and the occasion for which it was carved. Welcome poles were traditionally placed on village beachfronts to greet visitors arriving by canoe. Inside the homes of high-ranking chiefs is where house poles were found. The family’s history was carefully carved into each pole. Placed along the rear or front walls of a house, house poles also helped to support the main beam of the roof.

Memorial poles stood in front of a house. They were erected in memory of a deceased chief or a high-ranking clan member. The poles depicted the person’s accomplishments or family history. Mortuary poles were also raised to honor the dead, but they differed from memorial poles, having a burial box placed at the top of the pole. Inside the burial box were the remains of the deceased.

While many of these poles can still be found in various locations on the west coast of North America, there is one pole that can now only be found in a museum—the shame pole. Traditionally, shame poles were carved for a chief to embarrass and ridicule another who had done something wrong. Once the wrong was made right, the pole was taken down.

Totem poles are important expressions of specific Aboriginal cultures. Despite the threats posed by cultural and political encroachment of colonial forces, the art of totem pole carving has survived. Aboriginal carvers continue to carve totems as symbols of their cultural pride and clan kinship.
accuracyRateSource: 大考中心 108 學年度學科能力測驗統計圖表：英文科答對率及鑑別度表

outline: 介紹北美西北岸原住民的圖騰柱，(not just) 不只是藝術品，也是口傳家族與氏族歷史的方式。
依位置與用途分類：迎賓柱立在海灘迎接訪客；屋柱立在酋長家中，刻著家族歷史，(also) 也支撐屋頂大梁。
紀念柱立在屋前紀念過世的酋長或族人，(also) 墓葬柱也是紀念死者，(but) 但頂端放有葬箱，裡面是遺骸。
(While) 多數圖騰柱仍可在北美西岸看到，羞辱柱現在只在博物館，(Once) 錯誤改正後柱子就會拆下。
(Despite) 儘管殖民勢力在文化與政治上入侵，雕刻藝術仍流傳至今，象徵文化自豪與氏族情誼。

zh: 北美的圖騰柱，是西北海岸的原住民刻上符號或人物圖案的柱子。圖騰柱取材自高大筆直的樹木，雕刻之後漆上鮮豔的色彩，不只是獨特的藝術品。沿海的原住民長久以來靠口述傳統，把知識一代一代傳下去，圖騰柱就是他們講述某個家族或氏族故事的傳統方式。
圖騰柱可以依照設立的位置和雕刻的場合，分成幾個類別。迎賓柱傳統上立在村落的海灘邊，迎接划獨木舟來訪的客人。屋柱則設在地位崇高的酋長家中，每一根都仔細刻上家族的歷史。屋柱立在房屋的後牆或前牆邊，也幫忙支撐屋頂的大梁。
紀念柱立在房屋前面，用來紀念過世的酋長或地位崇高的氏族成員，柱上刻畫這個人的功績或家族歷史。墓葬柱同樣是為了紀念死者而立，但和紀念柱不同的是，墓葬柱的頂端放了一個葬箱，裡面安放著死者的遺骸。
這些圖騰柱有許多到現在仍然可以在北美西岸各地看到，但有一種柱子現在只能在博物館裡看到，那就是羞辱柱。傳統上，酋長會刻羞辱柱，讓另一位做錯事的酋長難堪、受人嘲笑；等對方把錯誤彌補好，柱子就會拆下來。
圖騰柱是特定原住民文化的重要表現。儘管殖民勢力在文化和政治上的侵逼帶來威脅，圖騰柱的雕刻藝術仍然流傳了下來。原住民雕刻師至今仍持續雕刻圖騰柱，作為他們文化自豪與氏族情誼的象徵。

title: 「腦中神曲」現象（Earworms）
paras: Music has a tendency to get stuck in our heads. Sometimes a tune intrudes on our thoughts and then plays, and replays, in a never-ending loop. This interesting phenomenon becomes a subject explored by many scientists. They use a range of terms to describe it—stuck-song syndrome, sticky music, cognitive itch, or most commonly “earworm.” Earworms can run around our heads for several minutes to numerous hours. As the melody repeats, it becomes embedded into our mind. Even though our ears do not hear the tune, our brain continues to play it.

Earworms often take the form of song fragments rather than entire songs, and the song is usually a familiar one. Researchers are not sure why some songs are more likely to get stuck in our heads than others, but everyone has their own tunes. Often those songs have a simple, upbeat melody and catchy, repetitive lyrics, such as popular commercial jingles and slightly annoying radio hits. Recent or repeated exposure to a song or even a small part of a song can also trigger earworms, as can word associations, such as a phrase similar to the lyrics of a song.

While earworms might be annoying, most people who experience them nevertheless report that they are pleasant or at least neutral. Only a third of people are disturbed by the song in their heads. How people cope with their earworms seems to depend on how they feel about them. Those who have positive feelings about their stuck songs prefer to just “let them be,” while those with negative feelings turn to more behavioral responses, which include coping strategies such as singing, talking, or even praying.
accuracyRateSource: 大考中心 108 學年度學科能力測驗統計圖表：英文科答對率及鑑別度表

outline: 音樂常卡在腦中不斷重播，科學家稱這個現象為「耳蟲」等名稱。
耳蟲可持續數分鐘到數小時，(Even though) 耳朵沒聽到，大腦仍繼續播放。
耳蟲常是熟悉歌曲的片段，(but) 每個人的耳蟲不同，旋律簡單輕快、歌詞重複的歌最容易卡住。
最近或反覆聽到某首歌，(also) 或聽到和歌詞相似的字句，也會引發耳蟲。
(While) 耳蟲雖然惱人，(nevertheless) 多數人覺得愉快或無所謂；有正面感受的人順其自然，(while) 負面感受的人會唱歌、說話或祈禱來應付。

zh: 音樂很容易卡在腦子裡。有時候一段旋律闖進我們的思緒，接著不停播放、重播，沒完沒了。這個有趣的現象成了許多科學家研究的主題，他們用各種名稱來描述它：卡歌症候群、黏人音樂、認知搔癢，最常用的是「耳蟲」。耳蟲可以在腦中盤旋幾分鐘到好幾個小時。旋律一再重複，就深深嵌進我們的腦海；即使耳朵沒有聽到這段旋律，大腦還是繼續播放。
耳蟲常常是歌曲的片段，而不是整首歌，而且通常是熟悉的歌。研究人員不確定為什麼有些歌比其他歌更容易卡在腦中，不過每個人都有自己的耳蟲歌。這些歌常常旋律簡單輕快，歌詞朗朗上口、一再重複，像是流行的廣告歌曲，以及有點煩人的電台熱門歌曲。最近聽過或反覆聽到一首歌，甚至只是歌曲的一小段，都可能引發耳蟲；字詞的聯想也會，例如聽到和某首歌歌詞相似的句子。
耳蟲雖然可能惱人，大部分有過這種經驗的人卻表示，感覺是愉快的，至少無所謂，只有三分之一的人會因為腦中的歌感到困擾。人們怎麼應付耳蟲，似乎取決於他們對耳蟲的感受。對卡在腦中的歌有正面感受的人，寧願「隨它去」；有負面感受的人則會採取比較多的行動，像是唱歌、說話，甚至祈禱，來應付耳蟲。

title: 除蟲炸彈的無效性（The Ineffectiveness of Bug Bombs）
paras: Got a bug bite problem? Many people who are troubled by skin rashes caused by bug bites use “foggers,” or “bug bombs,” to get rid of the annoying crawlers in their homes. Many people think these bug killers or pesticides will penetrate every place where the insects hide. Actually, quite the opposite is true. Once the pests detect the chemical fog in the room, they’ll hide themselves in walls or other hideaways, where you’ll never be able to treat them effectively.

Ohio State University researchers tested three commercially sold foggers in a study on the effect of foggers on bedbugs. After testing these brands on five different groups of live bedbugs for two hours, the scientists saw that the foggers had little—if any—effect on the insects. The researchers said bedbugs hide in cracks and crevices such as under sheets and mattresses, or deep in carpets where foggers won’t reach. Moreover, bugs that do come in contact with the mist may be resistant to the pesticide.

Foggers, or bug bombs, should really be a measure of last resort. First of all, the gases used in bug bombs are highly flammable and thus pose a serious risk of fire or explosion if the product is not used properly. Second, once a bug bomb is used, every surface in your home will be covered with the toxic pesticide. When you use a bug bomb, a chemical mixture rains down on your counters, furniture, floors, and walls, leaving behind oily and toxic substances. Your health might thus be endangered. Therefore, it is suggested that people leave the problem to the professionals.
accuracyRateSource: 大考中心 108 學年度學科能力測驗統計圖表：英文科答對率及鑑別度表

outline: 許多人用除蟲噴霧彈對付咬人的蟲，以為藥劑能滲透每個角落，(Actually) 事實正好相反，蟲會躲進牆裡。
俄亥俄州立大學測試三種市售除蟲彈，發現對床蝨幾乎無效，因為床蝨躲在縫隙、床墊下、地毯深處。
(Moreover) 接觸到藥霧的蟲也可能有抗藥性。
除蟲彈應是最後手段，(First of all) 氣體易燃，有爆炸風險，(Second) 有毒藥劑會留在家中各處表面，危害健康。
(Therefore) 建議把問題交給專業人員處理。

zh: 有蟲咬的困擾嗎？許多人因為蟲咬引起皮膚起疹子，就用「噴霧器」，也就是「除蟲彈」，來消滅家裡惱人的小蟲。很多人以為這些殺蟲劑能滲透到蟲子藏身的每個地方，事實上正好相反。害蟲一察覺室內的化學藥霧，就會躲進牆壁或其他藏身處，在那裡你永遠沒辦法有效地處理牠們。
俄亥俄州立大學的研究人員研究除蟲彈對床蝨的效果，測試了三種市售的除蟲彈。他們用這幾個品牌對五組活的床蝨測試兩個小時後，發現除蟲彈對這些蟲子幾乎沒有效果，甚至毫無效果。研究人員說，床蝨會躲在縫隙裡，像是床單和床墊底下，或是地毯深處，這些地方除蟲彈都噴不到。此外，真的接觸到藥霧的蟲子，也可能對殺蟲劑有抗藥性。
除蟲彈其實應該是最後的手段。首先，除蟲彈用的氣體非常易燃，使用不當就有起火或爆炸的嚴重危險。其次，一旦用了除蟲彈，家裡每一個表面都會蓋上一層有毒的殺蟲劑。使用除蟲彈時，化學藥劑會像雨一樣落在流理台、家具、地板和牆壁上，留下油膩、有毒的物質，可能因此危害你的健康。所以，建議大家把這個問題交給專業人員處理。

title: 過度醫療的問題（The Problem of Overtreatment）
paras: When it comes to medical care, many patients and doctors believe “more is better.” But what they do not realize is that overtreatment—too many scans, too many blood tests, too many procedures—may pose harm. Sometimes a test leads you down a path to more and more testing, some of which may be invasive, or to treatment for things that should be left alone.

Terrence Power, for example, complained that after his wife learned she had Wegener’s disease, an uncommon disorder of the immune system, they found it difficult to refuse testing recommended by her physician. The doctor insisted on office visits every three weeks, even when she was feeling well. He frequently ordered blood tests and X-rays, and repeatedly referred her to specialists for even minor complaints. Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered, and she was hospitalized as a precaution when she developed a cold. She had as many as 25 doctor visits during one six-month period. The couple was spending about $30,000 a year for her care.

After several years of physical suffering and near financial ruin from the medical costs, the couple began questioning the treatment after consulting with other patients in online support groups. “It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said. “You think she’s getting the best care in the world, but after a while you start to wonder: What is the objective?” Mr. Power then spoke with his own primary care doctor, who advised him to find a new specialist to oversee Mrs. Power’s care. Under the new doctor’s care, the regular testing stopped and Mrs. Power’s condition stabilized. Now she sees the doctor only four or five times a year.

outline: 許多病人和醫生認為醫療越多越好，(But) 過度醫療其實可能有害，一項檢查常引來更多檢查。
(for example) 以 Power 太太為例：醫生堅持每三週回診，頻繁抽血、照 X 光，連小毛病也轉診專科。
(Even when) 檢查正常仍加做檢查，感冒就住院，半年看診 25 次，一年花費約三萬美元。
(After) 多年身心與經濟的煎熬後，夫妻和網路病友交流，開始質疑治療。
(then) 先生的家庭醫師建議換專科醫師，停止例行檢查後病情穩定，(Now) 現在一年只看診四、五次。

zh: 談到醫療照護，許多病人和醫生都相信「越多越好」。但是他們沒有意識到，過度醫療，也就是太多掃描、太多抽血檢驗、太多醫療程序，可能會造成傷害。有時候一項檢查會帶著你走上越來越多檢查的路，其中有些可能是侵入性的；有時候則會去治療一些原本應該放著不管的問題。

以 Terrence Power 為例，他抱怨妻子得知自己罹患韋格納肉芽腫（一種罕見的免疫系統疾病）之後，兩人發現很難拒絕醫師建議的檢查。醫生堅持她每三週回診一次，即使她覺得身體很好也一樣。醫生經常要她抽血、照 X 光，連小毛病也一再轉診給專科醫師。就算檢查結果正常，醫生還是安排更多檢查；她感冒時，醫生也為了預防萬一讓她住院。在某個半年期間，她看診多達 25 次。這對夫妻每年要花大約三萬美元在她的醫療上。

經過好幾年身體上的折磨，醫療費用也幾乎讓他們破產，這對夫妻在網路病友互助團體裡和其他病人交流之後，開始質疑這些治療。Power 先生說：「醫生什麼時候做得太過頭了，真的很難判斷。你以為她得到的是世界上最好的照顧，但過了一陣子你會開始懷疑：這樣做的目的到底是什麼？」Power 先生後來和自己的家庭醫師談過，醫師建議他另外找一位專科醫師負責 Power 太太的治療。在新醫師的照護下，例行檢查停了，Power 太太的病情也穩定下來。現在她一年只看醫生四、五次。

title: 大規模線上開放課程（MOOCs）
paras: MOOC, a massive open online course, aims at providing large-scale interactive participation and open access via the web. In addition to traditional course materials such as videos, readings, and problem sets, MOOCs provide interactive user forums that help build a community for the students, professors, and teaching assistants.

MOOCs first made waves in the fall of 2011, when Professor Sebastian Thrun from Stanford University opened his graduate-level artificial intelligence course up to any student anywhere, and 160,000 students in more than 190 countries signed up. This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways. Since the courses can be taken by hundreds of thousands of students at the same time, the number of universities might decrease dramatically. Professor Thrun has even envisioned a future in which there will only need to be 10 universities in the world. Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free. This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.

There is a lot of excitement and fear surrounding MOOCs. While some say free online courses are a great way to increase the enrollment of minority students, others have said they will leave many students behind. Some critics have said that MOOCs promote an unrealistic one-size-fits-all model of higher education and that there is no replacement for true dialogues between professors and their students. After all, a brain is not a computer. We are not blank hard drives waiting to be filled with data. People learn from people they love and remember the things that arouse emotion. Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.

zh: MOOC 是大規模線上開放課程，目標是透過網路提供大規模的互動參與和開放的學習管道。除了影片、閱讀材料和習題這些傳統的課程教材，MOOC 還提供互動式的使用者論壇，幫助學生、教授和助教建立一個社群。

MOOC 最早在 2011 年秋天引起轟動：史丹佛大學的 Sebastian Thrun 教授把他研究所程度的人工智慧課程開放給世界各地的任何學生，結果有 190 多個國家、16 萬名學生報名。這種新型態的線上課程在許多方面撼動了高等教育界。由於一門課可以同時讓數十萬名學生修讀，大學的數量可能會大幅減少。Thrun 教授甚至設想，未來全世界只需要 10 所大學。MOOC 有許多是由知名大學的教授授課，而它最引人注目的地方或許是免費。這對手頭很緊的學生來說當然是好消息。
MOOC 帶來許多期待，也引起許多擔憂。有些人說，免費的線上課程是增加少數族群學生入學人數的好方法；也有人說，這種課程會讓許多學生跟不上。有些批評者認為，MOOC 推行的是一種不切實際、一體適用的高等教育模式，而教授和學生之間真正的對話是無可取代的。畢竟，人腦不是電腦，我們不是等著裝滿資料的空白硬碟。人會向自己喜愛的人學習，也會記住引起情緒的事物。有些批評者擔心，線上學生會錯過大學的社交生活。

title: 中東地區的失學兒童（Children Out of School in the Middle East）
paras: Ongoing conflicts across the Middle East have prevented more than 13 million children from attending school, according to a report published by UNICEF, the United Nations Children’s Fund.

The report states that 40% of all children across the region are currently not receiving an education, which is a result of two consequences of violence: structural damage to schools and the displacement of populations, also called “forced migration.” Both issues result from the tide of violence that has crossed the region in recent years. The report examines nine countries where a state of war has become the norm. Across these countries, violence has made 8,500 schools unusable. In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.

The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011. With the crisis now in its fifth year, basic public services, including education, inside Syria have been stretched to breaking point. Within the country, the quality and availability of education depends on whether a particular region is suffering violence.

The report concludes with an earnest request to international policymakers to distribute financial and other resources to ease the regional crisis. With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance. The forces that are crushing individual lives and futures are also destroying the prospects for an entire region.

zh: 根據聯合國兒童基金會發表的一份報告，中東各地持續不斷的衝突，使超過 1,300 萬名兒童無法上學。
報告指出，這個地區所有的兒童中，目前有 40% 沒有接受教育，原因是暴力帶來的兩個後果：學校建築毀損，以及人口流離失所，也就是所謂的「強迫遷徙」。這兩個問題都來自近年席捲這個地區的暴力浪潮。報告調查了九個長期處於戰爭狀態的國家，在這些國家裡，暴力已經使 8,500 所學校無法使用。在某些情況下，社區把學校建築當作流離失所者的收容所，在伊拉克各地原本的學校裡，一間教室最多住了九戶人家。
報告特別關注敘利亞。敘利亞自 2011 年爆發血腥內戰以來，至少已有 900 萬人流離失所。危機如今已進入第五年，敘利亞境內包括教育在內的基本公共服務，都已經不堪負荷、瀕臨崩潰。在敘利亞國內，教育的品質和普及程度，要看某個地區是否正發生暴力衝突。
報告最後懇切呼籲國際決策者，提供資金和其他資源來緩解這個地區的危機。已經有超過 1,300 萬名兒童因為衝突離開教室，說一整個世代兒童的教育前景岌岌可危，一點也不誇張。摧毀個人生命和未來的這股力量，也正在摧毀整個地區的前景。

title: 畫家溫斯洛·霍默（Winslow Homer）
paras: Winslow Homer (1836-1910) is regarded by many as the greatest American painter of the nineteenth century. Born and raised in Boston, he began his career at age eighteen in his hometown, working as an apprentice at a printing company. Skilled at drawing, he soon made a name for himself making illustrations for novels, sheet music, magazines, and children’s books.

He then moved to New York City, where he worked as a freelance illustrator with Harper’s Weekly, a popular magazine of the time, and began painting. Homer was assigned to cover the inauguration of President Lincoln and, later, the Civil War. His pictures of the Union troops won international recognition. Homer moved to England and, after a two-year stay, returned to America. He settled permanently in Maine in 1883.

From the late 1850s until his death in 1910, Winslow Homer produced a body of work distinguished by its thoughtful expression and its independence from artistic conventions. A man of multiple talents, Homer excelled equally in the arts of illustration, oil painting, and watercolor. Many of his works—depictions of children at play and in school, farm girls attending to their work, hunters and their prey—have become classic images of nineteenth-century American life. Others speak to more universal themes such as the primal relationship of humans to nature.

This two-week exhibition highlights a wide and representative range of Homer’s art. It shows his extraordinary career from the battlefields, farmland, and coastal villages of America, to the North Sea fishing village of Cullercoats, the rocky coast of Maine, the Adirondacks, and the Caribbean. The exhibition offers viewers an opportunity to experience and appreciate the breadth of his remarkable artistic achievement.

zh: 許多人認為溫斯洛·霍默（1836–1910）是 19 世紀最偉大的美國畫家。他在波士頓出生長大，十八歲在家鄉展開職業生涯，在一家印刷公司當學徒。他擅長繪畫，很快就以替小說、樂譜、雜誌和兒童書繪製插畫而出名。
後來他搬到紐約市，替當時很受歡迎的雜誌 Harper’s Weekly 擔任自由插畫家，也開始作畫。霍默受派報導林肯總統的就職典禮，後來又報導南北戰爭。他描繪北軍的畫作贏得國際肯定。霍默後來搬到英國，住了兩年後回到美國，1883 年在緬因州定居。
從 1850 年代後期到 1910 年去世，霍默創作了大量作品，特色是表達深刻，而且不受藝術傳統束縛。霍默多才多藝，插畫、油畫和水彩都同樣出色。他的許多作品，像是描繪孩子遊戲和上學、農家女孩忙著做事、獵人和獵物的畫，都已經成為 19 世紀美國生活的經典畫面。其他作品則觸及更普遍的主題，例如人和大自然之間最原始的關係。
這次為期兩週的展覽，展出霍默藝術作品中範圍廣泛又具代表性的一批。展覽呈現他非凡的創作生涯，從美國的戰場、農田和海邊村落，到北海的漁村卡勒科茨、緬因州的岩岸、阿第倫達克山脈和加勒比海。觀眾可以藉這次展覽，體會並欣賞他卓越藝術成就的廣度。

title: 白宮的歷史（The History of the White House）
paras: For more than two hundred years, the White House has stood as a symbol of the United States Presidency, the U.S. government, and the American people. In 1790, President George Washington declared that the federal government would reside in a district “not exceeding ten miles square … on the river Potomac.” As preparations began, a competition was held to find a builder of the “President’s House.” Nine proposals were submitted, and the Irish-born architect James Hoban won the gold medal for his practical and handsome design. Construction began when the first cornerstone was laid in October of 1792. Although President Washington oversaw the construction of the house, he never lived in it. It was not until 1800, when the White House was nearly completed, that its first residents, President John Adams and his wife Abigail, moved in.

American presidents can express their individual style in how they decorate the house and in how they receive the public. Thomas Jefferson held the first inaugural open house in 1805; many of those who attended the swearing-in ceremony at the U.S. Capitol simply followed him home. President Jefferson also opened the house for public tours, and it has remained open, except during wartime, ever since. In addition, Jefferson welcomed visitors to annual receptions on New Year’s Day and on the Fourth of July. Abraham Lincoln did the same, but then the inaugural crowds became far too large for the White House to accommodate comfortably, and this also created a security issue. It was not until Grover Cleveland’s first presidency that some effective crowd control measures were implemented to address the problem caused by this practice.

At various times in history, the White House has been known as the “President’s Palace,” the “President’s House,” and the “Executive Mansion.” President Theodore Roosevelt officially gave the White House its current name in 1901.

outline: 白宮兩百多年來象徵美國總統、政府與人民。
(In 1790) 華盛頓宣布設立聯邦首都特區，(As) 籌備時舉辦設計比賽，愛爾蘭籍建築師霍本勝出，1792 年動工。
(Although) 華盛頓監督興建卻沒住過，(It was not until 1800) 亞當斯夫婦才成為第一批住戶。
傑佛遜首開就職開放日並開放參觀，(In addition) 元旦與國慶也接待訪客，(but then) 林肯時期人潮太多造成安全問題，(It was not until) 到克里夫蘭才實施人潮管制。
白宮曾有多個名稱，1901 年老羅斯福正式定名。

zh: 兩百多年來，白宮一直是美國總統職位、美國政府和美國人民的象徵。1790 年，華盛頓總統宣布聯邦政府將設在波多馬克河畔一個「不超過十英里見方」的特區。籌備工作展開後，政府舉辦了一場比賽，徵求「總統府」的建造者。比賽共收到九件設計提案，出生於愛爾蘭的建築師霍本以實用又美觀的設計贏得金牌。1792 年 10 月，第一塊基石奠下，工程正式開始。華盛頓總統雖然監督了白宮的興建，卻從來沒有住過。一直到 1800 年白宮快要完工時，第一批住戶亞當斯總統和夫人 Abigail 才搬進去。

美國總統可以從白宮的布置和接待民眾的方式，展現個人的風格。傑佛遜在 1805 年舉辦了第一次就職開放日；許多在美國國會大廈參加宣誓典禮的民眾，乾脆跟著他一路回到白宮。傑佛遜總統也開放白宮讓民眾參觀，從此以後，除了戰爭期間，白宮一直對外開放。此外，傑佛遜每年元旦和七月四日國慶日也開放白宮，歡迎訪客。林肯也照著這麼做，但是後來就職的人潮多到白宮無法舒適地容納，也造成了安全問題。一直到克里夫蘭第一次擔任總統時，才實施了一些有效的人潮管制措施，解決這個做法帶來的問題。
白宮在歷史上不同時期，曾經叫做「總統宮」、「總統府」和「行政官邸」。1901 年，老羅斯福總統正式把它定名為現在的名稱。

title: 西尼羅病毒（West Nile Virus）
paras: West Nile is a tropical disease that begins in birds, which pass it on to mosquitoes that then go on to infect human beings with a bite. Most people who contract West Nile do not experience any symptoms at all, but, if they do, symptoms typically develop between 3 to 14 days after a mosquito bite. About 1 in 5 persons suffers fever, headaches, and body aches, usually lasting a week or so. A far less lucky 1 in 150 experiences high fever, tremors, paralysis, and coma. Some—especially the elderly and those with weak immune systems—die.

That is what made the major outbreaks of West Nile in the U.S. in the summer of 2012 so scary. The situation was particularly bad in Dallas, Texas, where the West Nile virus killed 10 people and sickened more than 200. The city declared a state of emergency and began aerial spraying of a pesticide to kill the mosquitoes, even though residents argued that the pesticide could be more dangerous than the disease.

Why was the summer of 2012 so hospitable to the West Nile virus and the mosquitoes that carry it? Blame the weather. An extremely mild winter allowed more mosquitoes than usual to survive, while the unusually high temperatures in that scorching summer further increased their number by speeding up their life cycle. The economic crisis may have also played a role: Homeowners who were not able to pay their bank loans were forced to abandon their properties, sometimes leaving behind swimming pools that made excellent mosquito breeding grounds.

The severity of tropical diseases is also a matter of whether governments are capable—and willing—to defend their populations against infections. Dallas County was not doing some of the key things to slow the spread of West Nile, such as testing dead birds and setting mosquito traps to test for the presence of the disease. Tropical infections are thus as much related to government inaction as they are to climate.

outline: 介紹西尼羅病毒的傳播途徑：鳥傳蚊，蚊子再叮人。
多數感染者沒有症狀，(but) 有些人發燒頭痛，少數人癱瘓昏迷，甚至死亡。
(That is what) 2012 年美國大爆發，達拉斯 10 人死亡、200 多人染病，宣布緊急狀態並空中噴藥，(even though) 居民認為農藥可能比疾病更危險。
原因之一是天氣：暖冬讓更多蚊子存活，酷暑加速繁殖；(also) 經濟危機使屋主棄屋，留下的泳池成了蚊子溫床。
疫情輕重 (also) 也取決於政府作為，達拉斯沒有檢測死鳥、設捕蚊器，(thus) 熱帶傳染病和政府不作為、氣候都有關。

zh: 西尼羅病毒會引起一種熱帶疾病。病毒最先出現在鳥類身上，鳥再把病毒傳給蚊子，蚊子接著叮人，把病毒傳染給人類。大部分感染西尼羅病毒的人完全沒有症狀；如果出現症狀，通常是在蚊子叮咬後 3 到 14 天之間。大約五分之一的人會發燒、頭痛、全身痠痛，通常持續一個星期左右。比較不幸的，大約每 150 人有 1 人會高燒、顫抖、癱瘓甚至昏迷。有些人會因此死亡，特別是年長者和免疫系統較弱的人。
正因為這樣，2012 年夏天西尼羅病毒在美國大爆發，才會那麼令人害怕。德州達拉斯的情況特別嚴重，病毒在當地造成 10 人死亡、200 多人染病。達拉斯市宣布進入緊急狀態，開始從空中噴灑農藥撲殺蚊子，儘管居民認為農藥可能比疾病本身還危險。
為什麼 2012 年夏天特別適合西尼羅病毒和傳播病毒的蚊子？要怪天氣。極為溫和的冬天讓比平常更多的蚊子活了下來，那年夏天又異常炎熱，高溫加快了蚊子的生命週期，數量因此更多。經濟危機可能也有影響：付不出銀行貸款的屋主不得不棄屋離開，有時留下的游泳池正好成了蚊子絕佳的繁殖場所。
熱帶疾病嚴不嚴重，也要看政府有沒有能力、有沒有意願保護人民不受感染。達拉斯郡沒有做到一些減緩西尼羅病毒擴散的關鍵措施，例如檢驗死鳥、設置捕蚊器來檢測病毒是否存在。因此，熱帶傳染病和政府不作為的關係，跟它和氣候的關係一樣密切。

title: 海水淡化（Desalination）
paras: Most parts of Taiwan have access to sufficient supplies of fresh water for drinking. But fresh water can be in short supply in many arid regions of the world such as Saudi Arabia, where there are limited water resources. As the world population continues to grow, shortages of fresh water will occur more often and the need for additional water supplies will become critical. Some may ask, “Since the ocean covers more than 70 percent of the Earth, why not just get drinking water from the ocean?”

To turn seawater into fresh water, we need to remove the salt in seawater, that is, to desalinate seawater. The problem is that the desalination of water requires a lot of energy. Salt dissolves very easily in water, forming strong chemical bonds, and those bonds are difficult to break. The energy and technology to desalinate water are both expensive, and this means that desalinating water can be costly.

There are environmental costs of desalination as well. Sea life can get sucked into desalination plants, killing small ocean creatures like baby fish and plankton, upsetting the food chain. Also, there is the problem of what to do with the separated salt, which is left over as a very concentrated brine. Pumping this super-salty water back into the ocean can harm local aquatic life. Reducing these impacts is possible, but it adds to the costs.

Despite the economic and environmental hurdles, desalination is becoming increasingly attractive as human beings are using up fresh water from other sources. At present, desalinating seawater is the only viable way to provide water to growing populations in rural areas of the Middle East and North Africa. Therefore, the race is on to find a cheaper, cleaner, and more energy-efficient way of desalinating seawater, and promising new findings are being reported.

outline: 台灣多數地方淡水充足，(But) 沙烏地阿拉伯等乾旱地區缺水，人口成長將使缺水更嚴重，有人問何不取用海水。
(that is) 海水要淡化才能喝，(The problem is that) 但淡化耗能，成本很高。
(as well) 淡化也有環境代價：吸入海洋生物、破壞食物鏈，(Also) 濃鹽水排回海中會傷害生態。
(Despite) 儘管有經濟與環境障礙，淡化越來越受重視，(At present) 目前是中東、北非鄉村唯一可行的供水方式。
(Therefore) 各方競相研發更便宜、乾淨、節能的淡化技術，也已有可喜的發現。

zh: 台灣大部分地方都有充足的淡水可以飲用。不過，世界上許多乾旱地區的淡水可能供應不足，例如水資源有限的沙烏地阿拉伯。隨著世界人口持續成長，淡水短缺會越來越常發生，增加供水也會變得非常迫切。有些人可能會問：「既然海洋覆蓋了地球百分之七十以上的面積，為什麼不乾脆從海洋取得飲用水呢？」
要把海水變成淡水，就得去除海水中的鹽分，也就是把海水淡化。問題是，海水淡化需要大量能源。鹽很容易溶解在水中，形成很強的化學鍵，而這些化學鍵很難打斷。淡化海水所需的能源和技術都很昂貴，這表示淡化海水的成本可能很高。
海水淡化也有環境上的代價。海洋生物可能隨著海水吸進淡化廠，小魚、浮游生物這類小型海洋生物因此死亡，擾亂了食物鏈。另外，分離出來的鹽要怎麼處理也是個問題，這些鹽會以極濃的鹽水留下來。把這種超鹹的水抽回海中，可能會傷害當地的水中生物。要降低這些影響是做得到的，但是會增加成本。
儘管有經濟和環境上的障礙，隨著人類漸漸用盡其他來源的淡水，海水淡化也越來越有吸引力。目前在中東和北非的鄉村地區，淡化海水是供水給日漸增加的人口唯一可行的辦法。因此，各方競相尋找更便宜、更乾淨、更節能的海水淡化方式，也陸續有令人振奮的新發現。

title: 搖籃曲的功能（The Functions of Lullabies）
paras: Four millennia ago, an ancient Babylonian wrote down what is possibly the first lullaby. It is a rather threatening lullaby, in which the baby is scolded for disturbing the house god with its crying and warned of terrifying consequences. It may have got the baby to sleep, but its message is far from comforting: If he/she does not stop crying, the demon will eat him/her. This lullaby may sound more scary than sleep-inducing, yet it is true that many lullabies—including those sung today—have dark undertones.

Research has shown that lullabies, when used correctly, can soothe and possibly even help to heal an infant; but it is the caretaker’s voice and the rhythm and melody of the music that babies respond to, not the content of the song. Then, what is the function of the content? According to studies, some lullabies provide advice, like the Babylonian lullaby, and quite a few others offer the space to sing the unsung, say the unsayable. Lyrics to those lullabies can indeed be interpreted as a reflection of the caregiver’s emotions.

Researchers believe that a large part of the function of lullabies is to help a mother vocalize her worries and concerns. The mother’s fear of loss especially makes sense since the infant/toddler years of life are fragile ones. Since there is a special physical bond between mother and child during this period, mothers feel they can sing to their child about their own fears and anxieties. Lullabies, therefore, serve as therapy for the mother. In addition, the songs are seemingly trying to work some magic—as if, by singing, the mother is saying, “Sadness has already touched this house; no need to come by again.”

outline: 四千年前巴比倫人寫下可能是最早的搖籃曲，內容帶有威脅，(yet) 許多搖籃曲至今仍有陰暗的弦外之音。
研究顯示搖籃曲能安撫嬰兒，(but) 嬰兒回應的是聲音和旋律，不是歌詞。
(Then) 那歌詞有什麼作用？有些提供建議，有些說出難以啟齒的話，反映照顧者的情緒。
研究者認為搖籃曲幫母親說出擔憂，嬰幼兒期很脆弱，母子關係又緊密，(therefore) 搖籃曲是母親的心理治療。
(In addition) 歌曲也像在施法，祈求悲傷別再上門。

zh: 四千年前，一位古巴比倫人寫下了可能是史上第一首的搖籃曲。這首搖籃曲帶著相當濃的威脅意味，歌詞責罵寶寶哭聲吵到了家神，還警告寶寶會有可怕的後果。這首歌也許真的哄得寶寶睡著，但傳達的訊息一點也不令人安心：寶寶如果不停止哭鬧，惡魔就會把他吃掉。這首搖籃曲聽起來與其說催人入眠，不如說嚇人；不過，許多搖籃曲，包括現在還在唱的，確實都帶著陰暗的弦外之音。
研究顯示，搖籃曲用得正確，可以安撫嬰兒，甚至可能有助於嬰兒康復；但嬰兒回應的是照顧者的聲音，以及音樂的節奏和旋律，不是歌曲的內容。那麼，歌詞有什麼作用呢？研究指出，有些搖籃曲像那首巴比倫搖籃曲一樣提供建議，還有不少搖籃曲提供一個空間，讓人唱出沒唱出口的心聲、說出說不出口的話。這些搖籃曲的歌詞，確實可以解讀成照顧者情緒的反映。
研究人員認為，搖籃曲很大一部分的作用，是幫助母親把擔憂和掛念說出來。嬰幼兒時期很脆弱，母親害怕失去孩子的心情特別可以理解。這段時期母子之間有一種特殊的身體連結，母親覺得可以對孩子唱出自己的恐懼和焦慮。因此，搖籃曲成了母親的心理治療。此外，這些歌似乎也想施一點法術，彷彿母親藉著歌唱在說：「悲傷已經來過這個家了，不必再來了。」

title: 狗狗認知測驗 Dognition（Dognition: Testing Dogs' Cognitive Traits）
paras: Is your dog an Einstein or a Charmer? For US $60, a recently-founded company called Dognition will help you learn more about your dog’s cognitive traits. It offers an online test telling you about the brain behind the bark.

Dognition’s test measures a dog’s intellect in several aspects—from empathy to memory to reasoning skills. But don’t expect it to measure your pet’s IQ. Dr. Hare, one of the venture’s co-founders, says a dog’s intelligence can’t be described with a single number. Just as humans have a wide range of intelligences, so do dogs. The question is what type your dog relies on more.

After you plunk your money down, Dognition’s website will take you through a questionnaire about your dog: For example, how excited does your dog get around other dogs, or children? Do fireworks scare your pup? Then, Dognition guides you through tests that are as fun as playing fetch or hide-and-seek. At the end, you get a report of your dog’s cognitive profile.

Your dog could fall into one of nine categories: Ace, Stargazer, Maverick, Charmer, Socialite, Protodog, Einstein, Expert, or Renaissance Dog. That can give you something to brag about on Dognition’s Facebook page. It also can shed new light on why dogs do the things they do. For example, a Charmer is a dog that trusts you so much that it would prefer to solve problems using information you give it rather than information it can get with its own eyes.
Dognition helps people understand their dogs in ways that they have never been able to do. This new understanding can enrich the relationship between dogs and their owners.

title: 巴西戰舞卡波耶拉（Capoeira）
paras: Capoeira is a martial art that combines elements of fight, acrobatics, drumming, singing, dance, and rituals. It involves a variety of techniques that make use of the hands, feet, legs, arms, and head. Although Capoeira appears dancelike, many of its basic techniques are similar to those in other martial arts.

Capoeira was created nearly 500 years ago in Brazil by African slaves. It is believed that the martial art was connected with tribal fighting in Africa, in which people fought body to body, without weapons, in order to acquire a bride or desired woman. In the sixteenth century, when the Africans were taken from their homes to Brazil against their will and kept in slavery, Capoeira began to take form among the community of slaves for self-defense. But it soon became a strong weapon in the life-or-death struggle against their oppressors. When the slave owners realized the power of Capoeira, they began to punish those who practiced it. Capoeiristas learned to camouflage the forbidden fights with singing, clapping, and dancing as though it were simply entertainment.

At first, Capoeira was considered illegal in Brazil. However, a man known as Mestre Bimba devoted a great deal of time and effort to convincing the Brazilian authorities that Capoeira has great cultural value and should become an official fighting style. He succeeded in his endeavor and transformed the martial art into Brazil’s national sport. He and Mestre Pastinha were the first to open schools, and the Capoeira tree grew, spreading its branches across the world. Nowadays, it is performed in movies and music clips. Capoeira is also believed to have influenced several dancing styles like breaking and hip-hop.

outline: 介紹卡波耶拉結合格鬥、雜技、鼓樂、歌唱與舞蹈，(Although) 看起來像舞蹈，基本技巧卻和其他武術相似。
近五百年前由巴西的非洲奴隸創立，可能源自非洲部落爭奪新娘的徒手格鬥。
(In the sixteenth century) 奴隸為了自衛而練，(But) 很快成為反抗壓迫者的武器，(When) 奴隸主開始懲罰練習的人，他們就用歌舞掩飾。
(At first) 卡波耶拉在巴西不合法，(However) Mestre Bimba 說服政府承認，使它成為巴西國技。
開設學校後傳遍世界，(Nowadays) 現在常出現在電影與音樂影片中，(also) 還影響了霹靂舞、嘻哈舞。

zh: 卡波耶拉是一種武術，結合了格鬥、雜技、擊鼓、歌唱、舞蹈和儀式等元素，用到的技巧五花八門，會運用手、腳、腿、手臂和頭部。卡波耶拉雖然看起來像舞蹈，許多基本技巧卻和其他武術相似。

卡波耶拉是將近五百年前，巴西的非洲奴隸創造出來的。一般認為這種武術和非洲的部落格鬥有關，人們赤手空拳、徒手搏鬥，為的是娶到新娘或心儀的女子。十六世紀，非洲人身不由己地離開家鄉，到巴西淪為奴隸，卡波耶拉就在奴隸群體中開始成形，用來自衛。但是它很快就成了奴隸對抗壓迫者、攸關生死的強大武器。奴隸主發現卡波耶拉的威力後，開始懲罰練習的人。練卡波耶拉的人於是學會用歌唱、拍手和舞蹈掩飾這些禁止的打鬥，讓它看起來只是娛樂。
一開始，卡波耶拉在巴西是違法的。不過，一位叫 Mestre Bimba 的人花了大量時間和心力，說服巴西政府卡波耶拉有很高的文化價值，應該成為正式的格鬥技。他成功了，把這門武術變成巴西的國技。他和 Mestre Pastinha 最早開設學校，卡波耶拉這棵樹從此開枝散葉，傳遍全世界。現在，電影和音樂影片裡都看得到卡波耶拉。一般也認為卡波耶拉影響了霹靂舞、嘻哈舞等好幾種舞蹈風格。

title: 畫家溫斯洛·霍默（Winslow Homer）
paras: Winslow Homer (1836-1910) is regarded by many as the greatest American painter of the nineteenth century. Born and raised in Boston, he began his career at age eighteen in his hometown, working as an apprentice at a printing company. Skilled at drawing, he soon made a name for himself making illustrations for novels, sheet music, magazines, and children’s books.

He then moved to New York City, where he worked as a freelance illustrator with Harper’s Weekly, a popular magazine of the time, and began painting. Homer was assigned to cover the inauguration of President Lincoln and, later, the Civil War. His pictures of the Union troops won international recognition. Homer moved to England and, after a two-year stay, returned to America. He settled permanently in Maine in 1883.

From the late 1850s until his death in 1910, Winslow Homer produced a body of work distinguished by its thoughtful expression and its independence from artistic conventions. A man of multiple talents, Homer excelled equally in the arts of illustration, oil painting, and watercolor. Many of his works—depictions of children at play and in school, farm girls attending to their work, hunters and their prey—have become classic images of nineteenth-century American life. Others speak to more universal themes such as the primal relationship of humans to nature.

This two-week exhibition highlights a wide and representative range of Homer’s art. It shows his extraordinary career from the battlefields, farmland, and coastal villages of America, to the North Sea fishing village of Cullercoats, the rocky coast of Maine, the Adirondacks, and the Caribbean. The exhibition offers viewers an opportunity to experience and appreciate the breadth of his remarkable artistic achievement.

outline: 介紹霍默是許多人眼中 19 世紀最偉大的美國畫家，在故鄉波士頓當印刷學徒，以插畫成名。
(then) 搬到紐約當自由插畫家並開始作畫，報導林肯就職，(later) 再報導南北戰爭，以北軍畫作贏得國際肯定。
旅居英國兩年後回國，1883 年定居緬因州。
(From the late 1850s until his death in 1910) 作品深刻、不受傳統束縛，插畫、油畫、水彩都出色，描繪 19 世紀美國生活與人和自然的關係。
介紹為期兩週的展覽，呈現他在各地創作的完整面貌。

zh: 許多人認為溫斯洛·霍默（1836–1910）是 19 世紀最偉大的美國畫家。他在波士頓出生長大，十八歲在家鄉展開職業生涯，在一家印刷公司當學徒。他擅長繪畫，很快就以替小說、樂譜、雜誌和兒童書繪製插畫而出名。
後來他搬到紐約市，替當時很受歡迎的雜誌 Harper’s Weekly 擔任自由插畫家，也開始作畫。霍默受派報導林肯總統的就職典禮，後來又報導南北戰爭。他描繪北軍的畫作贏得國際肯定。霍默後來搬到英國，住了兩年後回到美國，1883 年在緬因州定居。
從 1850 年代後期到 1910 年去世，霍默創作了大量作品，特色是表達深刻，而且不受藝術傳統束縛。霍默多才多藝，插畫、油畫和水彩都同樣出色。他的許多作品，像是描繪孩子遊戲和上學、農家女孩忙著做事、獵人和獵物的畫，都已經成為 19 世紀美國生活的經典畫面。其他作品則觸及更普遍的主題，例如人和大自然之間最原始的關係。
這次為期兩週的展覽，展出霍默藝術作品中範圍廣泛又具代表性的一批。展覽呈現他非凡的創作生涯，從美國的戰場、農田和海邊村落，到北海的漁村卡勒科茨、緬因州的岩岸、阿第倫達克山脈和加勒比海。觀眾可以藉這次展覽，體會並欣賞他卓越藝術成就的廣度。

title: 茶在英國的流行（How Tea Became Popular in Britain）
paras: Tea, the most typical English drink, became established in Britain because of the influence of a foreign princess, Catherine of Braganza, the queen of Charles II. A lover of tea since her childhood in Portugal, she brought tea-drinking to the English royal court and set a trend for the beverage in the seventeenth century. The fashion soon spread beyond the circle of the nobility to the middle classes, and tea became a popular drink at the London coffee houses where people met to do business and discuss events of the day. Many employers served a cup of tea to their workers in the middle of the morning, thus inventing a lasting British institution, the “tea break.” However, drinking tea in social settings outside the workplace was beyond the means of the majority of British people. It came with a high price tag and tea was taxed as well.

Around 1800, the seventh Duchess of Bedford, Anne Maria, began the popular practice of “afternoon tea,” a ceremony taking place at about four o’clock. Until then, people did not usually eat or drink anything between lunch and dinner. At approximately the same time, the Earl of Sandwich popularized a new way of eating bread—in thin slices, with something (e.g., jam or cucumbers) between them. Before long, a small meal at the end of the afternoon, involving tea and sandwiches, had become part of the British way of life.

As tea became much cheaper during the nineteenth century, its popularity spread right through all corners of the British society. Thus, tea became Britain’s favorite drink. In working-class households, it was served with the main meal of the day, eaten when workers returned home after a day’s labor. This meal has become known as “high tea.”
Today, tea can be drunk at any time of the day, and accounts for over two-fifths of all beverages consumed in Britain—with the exception of water.

outline: 茶在英國流行要歸功於查理二世的葡萄牙籍王后凱薩琳，17 世紀她把飲茶帶進宮廷。
(soon) 風氣擴及中產階級與倫敦咖啡館，雇主供茶給員工，(thus) 形成「喝茶休息時間」（tea break）的傳統，(However) 但茶價昂貴又課稅，一般人喝不起。
(Around 1800) 貝德福公爵夫人開創「下午茶」，(At approximately the same time) 三明治伯爵推廣三明治，(Before long) 茶配三明治成為英國生活的一部分。
(As) 19 世紀茶價下降，茶普及各階層，(Thus) 成為英國人最愛的飲料，勞工家庭晚餐配茶稱為 high tea。
(Today) 現在茶隨時都能喝，占英國飲料消費量的五分之二以上（水除外）。

zh: 茶是最典型的英國飲料，而茶能在英國流行起來，要歸功於一位外國公主，也就是查理二世的王后，布拉干薩的凱薩琳。凱薩琳在葡萄牙度過童年時就愛喝茶，她把飲茶的習慣帶進英國宮廷，在十七世紀帶動了喝茶的風氣。這股風氣很快就從貴族圈擴散到中產階級，茶也成了倫敦咖啡館裡受歡迎的飲料，人們在那裡碰面談生意、討論時事。許多雇主在上午工作到一半時，會請員工喝一杯茶，因而開創了一項延續至今的英國傳統：「喝茶休息時間」（tea break）。不過，大部分英國人負擔不起在工作場所以外的社交場合喝茶。茶的價格很高，還要課稅。
1800 年左右，第七代貝德福公爵夫人 Anne Maria 開始了大受歡迎的「下午茶」習慣，這是一種大約在下午四點舉行的儀式。在那之前，人們在午餐和晚餐之間通常不吃也不喝任何東西。差不多在同一個時候，三明治伯爵推廣了一種吃麵包的新方式：把麵包切成薄片，中間夾東西（例如果醬或小黃瓜）。不久之後，在下午快結束時吃一頓有茶有三明治的小餐點，就成了英國人生活的一部分。
十九世紀茶變得便宜許多，喝茶的風氣也傳遍英國社會的每個角落。因此，茶成了英國人最喜愛的飲料。在勞工家庭裡，茶搭配的是一天中最主要的那一餐，也就是工人做完一天的工作、回家後吃的那一餐。這一餐後來就叫做「high tea」。
現在，任何時間都可以喝茶；除了水以外，茶占英國人所喝飲料的五分之二以上。

As tea became much cheaper during the nineteenth century, its popularity spread right through all corners of the British society.
Today, tea can be drunk at any time of the day, and accounts for over two-fifths of all beverages consumed in Britain—with the exception of water.

title: 日本的血型性格論（Blood Type Personality Theory in Japan）
paras: In Japan, a person’s blood type is popularly believed to decide his/her temperament and personality. Type-A people are generally considered sensitive perfectionists and good team players, but over-anxious. Type Os are curious and generous but stubborn. Type ABs are artistic but mysterious and unpredictable, and type Bs are cheerful but eccentric, individualistic, and selfish. Though lacking scientific evidence, this belief is widely seen in books, magazines, and television shows.

The blood-type belief has been used in unusual ways. The women’s softball team that won gold for Japan at the Beijing Olympics is reported to have used blood-type theories to customize training for each player. Some kindergartens have adopted teaching methods along blood group lines, and even major companies reportedly make decisions about assignments based on an employee’s blood type. In 1990, Mitsubishi Electronics was reported to have announced the formation of a team composed entirely of AB workers, thanks to “their ability to make plans.”

The belief even affects politics. One former prime minister considered it important enough to reveal in his official profile that he was a type A, while his opposition rival was type B. In 2011, a minister, Ryu Matsumoto, was forced to resign after only a week in office, when a bad-tempered encounter with local officials was televised. In his resignation speech, he blamed his failings on the fact that he was blood type B.

The blood-type craze, considered simply harmless fun by some Japanese, may manifest itself as prejudice and discrimination. In fact, this seems so common that the Japanese now have a term for it: bura-hara, meaning blood-type harassment. There are reports of discrimination leading to children being bullied, ending of happy relationships, and loss of job opportunities due to blood type.
accuracyRateSource: 大考中心 105 學年度學科能力測驗統計圖表：英文科答對率及鑑別指數表

outline: 日本人普遍相信血型決定性格，並介紹各血型的刻板印象，(Though) 雖然缺乏科學根據，卻常見於書報電視。
血型說用在運動訓練、幼稚園教學與企業人事，以三菱電機的 AB 型團隊為例。
(even) 血型說甚至影響政治，以前首相公開血型、松本龍辭職時歸咎於血型為例。
有些人覺得血型說無傷大雅，但它可能演變成偏見與歧視，(In fact) 日本人還為此造了「血型騷擾」一詞。
舉出血型歧視造成的後果：有兒童成了霸凌的對象，也有人感情破裂、失去工作機會。

zh: 在日本，一般人普遍相信血型決定一個人的脾氣和性格。A 型的人通常給人敏感、追求完美、善於團隊合作的印象，但過度焦慮；O 型的人好奇又大方，但固執；AB 型的人有藝術氣息，但神祕又難以捉摸；B 型的人開朗，但古怪、個人主義又自私。這種說法雖然缺乏科學根據，卻常常出現在書籍、雜誌和電視節目裡。
血型說還有一些不尋常的用法。據報導，在北京奧運替日本拿下金牌的女子壘球隊，就用血型理論替每位球員量身打造訓練。有些幼稚園依照血型採用不同的教學方法，據說連大公司也會根據員工的血型決定職務分派。1990 年，據報導三菱電機宣布成立一支全由 AB 型員工組成的團隊，理由是他們「有規劃的能力」。
血型說甚至影響政治。一位前首相認為血型重要到要在官方簡介裡公開，說自己是 A 型，而他的反對黨對手是 B 型。2011 年，一位部長松本龍和地方官員見面時脾氣暴躁，畫面在電視上播出，他上任才一週就不得不辭職。他在辭職演說中，把自己的過失歸咎於自己是 B 型。
有些日本人認為血型熱只是無傷大雅的娛樂，但它可能演變成偏見和歧視。事實上，這種情形似乎普遍到日本人已經為它造了一個詞：bura-hara，意思是「血型騷擾」。有報導指出，血型歧視讓有些兒童成了霸凌的對象，有些美好的感情因而破裂，也有人失去工作機會。

title: 小發明家的故事（The Story of a Young Inventor）
paras: Like many other five-year-olds, Jeanie Low of Houston, Texas, would use a stool to help her reach the bathroom sink. However, the plastic step-stool she had at home was unstable and cluttered up the small bathroom shared by her whole family. After learning of an invention contest held by her school that year, Jeanie resolved to enter the contest by creating a stool that would be a permanent fixture in the bathroom, and yet could be kept out of the way when not in use.

Jeanie decided to make a stool attached to the bathroom cabinet door under the sink. She cut a plank of wood into two pieces, each about two feet wide and one foot long. Using metal hinges, Jeanie attached one piece of the wood to the front of the cabinet door, and the second piece to the first. The first piece was set just high enough so that when it swung out horizontally from the cabinet door, the second piece would swing down from the first, just touching the ground, and so serving as a support for the first piece of the wood. This created a convenient, sturdy platform for any person too short to reach the sink. When not in use, the hinges allowed the two pieces of wood to fold back up tightly against the cabinet, where they were held in place by magnets. Jeanie called her invention the “Kiddie Stool.”

Jeanie’s Kiddie Stool won first place in her school’s contest. Two years later, it was awarded first prize again at Houston’s first annual Invention Fair. As a result, Jeanie was invited to make a number of public appearances with her Kiddie Stool, and was featured on local TV as well as in newspapers. Many people found the story of the Kiddie Stool inspiring because it showed that with imagination, anyone can be an inventor.

(As a result) 她多次公開亮相，登上電視報紙，故事激勵許多人：只要有想像力，人人都能發明。

zh: 德州休士頓的 Jeanie Low 和許多五歲小孩一樣，要踩凳子才搆得到浴室的洗手台。不過，她家裡那張塑膠踏凳不穩，又讓全家人共用的小浴室顯得很擠。得知學校那一年要舉辦發明比賽之後，Jeanie 決定參加，做一張固定在浴室裡、不用時又能收起來不擋路的凳子。

Jeanie 決定做一張裝在洗手台下方櫃門上的凳子。她把一塊木板鋸成兩片，每片大約兩英尺寬、一英尺長。她用金屬鉸鏈把第一片木板裝在櫃門正面，再把第二片裝在第一片上。第一片的位置裝得剛好夠高，從櫃門往外水平展開時，第二片會從第一片往下擺，剛好碰到地面，成為第一片木板的支撐。這樣就成了一個方便又穩固的平台，任何個子太矮、搆不到洗手台的人都能用。不用的時候，鉸鏈讓兩片木板能緊緊摺回櫃門上，再用磁鐵固定。Jeanie 把她的發明取名為「Kiddie Stool」（兒童凳）。
Jeanie 的兒童凳在學校的比賽中得到第一名。兩年後，兒童凳在休士頓第一屆年度發明展又得到首獎。因此，Jeanie 受邀帶著兒童凳多次公開亮相，也登上地方電視和報紙。許多人覺得兒童凳的故事很激勵人心，因為它說明了只要有想像力，人人都可以當發明家。

title: 中東地區的失學兒童（Children Out of School in the Middle East）
paras: Ongoing conflicts across the Middle East have prevented more than 13 million children from attending school, according to a report published by UNICEF, the United Nations Children’s Fund.

The report states that 40% of all children across the region are currently not receiving an education, which is a result of two consequences of violence: structural damage to schools and the displacement of populations, also called “forced migration.” Both issues result from the tide of violence that has crossed the region in recent years. The report examines nine countries where a state of war has become the norm. Across these countries, violence has made 8,500 schools unusable. In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.

The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011. With the crisis now in its fifth year, basic public services, including education, inside Syria have been stretched to breaking point. Within the country, the quality and availability of education depends on whether a particular region is suffering violence.

The report concludes with an earnest request to international policymakers to distribute financial and other resources to ease the regional crisis. With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance. The forces that are crushing individual lives and futures are also destroying the prospects for an entire region.

失學原因有二：學校建築毀損，以及人口流離失所，(also called) 也就是「強迫遷徙」。

報告指出，這個地區所有的兒童中，目前有 40% 沒有接受教育，原因是暴力帶來的兩個後果：學校建築毀損，以及人口流離失所，也就是所謂的「強迫遷徙」。這兩個問題都來自近年席捲這個地區的暴力浪潮。報告調查了九個長期處於戰爭狀態的國家，在這些國家裡，暴力已經使 8,500 所學校無法使用。在某些情況下，社區把學校建築當作流離失所者的收容所，在伊拉克各地原本的學校裡，一間教室最多住了九戶人家。
報告特別關注敘利亞。敘利亞自 2011 年爆發血腥內戰以來，至少已有 900 萬人流離失所。危機如今已進入第五年，敘利亞境內包括教育在內的基本公共服務，都已經不堪負荷、瀕臨崩潰。在敘利亞國內，教育的品質和普及程度，要看某個地區是否正發生暴力衝突。
報告最後懇切呼籲國際決策者，提供資金和其他資源來緩解這個地區的危機。已經有超過 1,300 萬名兒童因為衝突離開教室，說一整個世代兒童的教育前景岌岌可危，一點也不誇張。摧毀個人生命和未來的這股力量，也正在摧毀整個地區的前景。

title: 海蛇的飲水策略（How Sea Snakes Drink）
paras: Many marine animals, including penguins and marine iguanas, have evolved ways to get rid of excess salt by using special salt-expelling glands around their tongue. However, the sea snake’s salt glands cannot handle the massive amounts of salt that would enter their bodies if they actually drank seawater. This poses a serious problem when it comes to getting enough water to drink. If seawater is not an option, how does this animal survive in the ocean?

An international team of researchers focused on a population of yellow-bellied sea snakes living near Costa Rica, where rain often does not fall for up to seven months out of the year. Because yellow-bellied sea snakes usually spend all of their time far from land, rain is the animals’ only source of fresh water. When it rains, a thin layer of fresh water forms on top of the ocean, providing the snakes with a fleeting opportunity to lap up that precious resource. But during the dry season when there is no rain, snakes presumably have nothing to drink. Thus, the team became interested in testing whether sea snakes became dehydrated at sea.

The researchers collected more than 500 yellow-bellied sea snakes and weighed them. They found that during the dry season about half of the snakes accepted fresh water offered to them, while nearly none did during the wet season. A snake’s likelihood to drink also correlated with its body condition, with more withered snakes being more likely to drink, and to drink more. Finally, as predicted, snakes captured during the dry season contained significantly less body water than those scooped up in the rainy season. Thus, it seems the snake is able to endure certain degrees of dehydration in between rains. Scientists believe that dehydration at sea may explain the declining populations of sea snakes in some parts of the world.

outline: 許多海洋動物能排出多餘鹽分，(However) 海蛇的鹽腺應付不了海水，(If) 那牠們不喝海水要怎麼生存？
研究團隊鎖定哥斯大黎加附近的黃腹海蛇，(Because) 雨水是牠們唯一的淡水來源，(When it rains) 下雨時才能喝到海面上的淡水。
(But) 乾季沒有水喝，(Thus) 團隊想知道海蛇是否在海上脫水。
研究發現乾季約一半的海蛇會喝淡水，(while) 雨季幾乎不喝，越乾瘦的蛇喝得越多。
(Finally) 乾季捕獲的海蛇體內水分明顯較少，(Thus) 可見海蛇能忍受一定程度的脫水，脫水也可能是部分地區海蛇減少的原因。

zh: 許多海洋動物，包括企鵝和海鬣蜥，都演化出排除多餘鹽分的方法，靠的是舌頭周圍專門排鹽的腺體。不過，海蛇如果真的喝下海水，大量的鹽分會進入體內，牠們的鹽腺應付不了。要喝到足夠的水，這就成了一個嚴重的問題。既然不能喝海水，這種動物要怎麼在海洋裡生存呢？
一個國際研究團隊鎖定一群住在哥斯大黎加附近的黃腹海蛇，當地一年中可能長達七個月不下雨。黃腹海蛇通常一直待在遠離陸地的海上，所以雨水是牠們唯一的淡水來源。下雨時，海面上會形成一層薄薄的淡水，海蛇才有短暫的機會舔飲這珍貴的資源。但是在不下雨的乾季，海蛇大概就沒有水可以喝了。因此，研究團隊想知道海蛇在海上是否會脫水。
研究人員捕捉了 500 多條黃腹海蛇，並替牠們秤重。他們發現，乾季時大約一半的海蛇會喝研究人員提供的淡水，雨季時則幾乎沒有一條海蛇會喝。海蛇喝不喝水，也和牠的身體狀況有關：越乾瘦的海蛇越可能喝水，也喝得越多。最後，一如預期，乾季捕獲的海蛇體內水分明顯比雨季捕獲的少。由此看來，海蛇似乎能在兩場雨之間忍受某種程度的脫水。科學家認為，海上脫水可能可以解釋某些地區海蛇數量為什麼減少。

ms.t: Thus, it seems the snake is able to endure certain degrees of dehydration in between rains.

title: 泰武國小古謠傳唱隊（Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers）
paras: In 2009, the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers were invited to perform in Belgium, France, Germany, and Luxemburg. In 2011, they were voted as one of the world’s top five performance groups by audiences of Japan Broadcasting Corporation’s Amazing Voice program.

Recalling the group’s first tour in Europe, Camake Valaule, a physical education teacher and the founder of the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers, admitted that he felt very nervous. He was worried that the audience would fall asleep since most of the 75-minute performance was a cappella, that is, singing without instrumental sound. Surprisingly, the audience listened with full focus and high spirits. Camake said, “They told me afterward that through our performance, they had a vision of our country, our village, without having to visit it. This experience greatly boosted our confidence.”

According to Camake Valaule, singing traditional ballads has helped students and their parents to re-understand their culture. “It used to be that the only ones who could sing these songs were tribal elders aged between 50 and 60. Now with the children performing the pieces, parents are beginning to ask, ‘Why do we not know how to sing these ballads?’ Many times nowadays, it is the children who teach the songs to their parents, putting back the pieces of a blurred memory.”

Winning international fame, however, was neither the original intention nor the main reason why Camake founded the group in 2006. The most important thing was to make children understand why they sing these songs and to preserve and pass on their culture. Referring to the relocation of Taiwu Elementary School and Taiwu Village following Typhoon Morakot in August 2009, Camake said, “We could not take the forest or our houses in the mountains with us; but we were able to bring our culture along. As long as the children are willing to sing, I will always be there for them, singing with them and leading them to experience the meaning of the ballads.”

outline: 泰武國小古謠傳唱隊 2009 年赴歐演出，2011 年獲日本 NHK 節目觀眾票選為全球五大表演團體。

唱古謠讓學生和家長重新認識自己的文化，(Now) 孩子唱了以後家長開始問，常常是孩子教父母唱。
(however) 國際名聲不是成團的初衷，最重要的是讓孩子明白為什麼而唱，傳承文化。

zh: 2009 年，泰武國小古謠傳唱隊受邀到比利時、法國、德國和盧森堡演出。2011 年，傳唱隊獲日本放送協會（NHK）《Amazing Voice》節目的觀眾票選為全球五大表演團體之一。
體育老師 Camake Valaule 是泰武國小古謠傳唱隊的創辦人，回想起傳唱隊第一次到歐洲巡迴演出，他坦承當時非常緊張。75 分鐘的演出大部分是 a cappella，也就是沒有樂器伴奏的清唱，所以他擔心觀眾會睡著。出乎意料的是，觀眾聽得全神貫注、興致高昂。Camake 說：「他們事後告訴我，透過我們的演出，他們不必親自造訪，就看見了我們的國家、我們的村子。這次經驗讓我們的信心大增。」
Camake Valaule 說，唱傳統古謠讓學生和家長重新認識自己的文化。「以前會唱這些歌的，只有五、六十歲的部落長老。現在孩子們唱這些歌，家長開始問：『為什麼我們不會唱這些古謠？』如今常常是孩子教父母唱，把模糊的記憶一片一片拼回來。」
不過，Camake 在 2006 年成立傳唱隊，原本的用意並不是贏得國際名聲，這也不是主要的理由。最重要的是讓孩子明白自己為什麼唱這些歌，並且保存、傳承自己的文化。談到 2009 年 8 月莫拉克颱風過後泰武國小和泰武村遷校遷村，Camake 說：「我們帶不走山上的森林和房子，但是我們可以把文化帶著走。只要孩子們願意唱，我就會一直陪著他們，和他們一起唱，帶他們體會古謠的意義。」

title: 過度醫療的問題（The Problem of Overtreatment）
paras: When it comes to medical care, many patients and doctors believe “more is better.” But what they do not realize is that overtreatment—too many scans, too many blood tests, too many procedures—may pose harm. Sometimes a test leads you down a path to more and more testing, some of which may be invasive, or to treatment for things that should be left alone.

Terrence Power, for example, complained that after his wife learned she had Wegener’s disease, an uncommon disorder of the immune system, they found it difficult to refuse testing recommended by her physician. The doctor insisted on office visits every three weeks, even when she was feeling well. He frequently ordered blood tests and X-rays, and repeatedly referred her to specialists for even minor complaints. Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered, and she was hospitalized as a precaution when she developed a cold. She had as many as 25 doctor visits during one six-month period. The couple was spending about $30,000 a year for her care.

After several years of physical suffering and near financial ruin from the medical costs, the couple began questioning the treatment after consulting with other patients in online support groups. “It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said. “You think she’s getting the best care in the world, but after a while you start to wonder: What is the objective?” Mr. Power then spoke with his own primary care doctor, who advised him to find a new specialist to oversee Mrs. Power’s care. Under the new doctor’s care, the regular testing stopped and Mrs. Power’s condition stabilized. Now she sees the doctor only four or five times a year.

outline: 許多病人和醫生認為醫療越多越好，(But) 過度醫療其實可能有害，一項檢查常引來更多檢查。
(for example) 以 Power 太太為例：醫生堅持每三週回診，頻繁抽血、照 X 光，連小毛病也轉診專科。
(Even when) 檢查正常仍加做檢查，感冒就住院，半年看診 25 次，一年花費約三萬美元。
(After) 多年身心與經濟的煎熬後，夫妻和網路病友交流，開始質疑治療。
(then) 先生的家庭醫師建議換專科醫師，停止例行檢查後病情穩定，(Now) 現在一年只看診四、五次。

zh: 談到醫療照護，許多病人和醫生都相信「越多越好」。但是他們沒有意識到，過度醫療，也就是太多掃描、太多抽血檢驗、太多醫療程序，可能會造成傷害。有時候一項檢查會帶著你走上越來越多檢查的路，其中有些可能是侵入性的；有時候則會去治療一些原本應該放著不管的問題。

以 Terrence Power 為例，他抱怨妻子得知自己罹患韋格納肉芽腫（一種罕見的免疫系統疾病）之後，兩人發現很難拒絕醫師建議的檢查。醫生堅持她每三週回診一次，即使她覺得身體很好也一樣。醫生經常要她抽血、照 X 光，連小毛病也一再轉診給專科醫師。就算檢查結果正常，醫生還是安排更多檢查；她感冒時，醫生也為了預防萬一讓她住院。在某個半年期間，她看診多達 25 次。這對夫妻每年要花大約三萬美元在她的醫療上。

經過好幾年身體上的折磨，醫療費用也幾乎讓他們破產，這對夫妻在網路病友互助團體裡和其他病人交流之後，開始質疑這些治療。Power 先生說：「醫生什麼時候做得太過頭了，真的很難判斷。你以為她得到的是世界上最好的照顧，但過了一陣子你會開始懷疑：這樣做的目的到底是什麼？」Power 先生後來和自己的家庭醫師談過，醫師建議他另外找一位專科醫師負責 Power 太太的治療。在新醫師的照護下，例行檢查停了，Power 太太的病情也穩定下來。現在她一年只看醫生四、五次。

ms.t: But what they do not realize is that overtreatment—too many scans, too many blood tests, too many procedures—may pose harm.

title: 攝影家布列松（Photographer Henri Cartier-Bresson）
paras: Henri Cartier-Bresson (1908–2004) is one of the most original and influential figures in the history of photography. His humane, spontaneous photographs helped establish photojournalism as an art form.

Cartier-Bresson’s family was wealthy—his father made a fortune as a textile manufacturer—but Cartier-Bresson later joked that due to his parents’ frugal ways, it often seemed as though his family was poor.

Educated in Paris, Cartier-Bresson developed an early love for literature and the arts. As a teenager, Cartier-Bresson rebelled against his parents’ formal ways of education. In his early adulthood, he even drifted toward communism. But it was art that remained at the center of his life.

Cartier-Bresson traveled to Africa in 1931 to hunt antelope and boar. And Africa fueled another interest in him: photography. He then wandered around the world with his camera, using a handheld camera to catch images from fleeting moments of everyday life.

Not long after World War II, Cartier-Bresson traveled east, spending considerable time in India, where he met and photographed Gandhi shortly before his assassination in 1948. Cartier-Bresson’s subsequent work to document Gandhi’s death and its immediate impact on the country became one of Life Magazine’s most prized photo essays.

Cartier-Bresson’s approach to photography remained much the same throughout his life. He made clear his dislike of images that had been improved by artificial light, darkroom effects, and even cropping. The naturalist in Cartier-Bresson believed that all editing should be done when the photo is taken. In 1952, his first book, The Decisive Moment, a rich collection of his work spanning two decades, was published. “There is nothing in this world that does not have a decisive moment,” he said.
In 1968, he began to turn away from photography and returned to his passion for drawing and painting.

zh: 布列松（Henri Cartier-Bresson，1908–2004）是攝影史上最有原創性、最具影響力的人物之一。他的照片充滿人情味、自然不做作，讓新聞攝影確立為一種藝術形式。
布列松家境富裕，父親經營紡織業發了大財；不過布列松後來開玩笑說，因為父母很節儉，家裡常常看起來好像很窮。
布列松在巴黎受教育，很早就熱愛文學和藝術。青少年時期，他反抗父母那套拘謹的教育方式。成年初期，他甚至一度傾向共產主義。不過，藝術始終是他生活的重心。
1931 年，布列松到非洲獵捕羚羊和野豬。非洲也引發了他另一個興趣：攝影。之後他帶著相機周遊世界，用手持相機捕捉日常生活中稍縱即逝的瞬間。
第二次世界大戰結束後不久，布列松往東方旅行，在印度待了相當長的時間。他在印度見到甘地，並替甘地拍照，不久之後甘地就在 1948 年遇刺身亡。布列松後來記錄甘地之死，以及甘地之死對印度立即造成的衝擊，這組作品成為《生活》雜誌最珍貴的攝影專題之一。
布列松一生拍照的方式幾乎沒有改變。他明白表示，不喜歡用人工光源、暗房效果，甚至裁切修飾過的照片。布列松是個自然主義者，認為所有的編修都應該在拍攝的當下完成。1952 年，他出版第一本書《決定性的瞬間》，收錄了他二十年來的作品。他說：「這世界上沒有一件事沒有決定性的瞬間。」
1968 年，布列松開始逐漸遠離攝影，回到他熱愛的素描和繪畫。

title: 「久坐病」的危害（The Dangers of "Sitting Disease"）
paras: You’ve most likely heard the news by now: A car-commuting, desk-bound, TV-watching lifestyle can be harmful to our health. All the time that we spend rooted in the chair is linked to increased risks of so many deadly diseases that experts have named this modern-day health epidemic the “sitting disease.”

Sitting for too long slows down the body’s metabolism and the way enzymes break down our fat reserves, raising both blood sugar levels and blood pressure. Small amounts of regular activity, even just standing and moving around, throughout the day is enough to bring the increased levels back down. And those small amounts of activity add up—30 minutes of light activity in two or three-minute bursts can be just as effective as a half-hour block of exercise. But without that activity, blood sugar levels and blood pressure keep creeping up, steadily damaging the inside of the arteries and increasing the risk of diabetes, heart disease, stroke, and other serious diseases. In essence, fundamental changes in biology occur if you sit for too long.

But wait, you’re a runner. You needn’t worry about the harm of a sedentary lifestyle because you exercise regularly, right? Well, not so fast. Recent studies show that people spend an average of 64 hours a week sitting, whether or not they exercise 150 minutes a week as recommended by World Health Organization (WHO). Regular exercisers, furthermore, are found to be about 30 percent less active on days when they exercise. Overall, most people simply aren’t exercising or moving around enough to counteract all the harm that can result from sitting nine hours or more a day.
Scared straight out of your chair? Good. The remedy is as simple as standing up and taking activity breaks.

outline: 開車通勤、久坐辦公、看電視的生活有害健康，專家稱為「久坐病」。
久坐使新陳代謝變慢，血糖血壓上升，少量活動就能降下來，(And) 零星的輕度活動累積起來和半小時運動一樣有效。
(But without that activity) 不活動的話，血糖血壓持續升高，增加糖尿病、心臟病、中風的風險。
(But wait) 有運動也不能放心：無論是否運動，每週平均坐 64 小時，(furthermore) 運動當天的活動量反而較少。
(Overall) 多數人的活動量抵銷不了久坐的傷害，解決方法就是起身活動、多休息。

zh: 你現在大概已經聽說了：開車通勤、整天坐辦公桌、看電視的生活方式可能有害健康。我們坐在椅子上不動的時間，和許多致命疾病的風險升高都有關，專家甚至把這種現代的健康流行病稱為「久坐病」。

坐太久會讓身體的新陳代謝變慢，酵素分解體內脂肪的速度也變慢，使血糖和血壓都升高。一整天裡只要有少量、規律的活動，即使只是站起來走動一下，就足以讓升高的數值降回來。而且這些少量的活動會累積起來：每次活動兩三分鐘，加起來 30 分鐘的輕度活動，效果可能和一次做完半小時的運動一樣好。但是如果沒有這些活動，血糖和血壓就會持續慢慢上升，不斷損害動脈內壁，增加糖尿病、心臟病、中風和其他重大疾病的風險。基本上，坐太久的話，身體在生理上就會產生根本的變化。
不過等等，你有在跑步。你有規律運動，所以不必擔心久坐不動的生活方式帶來的傷害，對吧？嗯，先別急著下結論。最近的研究顯示，不論有沒有照世界衛生組織（WHO）的建議每週運動 150 分鐘，人們平均每週都要坐 64 個小時。此外，研究還發現，規律運動的人在有運動的那幾天，活動量反而少了大約 30%。整體來說，大多數人的運動量或活動量根本不夠，抵銷不了每天坐九小時以上可能造成的種種傷害。
嚇得從椅子上跳起來了嗎？很好。解決方法很簡單，就是站起來，找時間休息、活動一下。

title: 小說家童妮·摩里森（Novelist Toni Morrison）
paras: American writer Toni Morrison was born in 1931 in Ohio. She was raised in an African American family filled with songs and stories of Southern myths, which later shaped her prose. Her happy family life led to her excellent performance in school, despite the atmosphere of racial discrimination in the society.

After graduating from college, Morrison started to work as a teacher and got married in 1958. Several years later, her marriage began to fail. For a temporary escape, she joined a small writers’ group, in which each member was required to bring a story or poem for discussion. She wrote a story based on the life of a girl she knew in childhood who had prayed to God for blue eyes. The story was well received by the group, but then she put it away, thinking she was done with it.

In 1964, Morrison got divorced and devoted herself to writing. One day, she dusted off the story she had written for the writers’ group and decided to make it into a novel. She drew on her memories from childhood and expanded upon them using her imagination so that the characters developed a life of their own. The Bluest Eye was eventually published in 1970. From 1970 to 1992, Morrison published five more novels.

In her novels, Morrison brings in different elements of the African American past, their struggles, problems and cultural memory. In Song of Solomon, for example, Morrison tells the story of an African American man and his search for identity in his culture. The novels and other works won her several prizes. In 1993, Morrison received the Nobel Prize in Literature. She is the eighth woman and the first African American woman to win the honor.

zh: 美國作家童妮·摩里森（Toni Morrison）1931 年生於俄亥俄州。她在一個非裔美國人家庭長大，家裡充滿了美國南方神話的歌謠和故事，這些歌謠和故事後來形塑了她的文字風格。雖然當時社會上瀰漫著種族歧視的氣氛，幸福的家庭生活仍讓她在學校表現優異。
大學畢業後，摩里森開始教書，1958 年結婚。幾年後，她的婚姻開始出問題。為了暫時逃離，她加入一個小型的寫作社團，每位社員都要帶一篇故事或一首詩來討論。她以童年認識的一個女孩為藍本寫了一篇故事，那個女孩曾經向上帝祈求擁有一雙藍眼睛。這篇故事在社團裡大受好評，但她之後就把故事收了起來，以為這篇故事已經寫完了。
1964 年，摩里森離婚，從此專心寫作。有一天，她把當年替寫作社團寫的那篇故事翻出來，決定擴寫成小說。她取材自童年的記憶，再加上自己的想像，讓書中的角色有了自己的生命。《最藍的眼睛》終於在 1970 年出版。從 1970 年到 1992 年，摩里森又出版了五本小說。
摩里森在小說裡融入非裔美國人過去的種種：他們的奮鬥、面對的問題和文化記憶。例如在《所羅門之歌》裡，摩里森講述一個非裔美國男子在自己的文化中尋找自我認同的故事。她的小說和其他作品替她贏得好幾個獎項。1993 年，摩里森獲得諾貝爾文學獎，是第八位得到這項榮譽的女性，也是第一位獲獎的非裔美國女性。

title: 伊曼紐三兄弟的成功之道（The Success of the Emanuel Brothers）
paras: Below is an excerpt from an interview with Zeke Emanuel, a health-policy expert, on his famous brothers.

Interviewer: You’re the older brother of Rahm, the mayor of Chicago, and Ari, an extremely successful talent agent. And you’re a bioethicist and one of the architects of Obamacare. Isn’t writing a book about how great your family is a bit odd?

Zeke: I don’t write a book about how great my family is. There are lots of idiocies and foolishness—a lot to make fun of in the book. I wrote Brothers Emanuel because I had begun jotting stories for my kids. And then we began getting a lot of questions: What did Mom put in the cereal? Three successful brothers, all different areas.
I: To what do you attribute the Emanuel brothers’ success?

Z: I would put success in quotes. We strive. First, I think we got this striving from our mother to make the world a better place. A second important thing is you never rest on the last victory. There’s always more to do. And maybe the third important thing is my father’s admonition that offense is the best defense. We don’t give up.
I: Do you still not have a TV?
Z: I don’t own a TV. I don’t own a car. I don’t Facebook. I don’t tweet.
I: But you have four cell phones.
Z: I’m down to two, thankfully.
I: Your brothers are a national source of fascination. Where do you think they’ll be in five years?

Z: Ari will be a superagent running the same company. Rahm would still be mayor of Chicago. I will probably continue to be my academic self. The one thing I can guarantee is none of us will have taken a cruise, none of us will be sitting on a beach with a pina colada.

outline: 引言：訪問衛生政策專家 Zeke Emanuel，談他兩位知名的弟弟。
談寫書的緣由：書中也有不少糗事，原本是寫給孩子的故事，(And then) 後來很多人問兄弟三人為什麼都成功。
談成功的原因：(First) 母親讓世界更好的期許，(A second) 永不滿足於上一次勝利，(And maybe the third) 父親說攻擊是最好的防禦。
談生活：不看電視、沒有車、不用臉書和推特，手機從四支減為兩支。

zh: 以下節錄自一篇訪談，受訪者是衛生政策專家 Zeke Emanuel，談的是他那兩個有名的弟弟。
訪問者：你的弟弟 Rahm 是芝加哥市長，另一個弟弟 Ari 是非常成功的演藝經紀人，你是他們的哥哥。你本身是生命倫理學家，也是歐巴馬健保的設計者之一。寫一本書講自己的家人有多了不起，不覺得有點奇怪嗎？
Zeke：我寫的不是一本講我家人有多了不起的書。書裡有很多蠢事和傻事，有很多可以拿來取笑的地方。我寫《Brothers Emanuel》，是因為我原本開始替孩子們隨手記下一些故事。後來就有很多人來問我們：媽媽到底在麥片裡放了什麼？三兄弟都很成功，而且在不同的領域。
訪：你認為 Emanuel 兄弟成功的原因是什麼？
Z：「成功」這兩個字我會加上引號。我們是在努力。第一，我想我們這股努力的勁是從母親那裡來的，她希望讓世界變得更好。第二個重點是，永遠不要因為上一次的勝利就停下來，要做的事永遠還有。第三個重點，或許是父親的告誡：攻擊是最好的防禦。我們不放棄。
訪：你現在還是沒有電視嗎？
Z：我沒有電視，沒有車，不用臉書，也不發推特。
訪：但是你有四支手機。
Z：還好，我已經減到兩支了。
訪：全國都對你的兩個弟弟很感興趣。你認為五年後他們會在哪裡？
Z：Ari 會是一個超級經紀人，經營同一家公司。Rahm 應該還是芝加哥市長。我大概還是會繼續當學者。我唯一能保證的是，我們三個沒有人會去搭郵輪，也沒有人會坐在海灘上喝鳳梨可樂達。
