title: 大規模線上開放課程（MOOCs）
paras: MOOC, a massive open online course, aims at providing large-scale interactive participation and open access via the web. In addition to traditional course materials such as videos, readings, and problem sets, MOOCs provide interactive user forums that help build a community for the students, professors, and teaching assistants.

MOOCs first made waves in the fall of 2011, when Professor Sebastian Thrun from Stanford University opened his graduate-level artificial intelligence course up to any student anywhere, and 160,000 students in more than 190 countries signed up. This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways. Since the courses can be taken by hundreds of thousands of students at the same time, the number of universities might decrease dramatically. Professor Thrun has even envisioned a future in which there will only need to be 10 universities in the world. Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free. This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.

There is a lot of excitement and fear surrounding MOOCs. While some say free online courses are a great way to increase the enrollment of minority students, others have said they will leave many students behind. Some critics have said that MOOCs promote an unrealistic one-size-fits-all model of higher education and that there is no replacement for true dialogues between professors and their students. After all, a brain is not a computer. We are not blank hard drives waiting to be filled with data. People learn from people they love and remember the things that arouse emotion. Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.

outline: 介紹 MOOC 的定義，(In addition to) 除了傳統教材，還有互動論壇。
2011 年史丹佛大學一門人工智慧課開放全球選修，吸引十六萬人報名。
(Since) 一門課能同時容納數十萬人，大學數量可能大減，(Perhaps) 最大特色是免費。
(While) 支持者認為能增加少數族群入學機會，批評者擔心許多學生跟不上。
批評者也認為師生真正的對話無可取代，(After all) 人腦不是電腦，線上學生會失去大學的社交生活。

zh: MOOC 是大規模線上開放課程，目標是透過網路提供大規模的互動參與和開放的學習管道。除了影片、閱讀材料和習題這些傳統的課程教材，MOOC 還提供互動式的使用者論壇，幫助學生、教授和助教建立一個社群。

MOOC 最早在 2011 年秋天引起轟動：史丹佛大學的 Sebastian Thrun 教授把他研究所程度的人工智慧課程開放給世界各地的任何學生，結果有 190 多個國家、16 萬名學生報名。這種新型態的線上課程在許多方面撼動了高等教育界。由於一門課可以同時讓數十萬名學生修讀，大學的數量可能會大幅減少。Thrun 教授甚至設想，未來全世界只需要 10 所大學。MOOC 有許多是由知名大學的教授授課，而它最引人注目的地方或許是免費。這對手頭很緊的學生來說當然是好消息。
MOOC 帶來許多期待，也引起許多擔憂。有些人說，免費的線上課程是增加少數族群學生入學人數的好方法；也有人說，這種課程會讓許多學生跟不上。有些批評者認為，MOOC 推行的是一種不切實際、一體適用的高等教育模式，而教授和學生之間真正的對話是無可取代的。畢竟，人腦不是電腦，我們不是等著裝滿資料的空白硬碟。人會向自己喜愛的人學習，也會記住引起情緒的事物。有些批評者擔心，線上學生會錯過大學的社交生活。

title: 自動駕駛汽車的未來（The Future of Driverless Cars）
paras: Today the car seems to make periodic leaps in progress. A variety of driver assistance technologies are appearing on new cars. A developing technology called Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication, or V2V, is being tested by automotive manufacturers as a way to help reduce the number of accidents. V2V works by using wireless signals to send information back and forth between cars about their location, speed and direction, so that they keep safe distances from each other. Another new technology being tested is Vehicle-to-Infrastructure communication, or V2I. V2I would allow vehicles to communicate with road signs or traffic signals and provide information to the vehicle about safety issues. V2I could also request traffic information from a traffic management system and access the best possible routes. Both V2V and V2I have the potential to reduce around 80 percent of vehicle crashes on the road.

More and more new cars can reverse-park, read traffic signs, maintain a safe distance in steady traffic and brake automatically to avoid crashes. Moreover, a number of firms are creating cars that drive themselves to a chosen destination without a human at the controls. It is predicted that driverless cars will be ready for sale within five years. If and when cars go completely driverless, the benefits will be enormous. Google, which already uses prototypes of such cars to ferry its staff along Californian freeways, once put a blind man in a prototype and filmed him being driven off to buy takeaway hamburgers. If this works, huge numbers of elderly and disabled people can regain their personal mobility. The young will not have to pay crippling motor insurance, because their reckless hands and feet will no longer touch the wheel or the accelerator. People who commute by car will gain hours each day to work, rest, or read a newspaper.

越來越多新車能自動倒車入庫、辨識交通標誌、在車流穩定時保持安全車距，還能自動煞車避免撞車。此外，好幾家公司正在研發不需要人操控、自己開到指定目的地的汽車。據預測，無人駕駛汽車五年內就能上市。如果汽車真有完全無人駕駛的一天，好處會非常大。Google 已經用這種車的原型車在加州的高速公路上接送員工，還曾讓一位盲人坐進原型車，拍下他坐車去買外帶漢堡的過程。如果這行得通，大批年長者和身心障礙者就能重新自由行動。年輕人不必再付高得嚇人的汽車保險費，因為他們莽撞的手腳再也不會碰到方向盤和油門。開車通勤的人每天會多出好幾個小時，可以工作、休息或看報紙。

title: 瑞士刀的起源（The Origin of the Swiss Army Knife）
paras: The Swiss army knife is a popular device that is recognized all over the world. In Switzerland, there is a saying that every good Swiss citizen has one in his or her pocket. But the knife had humble beginnings.

In the late nineteenth century, the Swiss army issued its soldiers a gun that required a special screwdriver to dismantle and clean it. At the same time, canned food was becoming common in the army. Swiss generals decided to issue each soldier a standard knife to serve both as a screwdriver and a can opener.

It was a lifesaver for Swiss knife makers, who were struggling to compete with cheaper German imports. In 1884, Carl Elsener, head of the Swiss knife manufacturer Victorinox, seized that opportunity with both hands, and designed a soldier’s knife that the army loved. It was a simple knife with one big blade, a can opener, and a screwdriver.

A few years after the soldier’s knife was issued, the “Schweizer Offizier Messer,” or Swiss Officer’s Knife, came on the market. Interestingly, the Officer’s Knife was never given to those serving in the army. The Swiss military purchasers considered the new model with a corkscrew for opening wine not “essential for survival,” so officers had to buy this new model by themselves. But its special multi-functional design later launched the knife as a global brand. After the Second World War, a great number of American soldiers were stationed in Europe. And as they could buy the Swiss army knife at shops on military bases, they bought huge quantities of them. However, it seems that “Schweizer Offizier Messer” was too difficult for them to say, so they just called it the Swiss army knife, and that is the name it is now known by all over the world.

19 世紀末，瑞士陸軍發給士兵一種步槍，拆卸和清理都需要特殊的螺絲起子。同一時期，罐頭食品在軍中越來越普遍。瑞士的將領於是決定發給每個士兵一把制式刀具，既能當螺絲起子，也能開罐頭。
這對當時苦於和比較便宜的德國進口刀競爭的瑞士刀具業者來說，簡直是救命稻草。1884 年，瑞士刀具製造商 Victorinox 的負責人 Carl Elsener 緊緊抓住這個機會，設計出一款軍方很喜歡的士兵刀。這是一把簡單的刀，有一片大刀刃、一個開罐器和一支螺絲起子。

士兵刀發放幾年後，Schweizer Offizier Messer，也就是「瑞士軍官刀」上市了。有意思的是，軍方從來沒有發軍官刀給軍人。瑞士軍方的採購人員認為，這款多了一支開葡萄酒用的軟木塞開瓶器的新刀，並不是「生存必需品」，所以軍官得自己掏錢買。但後來正是這種特殊的多功能設計，讓這把刀成了全球品牌。第二次世界大戰後，大批美軍駐紮在歐洲，他們可以在軍事基地的商店買到這種刀，於是大量購買。不過 Schweizer Offizier Messer 對美軍來說似乎太難唸了，他們乾脆叫它 Swiss army knife，現在全世界都用這個名字稱呼它。

title: 太空垃圾的問題（The Problem of Space Junk）
paras: Space is where our future is—trips to the Moon, Mars and beyond. Most people would think that aside from comets and stars there is little else out there. But, since our space journey started we have left so much trash there that scientists are now concerned that if we don’t clean it up, we may all be in mortal danger.

The first piece of space junk was created in 1964, when the American satellite Vanguard I stopped operating and lost its connection with the ground center. However, since it kept orbiting around the Earth without any consequences, scientists became increasingly comfortable abandoning things that no longer served any useful purpose in space.

It is estimated that there are currently over 500,000 pieces of man-made trash orbiting the Earth at speeds of up to 17,500 miles per hour. The junk varies from tiny pieces of paint chipped off rockets to cameras, huge fuel tanks, and even odd items like the million-dollar tool kit that astronaut Heidemarie Stefanyshyn-Piper lost during a spacewalk.

The major problem with the space trash is that it may hit working satellites and damage traveling spacecraft. Moreover, pieces of junk may collide with each other and break into fragments which fall back to the Earth. To avoid this, scientists have devised several ways for clearing the sky. Ground stations have been built to monitor larger pieces of space trash to prevent them from crashing into working satellites or space shuttles. Future plans include a cooperative effort among many nations to stop littering in space and to clean up the trash already there.

outline: 太空是人類的未來，(But) 人類已在太空留下大量垃圾，可能危及人類。

估計目前有超過五十萬件垃圾高速繞行地球，從油漆碎片到工具箱都有。

zh: 太空是人類未來的所在，我們要去月球、火星，還要去更遠的地方。大部分人會以為，除了彗星和星星，太空裡沒什麼別的東西。但是，自從人類開始探索太空，我們已經在那裡留下太多垃圾，多到科學家現在擔心，如果不清理乾淨，我們可能全都會有生命危險。
第一件太空垃圾出現在 1964 年：美國的先鋒一號衛星停止運作，和地面中心失去聯繫。不過，先鋒一號一直繞著地球運行，沒有造成任何後果，於是科學家越來越習慣把太空中不再有用的東西丟著不管。
據估計，目前有超過五十萬件人造垃圾以最高每小時 17,500 英里的速度繞著地球運行。這些垃圾大小不一，小到火箭上剝落的油漆碎片，大到相機、巨大的燃料箱，甚至還有奇特的東西，例如太空人 Heidemarie Stefanyshyn-Piper 太空漫步時弄丟的那個價值百萬美元的工具箱。
太空垃圾的主要問題是可能撞上運作中的衛星，損壞航行中的太空船。此外，垃圾之間可能互相碰撞，碎成碎片掉回地球。為了避免這種情形，科學家想出了幾種清理天空的方法。目前已經建立地面站，監測體積較大的太空垃圾，防止這些垃圾撞上運作中的衛星或太空梭。未來的計畫包括各國合作，停止在太空亂丟垃圾，並且清理已經在那裡的垃圾。

title: 能量飲料與酒測（Energy Drinks and Breathalyzer Tests）
paras: An alcohol breath test (ABT) is often used by the police to find out whether a person is drunk while driving. In the United States, the legal blood alcohol limit is 0.08% for people aged 21 years or older, while people under 21 are not allowed to drive a car with any level of alcohol in their body. A “positive” test result, a result over the legal limit, allows the police to arrest the driver. However, many people who tested positive on the test have claimed that they only drank a “non-alcoholic” energy drink. Can one of these energy drinks really cause someone to test positive on an ABT? Researchers in Missouri set up an experiment to find out.

First, the amount of alcohol in 27 different popular energy drinks was measured. All but one had an alcohol level greater than 0.005%. In nine of the 27 drinks, the alcohol level was at least 0.096%. The scientists then investigated the possibility that these small levels of alcohol could be detected by an ABT. They asked test subjects to drink a full can or bottle of an energy drink and then gave each subject an ABT one minute and 15 minutes after the drink was finished.

For 11 of the 27 energy drinks, the ABT did detect the presence of alcohol if the test was given within one minute after the drink was taken. However, alcohol could not be detected for any of the drinks if the test was given 15 minutes after the drink was consumed. This shows that when the test is taken plays a crucial role in the test result. The sooner the test is conducted after the consumption of these drinks, the more likely a positive alcohol reading will be obtained.

outline: 說明酒測的用途與美國法定標準，(However) 許多酒測未過的人宣稱只喝了能量飲料。
密蘇里研究人員設計實驗查證。
(First) 先測量 27 種能量飲料的酒精含量，(then) 再讓受試者喝完後 1 分鐘、15 分鐘各測一次。
喝完 1 分鐘內有 11 種測出酒精，(However) 15 分鐘後全都測不出來。
(This shows that) 結論：測試時間是影響結果的關鍵。

zh: 警察常用酒精呼氣檢測（ABT）判斷一個人是不是酒後駕車。在美國，21 歲以上的人法定血液酒精濃度上限是 0.08%，未滿 21 歲的人只要體內有任何酒精，就不准開車。「陽性」的檢測結果，也就是超過法定上限，警察就可以逮捕駕駛人。然而，許多檢測呈陽性的人都聲稱自己只喝了「不含酒精」的能量飲料。喝這些能量飲料，真的會讓人酒測呈陽性嗎？密蘇里州的研究人員設計了一項實驗來找出答案。
首先，研究人員測量了 27 種熱門能量飲料的酒精含量。除了一種以外，其他飲料的酒精含量都超過 0.005%。27 種飲料中，有 9 種的酒精含量至少 0.096%。接著，科學家研究酒測能不能測出這麼少量的酒精。他們請受試者喝完一整罐或一整瓶能量飲料，然後在喝完後 1 分鐘和 15 分鐘各替每位受試者做一次酒精呼氣檢測。
在 27 種能量飲料中，如果在喝完 1 分鐘內檢測，有 11 種確實測得出酒精。然而，如果在喝完 15 分鐘後才檢測，不論哪一種飲料都測不出酒精。這表示什麼時候檢測，對檢測結果有關鍵的影響。喝完這些飲料之後越早檢測，酒測讀數就越可能呈陽性。

This shows that when the test is taken plays a crucial role in the test result.

title: 印度 Bindi 的文化意涵（The Cultural Meaning of the Bindi in India）
paras: The majority of Indian women wear a red dot between their eyebrows. While it is generally taken as an indicator of their marital status, the practice is primarily related to the Hindu religion. The dot goes by different names in different Hindi dialects, and “bindi” is the one that is most commonly known. Traditionally, the dot carries no gender restriction: Men as well as women wear it. However, the tradition of men wearing it has faded in recent times, so nowadays we see a lot more women than men wearing one.

The position of the bindi is standard: center of the forehead, close to the eyebrows. It represents a third, or inner eye. Hindu tradition holds that all people have three eyes: The two outer ones are used for seeing the outside world, and the third one is there to focus inward toward God. As such, the dot signifies piety and serves as a constant reminder to keep God in the front of a believer’s thoughts.

Red is the traditional color of the dot. It is said that in ancient times a man would place a drop of blood between his wife’s eyes to seal their marriage. According to Hindu beliefs, the color red is believed to bring good fortune to the married couple. Today, people go with different colors depending upon their preferences. Women often wear dots that match the color of their clothes. Decorative or sticker bindis come in all sizes, colors and variations, and can be worn by young and old, married and unmarried people alike. Wearing a bindi has become more of a fashion statement than a religious custom.

outline: 印度女性眉心的紅點 (While) 一般人常以為是已婚的記號，其實主要和印度教有關。

zh: 大部分印度女性都會在兩眉之間點一個紅點。一般人通常把紅點看作已婚的記號，不過這個習俗主要和印度教有關。這個紅點在不同的印地語方言裡有不同的名稱，最廣為人知的是「bindi」。傳統上，紅點沒有性別限制：男性和女性都會點。不過近來男性點紅點的傳統逐漸式微，所以現在我們看到點紅點的女性比男性多得多。
bindi 的位置有固定的標準：額頭正中央、靠近眉毛的地方。bindi 代表第三隻眼，也就是內在的眼睛。印度教的傳統認為，每個人都有三隻眼：外面的兩隻眼用來看外在的世界，第三隻眼則用來向內專注於神。因此，這個點象徵虔誠，時時提醒信徒要把神放在心中最重要的位置。
紅色是 bindi 的傳統顏色。相傳古時候男人會在妻子兩眼之間點一滴血，作為婚姻的印記。根據印度教的信仰，紅色會替夫妻帶來好運。現在大家會依照自己的喜好選擇不同的顏色。女性常常點和衣服同色的 bindi。裝飾用的 bindi 或貼紙式的 bindi 大小、顏色、樣式應有盡有，不論老少、已婚未婚都可以戴。戴 bindi 已經比較像是在展現時尚，而不是遵循宗教習俗。

title: 蘇格蘭裙（The Kilt）
paras: The kilt is a skirt traditionally worn by Scottish men. It is a tailored garment that is wrapped around the wearer’s body at the waist starting from one side, around the front and back and across the front again to the opposite side. The overlapping layers in front are called “aprons.” Usually, the kilt covers the body from the waist down to just above the knees. A properly made kilt should not be so loose that the wearer can easily twist the kilt around the body, nor should it be so tight that it causes bulging of the fabric where it is buckled. Underwear may be worn as one prefers.

One of the most distinctive features of the kilt is the pattern of squares, or sett, it exhibits. The association of particular patterns with individual families can be traced back hundreds of years. Then in the Victorian era (19th century), weaving companies began to systematically record and formalize the system of setts for commercial purposes. Today there are also setts for States and Provinces, schools and universities, and general patterns that anybody can wear.

The kilt can be worn with accessories. On the front apron, there is often a kilt pin, topped with a small decorative family symbol. A small knife can be worn with the kilt too. It typically comes in a very wide variety, from fairly plain to quite elaborate silver- and jewel-ornamented designs. The kilt can also be worn with a sporran, which is the Gaelic word for pouch or purse.

zh: 蘇格蘭裙是蘇格蘭男性傳統上穿的裙子。蘇格蘭裙是一件剪裁合身的衣服，從身體一側開始圍在腰部，繞過前面和後面，再橫過前面一次，到另一側為止。前面交疊的那幾層叫做「aprons」（前片）。蘇格蘭裙通常從腰部蓋到膝蓋上方一點。做得好的蘇格蘭裙不能鬆到穿的人能輕易把裙子在身上轉來轉去，也不能緊到扣環的地方布料鼓起來。裡面要不要穿內褲，全看個人喜好。
蘇格蘭裙最明顯的特色之一，是裙子上的方格圖案，也就是 sett。特定的圖案代表特定的家族，這種關聯可以追溯到幾百年前。後來到了維多利亞時代（十九世紀），紡織公司為了商業目的，開始有系統地記錄這些方格圖案，並且建立一套制度。現在也有代表州和省、學校和大學的方格圖案，還有任何人都能穿的一般圖案。
蘇格蘭裙可以搭配配件。前片上常常別著一根裙針，針頭有一個裝飾用的小型家族標誌。穿蘇格蘭裙也可以配戴一把小刀，小刀的樣式非常多，從相當簡單的，到用銀和寶石裝飾得很精緻的都有。蘇格蘭裙也可以搭配 sporran，這是蓋爾語，意思是小袋子或錢包。

title: 爵士歌手 Wesla Whitfield 的故事（The Story of Wesla Whitfield）
paras: Wesla Whitfield, a famous jazz singer, has a unique style and life story, so I decided to see one of her performances and interview her for my column.

I went to a nightclub in New York and watched the stage lights go up. After the band played an introduction, Wesla Whitfield wheeled herself onstage in a wheelchair. As she sang, Whitfield’s voice was so powerful and soulful that everyone in the room forgot the wheelchair was even there.

At 57, Whitfield is small and pretty, witty and humble, persistent and philosophical. Raised in California, Whitfield began performing in public at age 18, when she took a job as a singing waitress at a pizza parlor. After studying classical music in college, she moved to San Francisco and went on to sing with the San Francisco Opera Chorus.

Walking home from rehearsal at age 29, she was caught in the midst of a random shooting that left her paralyzed from the waist down. I asked how she dealt with the realization that she’d never walk again, and she confessed that initially she didn’t want to face it. After a year of depression she tried to kill herself. She was then admitted to a hospital for treatment, where she was able to recover.

Whitfield said she came to understand that the only thing she had lost in this misfortunate event was the ability to walk. She still possessed her most valuable asset—her mind. Pointing to her head, she said, “Everything important is in here. The only real disability in life is losing your mind.” When I asked if she was angry about what she had lost, she admitted to being frustrated occasionally, “especially when everybody’s dancing, because I love to dance. But when that happens I just remove myself so I can focus instead on what I can do.”

zh: Wesla Whitfield 是知名的爵士歌手，她的風格和人生故事都很獨特，所以我決定去看她的一場演出，並且為我的專欄採訪她。
我到紐約的一家夜總會，看著舞台燈光亮起。樂團演奏完前奏後，Wesla Whitfield 坐著輪椅，自己把輪椅推上台。她一開口唱歌，歌聲渾厚、充滿感情，全場的人都忘了輪椅的存在。
57 歲的 Whitfield 個子嬌小、長得漂亮，風趣又謙虛，堅毅又豁達。她在加州長大，18 歲開始公開演出，那時她在一家披薩店找到一份工作，當會唱歌的服務生。大學念古典音樂之後，她搬到舊金山，後來加入舊金山歌劇院合唱團演唱。
29 歲那年，她排練完走路回家，遇上一場隨機槍擊，從此腰部以下癱瘓。我問她得知自己再也不能走路時是怎麼面對的，她坦承一開始不想面對。憂鬱了一年之後，她企圖自殺。後來她住進醫院接受治療，在那裡才恢復過來。
Whitfield 說，她後來明白，在這場不幸的事件裡，她失去的只有走路的能力。她最寶貴的資產，也就是她的心智，依然還在。她指著自己的頭說：「重要的東西都在這裡。人生唯一真正的殘缺，是失去心智。」我問她會不會為失去的東西感到憤怒，她承認偶爾會覺得挫折，「尤其是大家都在跳舞的時候，因為我很愛跳舞。不過遇到這種時候，我就離開現場，好把心思放在我能做的事情上。」

title: 餐叉的演進史（The Evolution of the Fork）
paras: Forks trace their origins back to the ancient Greeks. Forks at that time were fairly large with two tines that aided in the carving of meat in the kitchen. The tines prevented meat from twisting or moving during carving and allowed food to slide off more easily than it would with a knife.

By the 7th century A.D., royal courts of the Middle East began to use forks at the table for dining. From the 10th through the 13th centuries, forks were fairly common among the wealthy in Byzantium. In the 11th century, a Byzantine wife brought forks to Italy; however, they were not widely adopted there until the 16th century. Then in 1533, forks were brought from Italy to France. The French were also slow to accept forks, for using them was thought to be awkward.

In 1608, forks were brought to England by Thomas Coryate, who saw them during his travels in Italy. The English first ridiculed forks as being unnecessary. “Why should a person need a fork when God had given him hands?” they asked. Slowly, however, forks came to be adopted by the wealthy as a symbol of their social status. They were prized possessions made of expensive materials intended to impress guests. By the mid 1600s, eating with forks was considered fashionable among the wealthy British.

Early table forks were modeled after kitchen forks, but small pieces of food often fell through the two tines or slipped off easily. In late 17th century France, larger forks with four curved tines were developed. The additional tines made diners less likely to drop food, and the curved tines served as a scoop so people did not have to constantly switch to a spoon while eating. By the early 19th century, four-tined forks had also been developed in Germany and England and slowly began to spread to America.

outline: 追溯叉子源自古希臘，起初是廚房切肉用的兩齒大叉。
(By the 7th century A.D.) 中東宮廷開始用叉子進餐，(In the 11th century) 傳入義大利，(Then in 1533) 再傳入法國，但兩地都接受得很慢。
(In 1608) 叉子傳入英國，起初英國人嘲笑叉子沒有必要。
(Slowly, however) 叉子成為富人地位的象徵，(By the mid 1600s) 用叉子吃飯成為時尚。
(In late 17th century) 法國發展出四齒彎叉，不易掉食物又能舀，(By the early 19th century) 之後傳到德、英、美。

zh: 叉子的起源可以追溯到古希臘人。當時的叉子相當大，有兩根叉齒，在廚房裡用來幫忙切肉。切肉時，叉齒能讓肉不會扭動或移動，食物從叉子上滑下來，也比從刀子上滑下來容易。
到了西元七世紀，中東的宮廷開始在餐桌上用叉子吃飯。十到十三世紀，叉子在拜占庭的富人之間相當普遍。十一世紀時，一位拜占庭籍的妻子把叉子帶到義大利；不過，直到十六世紀，義大利人才廣泛使用叉子。接著在 1533 年，叉子從義大利傳到法國。法國人也很慢才接受叉子，因為他們認為用叉子很彆扭。
1608 年，Thomas Coryate 把叉子帶到英國，他是在義大利旅行時看到叉子的。英國人起初嘲笑叉子是多餘的東西。他們問：「上帝都給了人一雙手，人為什麼還需要叉子？」不過，富人慢慢用起叉子，把叉子當作社會地位的象徵。這些叉子是珍貴的財產，用昂貴的材料做成，為的是讓客人留下深刻的印象。到了 1600 年代中期，用叉子吃飯在英國富人之間已經是一種時尚。
早期的餐叉是照著廚房用的叉子做的，但小塊食物常常從兩根叉齒之間掉下去，或是很容易滑落。十七世紀末，法國發展出比較大、有四根彎曲叉齒的叉子。多了叉齒，用餐的人比較不容易讓食物掉下來；彎曲的叉齒還可以當杓子用，吃東西時就不必一直換成湯匙。到了十九世紀初，德國和英國也發展出四齒叉，並且慢慢傳到美國。

title: 如何拍攝動物（How to Photograph Animals）
paras: Animals are a favorite subject of many photographers. Cats, dogs, and other pets top the list, followed by zoo animals. However, because it’s hard to get them to sit still and “perform on command,” some professional photographers refuse to photograph pets.

One way to get an appealing portrait of a cat or dog is to hold a biscuit or treat above the camera. The animal’s longing look toward the food will be captured by the camera, but the treat won’t appear in the picture because it’s out of the camera’s range. When you show the picture to your friends afterwards, they’ll be impressed by your pet’s loving expression.

If you are using fast film, you can take some good, quick shots of a pet by simply snapping a picture right after calling its name. You’ll get a different expression from your pet using this technique. Depending on your pet’s mood, the picture will capture an interested, curious expression or possibly a look of annoyance, especially if you’ve awakened it from a nap.

Taking pictures of zoo animals requires a little more patience. After all, you can’t wake up a lion! You may have to wait for a while until the animal does something interesting or moves into a position for you to get a good shot. When photographing zoo animals, don’t get too close to the cages, and never tap on the glass or throw things between the bars of a cage. Concentrate on shooting some good pictures, and always respect the animals you are photographing.

要替貓或狗拍出討人喜愛的照片，有一個方法是把餅乾或零食舉在相機上方。相機會拍下寵物望著食物的渴望眼神，但零食不會出現在照片裡，因為零食在相機的拍攝範圍之外。事後你把照片拿給朋友看，朋友會對你家寵物充滿愛意的表情印象深刻。
如果你用的是高感光度底片，只要叫寵物的名字，然後馬上按下快門，就能迅速拍出幾張好照片。用這個技巧可以拍到寵物不同的表情。依寵物當時的心情而定，照片可能拍到感興趣、好奇的表情，也可能是一臉不耐煩，尤其是你把寵物從午睡中吵醒的時候。
拍動物園的動物需要多一點耐心。畢竟，你總不能把獅子叫醒吧！你可能得等一陣子，等動物做出有趣的動作，或是移動到好拍的位置。拍動物園的動物時，不要太靠近籠子，也絕對不要敲玻璃，或把東西丟進籠子的欄杆之間。專心拍出好照片，而且永遠要尊重你拍攝的動物。

title: 肢體語言的迷思（Myths of Body Language）
paras: There is a long-held belief that when meeting someone, the more eye contact we have with the person, the better. The result is an unfortunate tendency for people making initial contact—in a job interview, for example—to stare fixedly at the other individual. However, this behavior is likely to make the interviewer feel very uncomfortable. Most of us are comfortable with eye contact lasting a few seconds. But eye contact which persists longer than that can make us nervous.

Another widely accepted belief is that powerful people in a society—often men—show their dominance over others by touching them in a variety of ways. In fact, research shows that in almost all cases, lower-status people initiate touch. Women also initiate touch more often than men do.

The belief that rapid speech and lying go together is also widespread and enduring. We react strongly—and suspiciously—to fast talk. However, the opposite is a greater cause for suspicion. Speech that is slow, because it is laced with pauses or errors, is a more reliable indicator of lying than the opposite.

outline: 迷思一：眼神接觸越多越好，(However) 但凝視太久會讓人不自在。
迷思二：有權勢的人主動觸碰別人，(In fact) 研究顯示多半是地位較低的人主動觸碰，女性也比男性常主動。
迷思三：說話快代表說謊，(However) 其實說話慢、停頓多才更可能是說謊。

zh: 一直以來有一種說法：跟人見面時，和對方眼神接觸得越多越好。結果就造成一種不好的傾向：人們初次見面時，例如在工作面試中，會目不轉睛地盯著對方。然而，這樣做很可能讓面試官非常不自在。大部分人能接受持續幾秒鐘的眼神接觸，但是超過這個時間的眼神接觸，就可能讓我們緊張。
另一個普遍的說法是，社會上有權勢的人（往往是男性）會用各種方式觸碰別人，來顯示自己的支配地位。事實上，研究顯示，幾乎在所有情況下，都是地位較低的人主動觸碰別人。女性也比男性更常主動觸碰別人。
說話快和說謊脫不了關係，這種看法也同樣普遍，而且根深柢固。我們對說話快的人反應強烈，而且會起疑心。然而，反過來的情況才更值得懷疑。說話慢，是因為話裡夾雜了停頓或錯誤；比起說話快，說話慢更能可靠地看出對方在說謊。

title: 大象的辨敵能力（Elephants' Ability to Identify Enemies）
paras: It is easy for us to tell our friends from our enemies. But can other animals do the same? Elephants can! They can use their sense of vision and smell to tell the difference between people who pose a threat and those who do not.

In Kenya, researchers found that elephants react differently to clothing worn by men of the Maasai and Kamba ethnic groups. Young Maasai men spear animals and thus pose a threat to elephants; Kamba men are mainly farmers and are not a danger to elephants.

In an experiment conducted by animal scientists, elephants were first presented with clean clothing or clothing that had been worn for five days by either a Maasai or a Kamba man. When the elephants detected the smell of clothing worn by a Maasai man, they moved away from the smell faster and took longer to relax than when they detected the smells of either clothing worn by Kamba men or clothing that had not been worn at all.

Garment color also plays a role, though in a different way. In the same study, when the elephants saw red clothing not worn before, they reacted angrily, as red is typically worn by Maasai men. Rather than running away as they did with the smell, the elephants acted aggressively toward the red clothing.

The researchers believe that the elephants’ emotional reactions are due to their different interpretations of the smells and the sights. Smelling a potential danger means that a threat is nearby and the best thing to do is run away and hide. Seeing a potential threat without its smell means that risk is low. Therefore, instead of showing fear and running away, the elephants express their anger and become aggressive.

outline: 提出主題：大象能用視覺和嗅覺分辨敵友。
說明肯亞的馬賽族男性獵殺大象，(thus) 構成威脅，坎巴族則以務農為主。
嗅覺實驗：聞到馬賽族穿過的衣服，大象逃得更快，也較久才放鬆。
(though in a different way) 視覺實驗：看到馬賽族常穿的紅色衣服，(Rather than) 大象不逃跑，反而發動攻擊。
(Therefore, instead of) 研究者解釋：聞到氣味代表危險就在附近，只看到威脅則代表風險低，所以表現憤怒。

zh: 我們要分辨朋友和敵人很容易。但其他動物也做得到嗎？大象就做得到！大象能用視覺和嗅覺，分辨哪些人會構成威脅、哪些人不會。
研究人員在肯亞發現，大象對馬賽族和坎巴族男性穿過的衣服反應不同。年輕的馬賽族男性會用長矛獵殺動物，因此對大象構成威脅；坎巴族男性大多是農夫，對大象沒有危險。
在動物學家進行的一項實驗中，研究人員先讓大象接觸乾淨的衣服，或是馬賽族男性、坎巴族男性穿了五天的衣服。大象聞到馬賽族男性穿過的衣服時，比聞到坎巴族男性穿過的衣服或完全沒穿過的衣服，離開氣味的速度更快，也要更久才能放鬆下來。
衣服的顏色也有影響，不過方式不同。在同一項研究中，大象看到沒穿過的紅色衣服時，會生氣地做出反應，因為馬賽族男性通常穿紅色。大象不像聞到氣味時那樣逃跑，而是對紅色衣服表現出攻擊性。
研究人員認為，大象會有不同的情緒反應，是因為大象對氣味和視覺的解讀不同。聞到潛在的危險，表示威脅就在附近，最好的辦法就是逃跑躲起來。只看到潛在的威脅卻沒有聞到氣味，表示風險很低。因此，大象不會害怕逃跑，而是表現出憤怒，變得有攻擊性。

title: 從受傷到助人的籃球員（A Basketball Player's New Direction in Life）
paras: It was something she had dreamed of since she was five. Finally, after years of training and intensive workouts, Deborah Duffey was going to compete in her first high school basketball game. The goals of becoming an outstanding player and playing college ball were never far from Deborah’s mind.

The game was against Mills High School. With 1:42 minutes left in the game, Deborah’s team led by one point. A player of Mills had possession of the ball, and Deborah ran to guard against her. As Deborah shuffled sideways to block the player, her knee went out and she collapsed on the court in burning pain. Just like that, Deborah’s season was over.

After suffering the bad injury, Deborah found that, for the first time in her life, she was in a situation beyond her control. Game after game, she could do nothing but sit on the sidelines watching others play the game that she loved so much.

Injuries limited Deborah’s time on the court as she hurt her knees three more times in the next five years. She had to spend countless hours in a physical therapy clinic to receive treatment. Her frequent visits there gave her a passion and respect for the profession. And Deborah began to see a new light in her life.

Currently a senior in college, Deborah focuses on pursuing a degree in physical therapy. After she graduates, Deborah plans to use her knowledge to educate people how to best take care of their bodies and cope with the feelings of hopelessness that she remembers so well.

這場比賽的對手是 Mills 高中。比賽剩下 1 分 42 秒時，Deborah 的球隊領先一分。Mills 高中的一名球員持球，Deborah 跑過去防守。Deborah 側身滑步要擋住那名球員時，膝蓋突然受傷，她倒在球場上，痛得像火燒一樣。就這樣，Deborah 的球季結束了。
受了這次重傷之後，Deborah 發現自己生平第一次遇到無法掌控的處境。一場又一場比賽，她只能坐在場邊，看著別人打她那麼熱愛的籃球。
接下來五年裡，Deborah 的膝蓋又受傷了三次，傷勢讓她上場的時間很有限。她得在物理治療診所花上數不清的時間接受治療。因為常常去那裡，她對物理治療這一行產生了熱情和敬意。Deborah 開始在人生中看見新的曙光。

title: 紅杉的生態（The Ecology of Redwood Trees）
paras: Redwood trees are the tallest plants on the earth, reaching heights of up to 100 meters. They are also known for their longevity, typically 500 to 1000 years, but sometimes more than 2000 years. A hundred million years ago, in the age of dinosaurs, redwoods were common in the forests of a much more moist and tropical North America. As the climate became drier and colder, they retreated to a narrow strip along the Pacific coast of Northern California.

The trunk of redwood trees is very stout and usually forms a single straight column. It is covered with a beautiful soft, spongy bark. This bark can be pretty thick, well over two feet in the more mature trees. It gives the older trees a certain kind of protection from insects, but the main benefit is that it keeps the center of the tree intact from moderate forest fires because of its thickness. This fire resistant quality explains why the giant redwood grows to live that long. While most other types of trees are destroyed by forest fires, the giant redwood actually prospers because of them. Moderate fires will clear the ground of competing plant life, and the rising heat dries and opens the ripe cones of the redwood, releasing many thousands of seeds onto the ground below.

New trees are often produced from sprouts, little baby trees, which form at the base of the trunk. These sprouts grow slowly, nourished by the root system of the “mother” tree. When the main tree dies, the sprouts are then free to grow as full trees, forming a “fairy ring” of trees around the initial tree. These trees, in turn, may give rise to more sprouts, and the cycle continues.

outline: 介紹紅杉是地球上最高的植物，壽命長達數百到兩千年以上。
(As) 氣候變得乾冷，紅杉從北美各地退縮到加州太平洋沿岸。
說明樹皮厚實，可防蟲，(because) 更能保護樹心不受火災破壞，所以長壽。
(While) 其他樹毀於森林火災，紅杉反而受惠：火清除競爭植物，熱氣使毬果張開散播種子。
新樹常從樹幹基部的嫩芽長出，母樹死後形成「仙女環」，(in turn) 循環不息。

zh: 紅杉是地球上最高的植物，可以長到 100 公尺高。紅杉也以長壽聞名，通常能活 500 到 1000 年，有時甚至超過 2000 年。一億年前的恐龍時代，北美洲比現在潮濕得多，屬於熱帶氣候，當時紅杉在森林裡很常見。後來氣候變得比較乾冷，紅杉就退縮到北加州太平洋沿岸的一條狹長地帶。

紅杉的樹幹非常粗壯，通常長成一根筆直的柱子。樹幹外面覆蓋著漂亮、柔軟、像海綿一樣的樹皮。這層樹皮可以相當厚，比較成熟的樹，樹皮厚度超過兩英尺。樹皮讓老樹在某種程度上不受昆蟲侵害，但最主要的好處是，樹皮夠厚，遇到中等規模的森林火災時，能保護樹心完好無損。這種耐火的特性，就是巨大的紅杉能活那麼久的原因。大部分其他種類的樹木會毀於森林火災，巨大的紅杉卻反而因為森林火災長得更好。中等規模的火災會清除地面上和紅杉競爭的植物，上升的熱氣也會烘乾成熟的紅杉毬果，讓毬果張開，把成千上萬顆種子撒在下方的地面上。
新的樹常常從嫩芽長出來，嫩芽就是樹幹基部長出的小樹苗。這些嫩芽長得很慢，靠「母樹」的根系提供養分。母樹死了以後，嫩芽就能自由長成大樹，在原來那棵樹的周圍形成一圈「仙女環」。這些樹接著又可能長出更多嫩芽，就這樣循環下去。

title: 陶笛的歷史與文化（The History and Culture of the Ocarina）
paras: The ocarina, a flute-like musical instrument, has been around since the Stone Age. Ocarinas have been found in Africa, Asia, Europe, and South America. Most of those found were made from clay while some were made of bone, wood, and other materials. Because they produce sounds similar to bird calls, ocarinas have been credited with magical powers.

One variation of the ocarina in Chinese culture is the xun, which has a history of more than 7,000 years. It is made of earthenware clay and often comes in the shape of an egg. At various times in Chinese music history, the instrument has played an important role in the imperial orchestra for religious worship and palace entertainment.

Ocarinas were also found to serve various purposes in other cultures. For example, the Mayans of South America, like the Chinese, also used ocarinas for special ceremonies. From there European travelers brought this South American “whistle” back, and it was later modified to play the Western scale. In the 1800s, Italy saw the greatest development of the ocarina, where musicians formed groups to play ocarinas of various sizes. During World War II the ocarina was introduced to the United States and playing it became a pastime for soldiers.

In the 20th century, the ocarina was popular among the general public, and the application of ocarina music was extended to video games. In 1999, Nintendo released Zelda: the Ocarina of Time, the most popular video game of all time. The game features a character named Link who plays songs on an ocarina in order to go to different areas of the game.

outline: 陶笛歷史悠久，可追溯到石器時代，(Because) 因為聲音像鳥叫，古人認為它有魔力。
介紹中國的塤，有七千多年歷史，用於宮廷宗教祭祀與娛樂。
(For example) 舉馬雅人用陶笛於儀式為例，(From there) 之後傳入歐洲並改良，(In the 1800s) 在義大利發展最盛，(During World War II) 二戰時傳入美國。
(In the 20th century) 陶笛普及大眾，應用延伸到電玩。
(In 1999) 以任天堂《薩爾達傳說：時之笛》為例。

zh: 陶笛是一種類似長笛的樂器，從石器時代就已經存在。非洲、亞洲、歐洲和南美洲都發現過陶笛。發現的陶笛大多是用黏土做的，也有一些是用骨頭、木頭和其他材料做成。陶笛發出的聲音很像鳥叫，所以人們認為陶笛有神奇的魔力。
陶笛在中國文化裡的一種變化型是塤，有七千多年的歷史。塤是用陶土燒製而成，常常做成蛋的形狀。在中國音樂史上的不同時期，塤曾經在宮廷樂隊裡扮演重要的角色，用於宗教祭祀和宮廷娛樂。
在其他文化裡，陶笛也有各種用途。例如南美洲的馬雅人和中國人一樣，也在特殊的儀式上使用陶笛。後來歐洲的旅人把這種南美洲的「哨子」帶回歐洲，經過改良，陶笛就能吹奏西方音階。1800 年代，陶笛在義大利發展得最好，樂手組成樂團，吹奏各種尺寸的陶笛。第二次世界大戰期間，陶笛傳入美國，吹陶笛成為士兵的消遣。
二十世紀時，陶笛在一般大眾之間很受歡迎，陶笛音樂的應用也延伸到電玩遊戲。1999 年，任天堂推出《薩爾達傳說：時之笛》，這是有史以來最受歡迎的電玩遊戲。遊戲裡有一個叫做 Link 的角色，他用陶笛吹奏樂曲，好前往遊戲裡的不同區域。

title: 加拿大、法國與義大利的親子關係研究（Parent-Child Bonds in Canada, France, and Italy Study）
paras: A recent study examined the emotional bond between parents and their children. The researchers surveyed 1,256 students in Canada, France, and Italy. Professor Michel Claes, the leader of the research team, explained why they selected the three countries: “We chose French-Canadians because they share the same language as the French, and originally came from France. They share certain values. Italy was included because it was considered to have similar, strong, important family values.”

The most important finding of the study was the difference between Canadians and the others. Canadian parents value independence and are more willing to enter discussions with their children when there are disagreements. They are more tolerant and exercise less control. In contrast, Italian parents are stricter and more demanding. French parents are somewhere in the middle. In other words, Canadian parents are more lenient with their children than parents in France and Italy. Professor Claes explained the finding in terms of differences in education. “North America has its own democratic and educational values, which promote individualization. Tolerance and comprehension are encouraged and we exclude systems of control. Italy, on the other hand, promotes the respect of authority, control, and the need for permission,” he said.

Children from all three countries described their mothers as warm and open. Italian and Canadian children had similar feelings about their fathers and reported high levels of emotional bonding. But French fathers were seen by their children as being more distant. It seemed that the relationships of French mothers with their children were becoming closer over time; but fathers maintained a certain distance and coldness.

outline: 介紹一項親子情感連結的研究，說明選擇加拿大、法國、義大利的原因。
研究最重要的發現：加拿大父母重視獨立、較寬容，(In contrast) 義大利父母較嚴格，法國居中。
(In other words) 加拿大父母最寬鬆，研究者從教育價值觀解釋，(on the other hand) 義大利則重視權威與控制。
三國子女都覺得母親溫暖開放，義大利與加拿大子女和父親也很親近。
(But) 法國父親在子女眼中較疏遠冷淡。

zh: 最近一項研究探討父母和子女之間的情感連結。研究人員調查了加拿大、法國和義大利的 1,256 名學生。研究團隊的負責人 Michel Claes 教授說明他們選擇這三個國家的原因：「我們選擇法裔加拿大人，因為他們和法國人說同一種語言，祖先也來自法國，兩者有某些共同的價值觀。納入義大利，則是因為大家認為義大利也有類似的、強烈而重要的家庭價值觀。」

這項研究最重要的發現，是加拿大人和其他兩國的差異。加拿大的父母重視獨立，和子女意見不合時，比較願意和子女討論。加拿大的父母比較寬容，管得比較少。相反地，義大利的父母比較嚴格，要求也比較多。法國的父母則介於兩者之間。換句話說，加拿大的父母對子女比法國和義大利的父母寬鬆。Claes 教授從教育的差異解釋這項發現：「北美洲有自己的民主價值觀和教育價值觀，鼓勵個人化。我們鼓勵寬容和理解，排除控制的體系。另一方面，義大利重視尊重權威、控制，以及凡事要先得到允許。」
三個國家的子女都形容自己的母親溫暖、開放。義大利和加拿大的子女對父親的感覺相似，都表示和父親的情感連結很深。但是在法國子女眼中，父親比較疏遠。看起來法國母親和子女的關係隨著時間越來越親近，父親卻一直保持某種距離，態度冷淡。

title: 正面心理學與幸福研究（Positive Psychology and Happiness Research）
paras: Not long ago, joy wasn’t considered serious enough for psychologists to study. These scientists traditionally helped people with depression or other mental illnesses. But today, happiness is a hot subject of research. As part of a growing field called positive psychology, more and more researchers are looking for ways to help people become happier.

However, the field of positive psychology has to overcome significant obstacles. For one thing, it’s difficult to scientifically gauge happiness. It’s also hard to compare one person’s sense of well-being with another’s. For example, if your best friend says she feels great, but she’s crying a lot and acting more depressed than usual, would you rate her as happy or sad for the purposes of a scientific study? Likewise, on a scale of 1 to 10, how can we be sure that my “8” is happier than your “6”?

In recent years, however, researchers have developed a few accurate measurements of happiness. One of the techniques involves looking at how often people genuinely smile in their daily lives. It’s easy to tell real smiles from the fake smiles people put on for photographs. Genuine smiles engage the corners of the eyes and involve muscles around the mouth that fake smilers can’t control.

With the help of these techniques, recent studies have found that the happiest people are those who frequently do kind things for both friends and strangers. Other research-backed happiness boosters include keeping a diary of your future dreams, setting and pursuing goals, making friends and family members a big part of your life, expressing optimism about your future, extending gratitude to people who help you, and exercising regularly.

outline: 過去心理學家不研究快樂，(But today) 如今正向心理學成為熱門研究。
(However) 正向心理學面臨難題，(For one thing) 快樂難以科學測量，也難以跨人比較。
(For example, Likewise) 舉例說明自評與表現不一、分數難以比較的問題。
(however) 近年研究者發展出測量方法，例如觀察真笑的次數。
研究發現最快樂的人常行善，並列舉其他提升快樂的方法。

zh: 不久之前，心理學家還認為快樂不夠嚴肅，不值得研究。這些科學家傳統上幫助的是有憂鬱症或其他心理疾病的人。但是現在，快樂是熱門的研究主題。正向心理學這個領域日漸成長，越來越多研究人員在這個領域裡尋找讓人更快樂的方法。
不過，正向心理學必須克服幾個重大的障礙。第一，快樂很難用科學方法測量。要比較一個人和另一個人的幸福感也很困難。例如，如果你最好的朋友說她感覺很好，卻常常哭，看起來比平常還要沮喪，為了科學研究，你會把她評為快樂還是難過？同樣地，在 1 到 10 的量表上，我們怎麼能確定我的「8」比你的「6」快樂？
不過，近年來研究人員已經發展出幾種準確測量快樂的方法。其中一種技巧是觀察人們在日常生活中真心微笑的頻率。真心的笑容和人們拍照時擺出來的假笑很容易分辨。真心的笑容會牽動眼角，也會用到嘴巴周圍的肌肉，這些肌肉是假笑的人控制不了的。
藉助這些技巧，最近的研究發現，最快樂的人是那些經常替朋友和陌生人做好事的人。其他有研究支持、能提升快樂的方法還包括：把對未來的夢想寫成日記、設定並追求目標、讓親友在生活中占重要的位置、對未來抱持樂觀、向幫助過你的人表達感謝，以及規律運動。

title: 電玩遊戲對決策能力的影響（The Impact of Video Games on Decision-Making Skills）
paras: Video games have been blamed for many of the ills of the world. Parents complain that violent games make their children antisocial, violent, shallow, and overweight. Educators worry that video games are breeding a generation that cannot sustain their concentration.

However, a recent study from cognitive science suggests that there may be a benefit in playing some action games. The research, published in Current Biology, reports that video gamers make faster and more accurate decisions. What was particularly interesting was that the faster reaction times could also be acquired by non-video gamers with 50 hours of training over a few weeks. But for the benefits to increase, they had to play a particular sort of game. Only those who played fast-moving action video games such as “Call of Duty 2” and “Unreal Tournament” saw an improvement in their decision-making skills. Rather ironically, players of “The Sims 2,” a game where one has to decide how to organize an entire simulated world, did not show the same benefit.

The precise reason for this effect is still unknown. What is known, however, is that people make decisions based on probabilities, which are constantly being calculated and refined in their heads. The brain collects small pieces of information, eventually gathering enough to make an accurate decision. When driving a car, for example, these many probabilities will be compared to make decisions such as whether or not to brake. The more efficient a person is at collecting visual and auditory information, the faster he or she will become ready to make a decision.

outline: 家長與教育者批評電玩讓孩子反社會、肥胖、無法專心。
(However) 認知科學研究指出，動作電玩玩家決策更快、更準確，非玩家經過訓練也能獲益。
(But) 只有快節奏的動作遊戲才有效，(Rather ironically) 模擬經營遊戲反而沒有效果。
確切原因仍不清楚，(however) 但已知人是根據大腦不斷計算的機率做決定。
(for example) 以開車煞車為例，蒐集視聽資訊越有效率，決定就越快。

zh: 許多人把世上的種種問題怪到電玩遊戲頭上。家長抱怨暴力遊戲讓孩子變得反社會、暴力、膚淺，而且過胖。教育工作者擔心電玩遊戲正在養出無法持續專注的一代。

然而，認知科學最近的一項研究指出，玩某些動作遊戲可能有好處。這項研究發表在《Current Biology》期刊，指出電玩玩家做決定比較快、也比較準確。特別有意思的是，不玩電玩的人在幾週內接受 50 個小時的訓練，也能練出比較快的反應時間。不過，要讓好處增加，他們必須玩特定類型的遊戲。只有玩快節奏動作遊戲的人，例如《Call of Duty 2》和《Unreal Tournament》，決策能力才有進步。諷刺的是，《The Sims 2》要玩家決定怎麼安排整個模擬世界，玩這款遊戲的人卻沒有得到同樣的好處。
這種效果的確切原因目前還不清楚。不過，已經知道的是，人做決定是根據機率，這些機率在腦中不斷地計算、修正。大腦會蒐集零碎的資訊，最後累積到足夠的資訊，做出準確的決定。例如開車時，大腦會比較這許多機率，決定要不要踩煞車。一個人蒐集視覺和聽覺資訊的效率越高，就能越快準備好做出決定。

title: 紐西蘭特有種昆蟲威塔（The Weta, a Native Insect of New Zealand）
paras: On the island of New Zealand, there is a grasshopper-like species of insect that is found nowhere else on earth. New Zealanders have given it the nickname weta, which is a native Maori word meaning “god of bad looks.” It’s easy to see why anyone would call this insect a bad-looking bug. Most people feel disgusted at the sight of these bulky, slow-moving creatures.

Wetas are nocturnal creatures; they come out of their caves and holes only after dark. A giant weta can grow to over three inches long and weigh as much as 1.5 ounces. Giant wetas can hop up to two feet at a time. Some of them live in trees, and others live in caves. They are very long-lived for insects, and some adult wetas can live as long as two years. Just like their cousins grasshoppers and crickets, wetas are able to “sing” by rubbing their leg parts together, or against their lower bodies.

Most people probably don’t feel sympathy for these endangered creatures, but they do need protecting. The slow and clumsy wetas have been around on the island since the times of the dinosaurs, and have evolved and survived in an environment where they had no enemies until rats came to the island with European immigrants. Since rats love to hunt and eat wetas, the rat population on the island has grown into a real problem for many of the native species that are unaccustomed to its presence, and poses a serious threat to the native weta population.

outline: 介紹紐西蘭特有的昆蟲威塔，毛利語意為「醜陋之神」，多數人看到牠就覺得噁心。
描述威塔的習性：夜間活動、體型大、壽命長，(Just like) 也像蚱蜢、蟋蟀一樣能摩擦腳部發聲。
(but they do need protecting) 指出威塔雖然不討喜，卻需要保護。

(Since) 老鼠愛吃威塔，數量大增，嚴重威脅本地物種與威塔族群。

zh: 紐西蘭島上有一種長得像蚱蜢的昆蟲，在地球上其他地方都找不到。紐西蘭人替這種昆蟲取了個暱稱叫 weta（威塔），這是毛利語，意思是「醜陋之神」。不難理解為什麼有人會說這種昆蟲長得難看。大部分的人看到這種笨重、行動緩慢的生物，都會覺得噁心。
威塔是夜行性動物，天黑以後才會從洞穴和洞裡出來。巨型威塔可以長到三英寸以上，重達 1.5 盎司。巨型威塔一次可以跳兩英尺遠。有些威塔住在樹上，有些住在洞穴裡。以昆蟲來說，威塔非常長壽，有些成蟲可以活到兩年。威塔和牠們的近親蚱蜢、蟋蟀一樣，能把腳的部位互相摩擦，或在下半身上摩擦，發出「歌聲」。
大部分人大概不會同情這些瀕臨絕種的生物，但威塔確實需要保護。行動緩慢又笨拙的威塔從恐龍時代就生活在這座島上，在沒有天敵的環境中演化、生存下來，直到老鼠跟著歐洲移民來到島上。老鼠很愛獵食威塔，島上的老鼠數量已經成了許多本地物種的大問題，這些本地物種不習慣有老鼠存在；老鼠也嚴重威脅本地的威塔族群。

title: 美國高中畢業舞會的演變與意義（The Evolution and Significance of American High School Proms）
paras: The high school prom is the first formal social event for most American teenagers. It has also been a rite of passage for young Americans for nearly a century.

The word “prom” was first used in the 1890s, referring to formal dances in which the guests of a party would display their fashions and dancing skills during the evening’s grand march. In the United States, parents and educators have come to regard the prom as an important lesson in social skills. Therefore, proms have been held every year in high schools for students to learn proper social behavior.

The first high school proms were held in the 1920s in America. By the 1930s, proms were common across the country. For many older Americans, the prom was a modest, home-grown affair in the school gymnasium. Prom-goers were well dressed but not fancily dressed up for the occasion: boys wore jackets and ties and girls their Sunday dresses. Couples danced to music provided by a local amateur band or a record player. After the 1960s, and especially since the 1980s, the high school prom in many areas has become a serious exercise in excessive consumption, with boys renting expensive tuxedos and girls wearing designer gowns. Stretch limousines were hired to drive the prom-goers to expensive restaurants or discos for an all-night extravaganza.

Whether simple or lavish, proms have always been more or less traumatic events for adolescents who worry about self-image and fitting in with their peers. Prom night can be a dreadful experience for socially awkward teens or for those who do not secure dates. Since the 1990s, alternative proms have been organized in some areas to meet the needs of particular students. For example, proms organized by and for homeless youth were reported. There were also “couple-free” proms to which all students are welcome.

outline: 介紹高中畢業舞會是多數美國青少年第一次正式社交活動，也是成年禮。
說明 prom 一詞源自 1890 年代，家長與教育者視舞會為社交課，(Therefore) 所以每年舉辦。
(By the 1930s) 描述早期舞會樸素，(After the 1960s) 後來變得奢華、過度消費。
(Whether simple or lavish) 指出舞會常讓擔心形象、沒有舞伴的青少年感到難熬。
(Since the 1990s) 為了照顧特定學生，出現另類舞會，(For example) 如無家青少年舞會與不需舞伴的舞會。

zh: 對大部分美國青少年來說，高中畢業舞會是他們第一次參加的正式社交活動。將近一百年來，畢業舞會也一直是美國年輕人的成年禮。
「prom」這個字最早出現在 1890 年代，指的是正式的舞會，舞會的賓客會在晚上的開場大遊行中展示自己的服裝和舞技。在美國，家長和教育工作者逐漸把畢業舞會看作學習社交技巧的重要一課。因此，高中每年都會舉辦畢業舞會，讓學生學習合宜的社交行為。

美國最早的高中畢業舞會在 1920 年代舉行。到了 1930 年代，畢業舞會已經遍及全國。對許多年紀較大的美國人來說，畢業舞會是在學校體育館舉辦、簡樸的自辦活動。參加舞會的人穿著得體，但不會為這個場合刻意盛裝打扮：男生穿外套打領帶，女生穿上教堂時穿的洋裝。一對對舞伴隨著當地業餘樂團或唱機播放的音樂跳舞。1960 年代以後，尤其是 1980 年代以來，許多地區的高中畢業舞會變成大肆消費的活動，男生租昂貴的晚禮服，女生穿名牌禮服。參加舞會的人還會租加長型禮車，載他們到昂貴的餐廳或舞廳，狂歡一整夜。
不論簡樸還是奢華，對擔心自我形象、擔心能不能融入同儕的青少年來說，畢業舞會多少都是讓人難熬的事。對不擅社交的青少年，或是找不到舞伴的人來說，畢業舞會的那一晚可能是很可怕的經驗。1990 年代以來，有些地區開始舉辦另類的畢業舞會，滿足特定學生的需求。例如，有報導指出，有無家可歸的青少年自己籌辦、專為他們舉辦的舞會。也有「不需舞伴」的舞會，歡迎所有學生參加。

title: 房屋交換：旅遊新選擇與挑戰（Home Exchange: A New Travel Option and Challenges）
paras: No budget for your vacation? Try home exchanges—swapping houses with strangers. Agree to use each other’s cars, and you can save bucks on car rentals, too.

Home exchanges are not new. At least one group, Intervac, has been facilitating such an arrangement since 1953. But trading online is gaining popularity these days, with several sites in operation, including HomeExchanges. Founded in 1992, with some 28,000 listings, this company bills itself as the world’s largest home exchange club, reporting that membership has increased 30% this year.

The annual fee is usually less than US$100. Members can access thousands of listings for apartments, villas, suburban homes and farms around the world. Initial contact is made via e-mail, with subsequent communication usually by phone. Before a match is made, potential swappers tend to discuss a lot.

However, the concept may sound risky to some people. What about theft? Damage? These are reasonable causes for concern, but equally unlikely. As one swapper puts it, “Nobody is going to fly across the ocean or drive 600 miles to come steal your TV. Besides, at the same time they’re staying in your home, you are staying in their home.”

Exchange sites recommend that swappers discuss such matters ahead of time. They may fill out an agreement spelling out who shoulders which responsibilities if a problem arises. It does not matter if the agreement would hold up in court, but it does give the exchangers a little satisfaction.

Generally, the biggest complaint among home exchangers has to do with different standards of cleanliness. Swappers are supposed to make sure their home is in order before they depart, but one person’s idea of “clean” may be more forgiving than another’s. Some owners say if they come back to a less-than-sparkling kitchen, it may be inconvenient but would not sour them on future exchanges.

outline: 提出省錢度假的辦法：換屋，連車子也交換，(too) 還能省下租車費。
說明換屋不是什麼新鮮事，(But) 不過線上換屋越來越熱門，並介紹最大的換屋網站。
說明年費與聯絡方式：先用電子郵件聯絡，再以電話溝通。
(However) 有人擔心失竊、損壞，但機率不高，(Besides) 雙方同時住在對方家；網站建議事先簽協議劃分責任。
最常見的抱怨是清潔標準不同，(but) 但多數人不會因此放棄下次換屋。

zh: 沒有預算度假嗎？試試換屋吧，也就是和陌生人交換房子住。再約定好互相使用對方的車子，連租車的錢也能省下來。
換屋不是什麼新鮮事。至少有一個團體 Intervac 從 1953 年起就在協助安排這種交換。不過，現在線上交換越來越受歡迎，有好幾個網站在經營，包括 HomeExchanges。這家公司成立於 1992 年，大約有 28,000 筆房屋資料，自稱是全世界最大的換屋俱樂部，並表示今年會員人數增加了 30%。
年費通常不到 100 美元。會員可以查閱全世界數千筆公寓、別墅、郊區住宅和農場的資料。第一次聯絡是透過電子郵件，之後通常改用電話溝通。在配對成功之前，有意交換的雙方往往會討論很多。
不過，有些人可能覺得這個點子聽起來有風險。東西失竊怎麼辦？房子受損怎麼辦？這些擔心都有道理，但同樣都不太可能發生。一位換屋者這樣說：「沒有人會飛越大洋或開 600 英里的車，只為了來偷你的電視。何況他們住在你家的同時，你也正住在他們家。」
換屋網站建議換屋者事先討論這些事情。雙方可以填寫一份協議書，寫清楚萬一出了問題，哪些責任由誰負擔。這份協議在法律上有沒有效力並不重要，但確實能讓交換的雙方安心一點。
一般來說，換屋者最大的抱怨和清潔標準不同有關。換屋者應該在出發前把家裡整理好，但每個人對「乾淨」的標準不同，有人比較寬鬆。有些屋主說，回家時如果發現廚房不夠乾淨，可能會有點不方便，但不會因此不想再換屋。

title: 貝科吉鎮長跑選手的卓越秘訣（The Secrets Behind Bekoji's Excellent Distance Runners）
paras: Bekoji is a small town of farmers and herders in the Ethiopian highlands. There, time almost stands still, and horse-drawn carts outnumber motor vehicles. Yet, it has consistently yielded many of the world’s best distance runners.

It’s tempting, when breathing the thin air of Bekoji, to focus on the special conditions of the place. The town sits on the side of a volcano nearly 10,000 feet above sea level, making daily life a kind of high-altitude training. Children in this region often start running at an early age, covering great distances to fetch water and firewood or to reach the nearest school. Added to this early training is a physical trait shared by people there—disproportionately long legs, which is advantageous for distance runners.

A strong desire burns inside Bekoji’s young runners. Take the case of Million Abate. Forced to quit school in fifth grade after his father died, Abate worked as a shoe-shine boy for years. He saw a hope in running and joined Santayehu Eshetu’s training program. This 18-year-old sprinted to the finish of a 12-mile run with his bare feet bleeding. The coach took off his own Nikes and handed them to him. To help Abate continue running, the coach arranged a motel job for him, which pays $9 a month.

Most families in Bekoji live from hand to mouth, and distance running offers the younger generation a way out. Bekoji’s legend Derartu Tulu, who won the 10,000-meter Olympic gold medals in 1992 and 2000, is a national hero. As a reward, the government gave her a house. She also won millions of dollars in the races.

Motivated by such signs of success, thousands of kids from the villages surrounding Bekoji have moved into town. They crowd the classrooms at Bekoji Elementary School, where Eshetu works as a physical-education instructor. All these kids share the same dream: Some day they could become another Derartu Tulu.

outline: 介紹衣索比亞小鎮貝科吉生活步調緩慢，(Yet) 卻不斷培育出世界頂尖的長跑選手。
說明地理因素：小鎮位於高海拔火山邊，日常生活就是高地訓練。
孩子從小長途奔跑取水、撿柴、上學，(Added to this) 再加上天生的長腿。
年輕跑者渴望改變命運，以 Million Abate 為例，教練送鞋、替他找工作。
長跑是脫離貧窮的出路，(As a reward) 奧運金牌得主 Derartu Tulu 成為國家英雄，激勵數千名孩子湧入鎮上。

zh: 貝科吉是衣索比亞高原上一個住著農民和牧民的小鎮。在那裡，時間幾乎靜止不動，馬車比汽機車還多。然而，這個小鎮卻不斷培養出許多世界頂尖的長跑選手。
呼吸著貝科吉稀薄的空氣，人們很容易就會把焦點放在這個地方的特殊條件上。小鎮位在一座火山的山坡上，海拔將近一萬英尺，日常生活就像一種高海拔訓練。這個地區的孩子常常很小就開始跑步，為了取水、撿柴火或到最近的學校，要跑很長的距離。除了從小就有的這種訓練，當地人還有一個共同的身體特徵：腿長得特別長，這對長跑選手很有利。

貝科吉的年輕跑者心中燃燒著強烈的渴望。以 Million Abate 為例。他五年級時父親過世，不得不輟學，當了好幾年的擦鞋童。他在跑步中看到希望，加入了 Santayehu Eshetu 的訓練計畫。這個 18 歲的年輕人在一次 12 英里的長跑中衝刺到終點，光著的雙腳流著血。教練脫下自己的 Nike 球鞋送給他。為了讓 Abate 能繼續跑步，教練還替他安排了一份汽車旅館的工作，月薪 9 美元。
貝科吉大部分的家庭都過著勉強餬口的日子，長跑替年輕一代提供了一條出路。貝科吉的傳奇人物 Derartu Tulu 在 1992 年和 2000 年都贏得奧運一萬公尺金牌，是國家英雄。政府送她一棟房子作為獎勵。她也在比賽中贏得了數百萬美元的獎金。
在這些成功例子的激勵下，貝科吉周圍村莊的數千個孩子都搬到鎮上。他們擠滿了貝科吉小學的教室，Eshetu 就在這所學校當體育老師。這些孩子都有同一個夢想：有一天能成為下一個 Derartu Tulu。

title: 人類動物園計畫（The Human Zoo Project）
paras: A zoo in America has announced that it will have an enclosure housing people as part of a program to demonstrate humans are part of the animal kingdom. Six people at a time will be housed in an enclosure next to the chimpanzees and gorillas, and be treated like apes. Four groups of six people will be chosen to participate in the month-long project, each group staying in the enclosure for a week. Vets will check their health and they will be given behavioral stimulation devices such as puzzles and exercise equipment. They will be fed like the zoo's other apes, with some food being hidden to encourage their food searching skills.

The Human Zoo has several aims—it will educate people about humans' place in the animal kingdom, and raise awareness of the need for conservation. Most important of all, this project is expected to generate funds for the nation's largest chimpanzee enclosure planned for Monarto Zoo next year. Psychologists also will study the behavior of the humans as they interact in their enclosure.
There will be no “naked apes”; the exhibits will be wearing swimsuits and have a bag-shower to cool off if the weather gets warm. If it turns chilly, they can wear sports suits.

title: 餐廳氛圍的重要性（The Importance of Restaurant Atmosphere）
paras: People are attracted to a restaurant by more than just good food. Equally important is the way people feel while in the restaurant. Their physical and emotional response is a result of the atmosphere—the total environment to which customers are exposed. Atmosphere is made up of the building design, decoration, interior color scheme, texture of the walls, and service. If the guests relax and have a good feeling, the proper atmosphere can make the food, service and whole dining experience seem better.

People want to escape from their problems and everyday surroundings. Thus the atmosphere should project friendliness and comfort, be attractive and interesting. The atmosphere is remembered long after the meal is finished. For the restaurant owner, this means repeat customers and, hopefully, a profitable operation.

Not everyone wants the same restaurant atmosphere. After working all day, most people prefer to eat in a quiet, relaxed, intimate atmosphere. However, for those who work alone in a quiet environment, a noisy cafeteria might provide needed contrast. It is, therefore, very important to be familiar with the characteristics of the people you wish to serve.

People perceive such primary factors as sight, touch, smell, hearing, temperature, and tempo. Together these combine to make the atmosphere. Designing the “right” atmosphere takes careful consideration. The total atmosphere and operation of the restaurant should be geared in a special way. They need to attract the largest number possible from the target group.

outline: 提出吸引顧客的不只是美食，(Equally important is) 更重要的是顧客在餐廳裡的感受（氛圍）。
定義氛圍：由設計、裝飾、色彩、牆面質地、服務等組成，若顧客感到放鬆，氛圍能提升整體用餐體驗。
(Thus) 說明氛圍應營造友善、舒適、吸引人的感覺，(For the restaurant owner) 這意味著回頭客和營利。
(However) 指出不同顧客對氛圍有不同需求，(Therefore) 了解目標客群的特點很重要。
(Together these combine to make) 總結氛圍由多種感知因素結合而成，設計「正確」氛圍需仔細考量，以吸引目標客群。

zh: 吸引人們上餐廳的不只是好吃的食物。人在餐廳裡的感受同樣重要。顧客生理上和情緒上的反應，來自餐廳的氛圍，也就是顧客身處的整個環境。氛圍由建築設計、裝潢、室內配色、牆面質感和服務構成。如果客人放鬆下來、感覺很好，對的氛圍能讓食物、服務和整個用餐經驗都顯得更好。
人們想要逃開自己的煩惱和每天的生活環境。所以餐廳的氛圍應該讓人覺得友善、舒適，而且要吸引人、有意思。一頓飯吃完很久以後，人們還會記得那裡的氛圍。對餐廳老闆來說，這代表會有回頭客，也希望能因此賺錢。
不是每個人都想要同樣的餐廳氛圍。工作一整天以後，大多數人比較喜歡在安靜、放鬆、溫馨的氛圍裡吃飯。不過，對獨自在安靜環境裡工作的人來說，吵鬧的自助餐廳或許正好提供他們需要的反差。所以，了解你想服務的客人有什麼特點，是非常重要的。
人會感受到視覺、觸覺、嗅覺、聽覺、溫度和節奏這些主要的因素。這些因素結合起來，就構成了氛圍。設計出「對的」氛圍，需要仔細考量。餐廳整體的氛圍和經營都應該特別安排，要盡可能吸引最多的目標客群。

title: 喬治·馬洛里與聖母峰之謎（George Mallory and the Everest Mystery）
paras: George Leigh Mallory (1886-1924) was a British pioneering mountaineer, who was engaged in early attempts to conquer the world’s tallest mountain, Everest. He participated in three British attempts in 1921, 1922 and 1924. In the 1922 expedition, he reached a height of 27,000 feet. He retreated due to an avalanche (snow slide) in which seven Sherpa climbers lost their lives. The 1924 climb was his final one. Mallory and his partner, Sandy Irvine, departed from the high camp on June 8. They were even seen by geologist Noel Odell during a short break in the blowing snow as they moved toward the Second Step. After that there was no news of them—they were lost in the vast North Face of Everest. In 1960 Chinese climbers completed the same route that Mallory and Irvine attempted. A Chinese climber reportedly found a body believed to be Irvine’s at that time. In 1999 American climber Conrad Anker found the frozen body of Mallory at 26,760 feet. A positive identification was made by Mallory’s name label on the torn clothing. The appearance of Mallory’s body has again heated up the debate. Did Mallory and Irvine first reach the peak of Everest? Or did Sir Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay reach the summit in June of 1953 as is officially cited? While that debate continues, there is one thing that is certain—in March 1923, a reporter from The New York Times interviewed George Mallory. He asked Mallory, “Why do you want to climb Mount Everest?” His reply has become famous; he said, “Because it’s there.”

outline: 介紹 George Leigh Mallory 是一位英國登山先驅，早期嘗試征服聖母峰，參與三次遠征。
描述他 1922 年的嘗試因雪崩而撤退，1924 年是他最後一次攀登，與 Sandy Irvine 一同出發。
(After that) 他們失蹤於聖母峰北壁。(In 1960) 1960 年中國登山者完成相同路線，據報發現疑似 Irvine 的遺體。
(In 1999) 1999 年有人找到 Mallory 的遺體，他是不是第一個登頂的人又引起爭論。
(While that debate continues) 儘管爭論持續，(In March 1923) 但 Mallory 那句「因為山在那裡」的回答已成名言。

zh: George Leigh Mallory（1886–1924）是英國的登山先驅，曾參與早期征服世界最高峰聖母峰的嘗試。他參加了英國在 1921、1922 和 1924 年的三次攀登。1922 年的遠征，他爬到了 27,000 英尺的高度，後來因為一場雪崩撤退，七名雪巴登山者在那場雪崩中喪生。1924 年那次是他最後一次攀登。6 月 8 日，Mallory 和他的搭檔 Sandy Irvine 從高地營出發。地質學家 Noel Odell 還趁著風雪短暫停歇的時候，看見他們朝第二台階前進。在那之後就再也沒有他們的消息，兩人消失在聖母峰廣大的北壁上。1960 年，中國登山者走完了 Mallory 和 Irvine 當年嘗試的同一條路線。據報導，當時一名中國登山者發現一具相信是 Irvine 的遺體。1999 年，美國登山者 Conrad Anker 在 26,760 英尺處找到 Mallory 已經凍僵的遺體。從破爛衣服上的名牌，確認了這是 Mallory。Mallory 遺體的出現，讓這場爭論再度熱烈起來：最早登上聖母峰峰頂的，是 Mallory 和 Irvine 嗎？還是像官方記載的，是 Edmund Hillary 爵士和雪巴人 Tenzing Norgay 在 1953 年 6 月登頂？這場爭論還在持續，不過有一件事是確定的：1923 年 3 月，《紐約時報》的記者訪問 George Mallory，問他：「你為什麼想爬聖母峰？」他的回答後來非常有名，他說：「因為山就在那裡。」

title: 哲學的本質與任務（The Nature and Tasks of Philosophy）
paras: Philosophy is not a subject but an activity. You don’t study it; you do it. To be a philosopher, therefore, you need not be an academic, or an expert on the history of the practice of philosophy. However, you do need to think and argue in a particular way. You might already be a philosopher without knowing it.

The word “philosophy,” which means “love of knowledge,” comes from the Greek language. The earliest philosophers among the ancient Greeks were also mathematicians and scientists. These were people who had the tendency and also, crucially, the time to seek knowledge, because they had slaves to do all of the labor work.

Broadly speaking, there are two tasks for philosophers. The first is to search for truth. However, many philosophers say they don’t know what the word “truth” means, while other philosophers don’t think it exists at all. The search for truth is not the central concern of most academic philosophers, but that doesn’t mean everyone else shouldn’t have a go at it.

The second task is about the application of logical thinking to everyday questions, concepts, and ideas that are often taken for granted. This kind of conceptual analysis serves to clarify debate over the meaning of such concepts as justice, knowledge, and human nature. There is no point arguing about justice, knowledge, perception, or human nature unless we have some idea about what kind of things these terms might mean.
accuracyRateSource: 本卷非正式施測，無答對率

outline: (therefore) 定義哲學為一種活動而非學科，任何人無需學術背景都可成為哲學家，只要 (However) 以特定方式思考和論證。
解釋「哲學」一詞源自希臘語，意為「愛知識」，古代希臘哲學家同時也是數學家和科學家，他們有時間追求知識。
(Broadly speaking) 闡述哲學家的第一個任務：探索真理，但真理的定義與存在性有爭議。
(The second task is about) 闡述哲學家的第二個任務：將邏輯思維應用於日常概念分析，(unless) 以澄清諸如正義、知識、人性等詞語的意義。

zh: 哲學不是一門學科，而是一種活動。哲學不是拿來研讀的，而是拿來做的。所以要當哲學家，你不必是學者，也不必精通哲學發展的歷史。不過，你確實需要用一種特別的方式思考和論證。你可能已經是一位哲學家，只是自己不知道。
「哲學」這個詞的意思是「愛知識」，源自希臘文。古希臘最早的哲學家也是數學家和科學家。這些人有追求知識的傾向，而且很關鍵的是，他們也有追求知識的時間，因為他們有奴隸替他們做所有勞力的工作。
大致說來，哲學家有兩項任務。第一項是追求真理。然而，許多哲學家說他們不知道「真理」這個詞是什麼意思，另一些哲學家則認為真理根本不存在。追求真理不是大多數學院派哲學家關心的重點，但這不表示其他人不該試試看。
第二項任務是把邏輯思考應用在日常的問題、概念和想法上，這些東西往往大家都認為理所當然。這種概念分析能釐清大家對正義、知識、人性這類概念的意義有什麼爭論。如果我們對這些詞可能指什麼東西都沒有概念，爭論正義、知識、感知或人性就沒有意義。

title: 保險公司寫給「無所事事協會」的信（An Insurance Company’s Letter to the Institute of Not Doing Much）
paras: To Whom It May Concern:

Your address was forwarded to us by Why Bother Magazine. All of us here think The International Institute of Not Doing Much is the best organization in the world. You know how to avoid unnecessary activities!

We closely followed the advice in your article. First, we replaced all our telephones with carrier pigeons. Simply removing the jingle of telephones and replacing them with the pleasant sounds of birds has had a remarkable effect on everyone. Besides, birds are cheaper than telephone service. After all, we are a business. We have to think of the bottom line. As a side benefit, the birds also fertilize the lawn outside the new employee sauna.

Next, we sold the computers off to Stab, Grab, Grit, and Nasty, a firm of lawyers nearby. Our electricity bill went way down. Big savings! The boss is impressed. We have completely embraced paper technology. Now that we all use pencils, doodling is on the increase, and the quality of pencilwomanship is impressive, as you can tell from my handwriting in this letter. By the way, if you can, please send this letter back to us. We can erase and reuse it. Just tie it to Maggie’s leg and she’ll know where to take it.

Now it’s very calm and quiet here. You can notice the difference. No more loud chatter on the telephones! All we hear is the scratching of pencil on paper, the sound of pigeons, and the delivery of inter-office correspondence by paper airplane.
Wonderful! I’ve always wanted to work for an insurance company ever since I was a little girl. Now it’s perfect.

Sincerely yours,
Eleanor Lightly
Spokeswoman and Company Hair Stylist
ABC Activity Insurance: Insure against overdoing it

title: 加拉巴哥群島的綠色機場（The Green Airport of the Galápagos Islands）
paras: The Galápagos Islands are the Pacific island paradise where Darwin’s theory of evolution was born. They are places filled with giant tree lizards, sandy beaches, and tropical plants. Now they will be famous for one more thing: the world’s first green airport.

This group of islands off the coast of Ecuador has recently contracted Argentine Corporación America to manage the redevelopment of the airport on the island of Baltra. It is estimated that US$20 million is needed to complete the project by 2009. The new development has several important features: use of wind and solar energy, passive heating and cooling systems, as well as concrete runways in place of asphalt, which has a greater carbon footprint during its production cycle. This new development couldn’t be coming at a better time for the Galápagos, which were added to an environmental “danger list” in 2007.

Pacific islands like the Galápagos, Easter Island, and Tahiti, have economies that are driven almost completely by tourism. However, some people think these are “unsustainable models of development.” The number of visitors to the Galápagos rose more than 250% from 1990 to 2006, while the number of commercial flights to the area rose 193% from 2001 to 2006. These increases put great stress on the islands’ resources and environment. Air travel is especially criticized for exhausting natural resources and causing environmental damage. Thus, efforts are being made to reduce the environmental impact of the tourism industry. The greening of airports is just one of these attempts.
accuracyRateSource: 大考中心 98 學年度學科能力測驗統計圖表：英文科答對率及鑑別指數表

zh: 加拉巴哥群島是太平洋上的島嶼天堂，達爾文的演化論就在這裡誕生。這裡有巨大的樹蜥、沙灘和熱帶植物。現在，這些島嶼又要以另一件事聞名：世界上第一座綠色機場。

這個位於厄瓜多外海的群島，最近和阿根廷的 Corporación America 公司簽約，委託這家公司負責巴爾特拉島上機場的重建。估計需要 2,000 萬美元，才能在 2009 年以前完成這項工程。新的建設有幾個重要的特點：使用風能和太陽能、不靠機械設備、利用自然通風和日照的冷暖系統，還有用混凝土跑道取代柏油跑道，因為柏油在生產過程中的碳足跡比較大。加拉巴哥群島在 2007 年列入環境「危險名單」，這項新建設來得正是時候。

像加拉巴哥群島、復活節島和大溪地這些太平洋島嶼，經濟幾乎完全靠觀光帶動。然而，有些人認為這是「無法永續的發展模式」。從 1990 年到 2006 年，到加拉巴哥群島的遊客人數增加了 250% 以上，而從 2001 年到 2006 年，飛往當地的商業航班也增加了 193%。這些增加讓島上的資源和環境承受很大的壓力。其中，航空旅行尤其讓人詬病，因為它耗盡自然資源，又造成環境破壞。因此，大家正努力減少觀光業對環境的衝擊，機場綠化只是其中一項嘗試。

title: 牛隻對地磁場的感知能力研究（Study on Cattle's Perception of Earth's Magnetic Fields）
paras: According to popular folklore, many animals are smarter than they appear. Dogs bark before earthquakes; cattle predict rainfall by sitting on the ground. But cattle may have another hidden talent in telling which way is north.

Small animals such as mole rats living underground are known for the use of magnetism to navigate. Dr. Begall and her colleagues wanted to know whether larger mammals also have the ability to perceive magnetic fields. They investigated this possibility by studying images of thousands of cattle captured on Google Earth, a website that stitches together satellite photographs to produce an image of the Earth’s surface.

Grazing animals are known to orient themselves in a way that minimizes wind chill from the north and maximizes the warmth of the sun when they are cold. The researchers therefore had to study a lot of cows grazing in lots of different places at different times of day, in order to average out these factors and see whether cattle could act like compass needles.

The researchers concluded that cattle do generally orient themselves in a north-south direction. This north-south preference has also been noted in flies, termites and honeybees. But unfortunately, even the high resolution of Google Earth is not powerful enough to tell which end of the cow is its head, and which its tail. The researchers were therefore unable to answer their research questions of whether cattle prefer to look north or south, and whether that differs in the northern and southern hemispheres.
accuracyRateSource: 大考中心 98 學年度學科能力測驗統計圖表：英文科答對率及鑑別指數表

outline: (According to popular folklore) 開篇引入民間傳說，(But cattle may have another hidden talent) 並提出牛可能還有分辨方向的隱藏能力。
(wanted to know whether) 引出研究目的：Dr. Begall 團隊想知道大型哺乳動物是否也有感知地磁場的能力，(They investigated this possibility by studying) 並說明研究方法。
(The researchers therefore had to study) 闡述研究過程的複雜性：需要大量不同時間、地點的牛隻圖片來排除環境因素。
(The researchers concluded that) 提出研究結論：牛隻普遍傾向南北方向。
(But unfortunately) 指出研究的局限性：Google Earth 解析度不足以判斷牛頭牛尾方向，(were therefore unable to answer) 故無法確定偏好南北向或南北半球差異。

zh: 根據民間流傳的說法，很多動物比牠們看起來還要聰明。狗會在地震前吠叫；牛坐在地上，就是預告要下雨了。不過，牛可能還有另一項隱藏的本領：分辨哪個方向是北方。
大家都知道，像鼴鼠這類住在地底下的小動物，會利用磁性來辨認方向。Begall 博士和她的同事想知道，比較大的哺乳動物是不是也能感知磁場。他們研究了 Google Earth 上拍到的幾千頭牛的影像，來探究這個可能性。Google Earth 是一個把衛星照片拼接起來、呈現地球表面影像的網站。
大家知道，吃草的動物覺得冷的時候，站的方向會盡量減少北邊吹來的冷風，並盡量多曬一點太陽。因此研究人員必須研究在許多不同地方、一天裡不同時間吃草的大量牛隻，把這些因素平均掉，才能看出牛是不是能像指南針的指針一樣。
研究人員的結論是，牛確實大致朝南北方向站。蒼蠅、白蟻和蜜蜂身上也觀察到這種偏好南北方向的現象。可惜的是，即使 Google Earth 的解析度很高，還是不足以分辨牛的哪一端是頭、哪一端是尾巴。所以研究人員沒辦法回答他們的研究問題：牛比較喜歡面向北方還是南方？在北半球和南半球是不是不一樣？

title: 父母如何幫助孩子養成健康飲食習慣（How Parents Can Help Children Develop Healthy Eating Habits）
paras: Children normally have a distrust of new foods. But it’s the parents’ job to serve a variety of foods and expose their children to healthy dieting habits.

Some simple strategies can help even the pickiest eater learn to like a more varied diet. First of all, you don’t have to send children out of the kitchen. With hot stoves, boiling water and sharp knives at hand, it is understandable that parents don’t want children in the kitchen when they’re making dinner. But studies suggest that involving children in meal preparation is an important first step in getting them to try new foods. In one study, nearly 600 children from kindergarten to sixth grade took part in a nutrition curriculum intended to get them to eat more vegetables and whole grains. The researchers found that children who had cooked their own foods were more likely to eat those foods in the cafeteria than children who had not. Kids don’t usually like radishes, but if kids cut them up and put them in the salad, they will love the dish.

Another strategy is not to diet in front of your children. Kids are tuned into their parents’ eating preferences and are far more likely to try foods if they see their mother or father eating them. Given this powerful effect, parents who are trying to lose weight should be careful of how their dieting habits can influence a child’s perceptions about food and healthful eating. In one study of 5-year-old girls about dieting, one child noted that dieting involved drinking chocolate milkshakes, because her mother was using Slim-Fast drinks. Another child said dieting meant “you fix food but you don’t eat it.” By exposing young children to erratic dieting habits, parents may be putting them at risk for eating disorders.

zh: 孩子對新的食物通常抱著不信任的態度。但是準備各種食物、讓孩子接觸健康的飲食習慣，是父母的責任。

有一些簡單的策略，連最挑食的孩子都能慢慢喜歡更多樣的飲食。首先，你不必把孩子趕出廚房。廚房裡有熱騰騰的爐子、滾燙的開水和鋒利的刀子，父母做晚餐時不想讓孩子待在廚房，是可以理解的。不過研究顯示，讓孩子參與準備餐點，是讓他們嘗試新食物重要的第一步。在一項研究中，將近 600 名從幼稚園到六年級的孩子參加了一套營養課程，目的是讓他們多吃蔬菜和全穀類。研究人員發現，自己做過菜的孩子，在學校餐廳吃這些食物的可能性，比沒做過的孩子高。孩子通常不喜歡蘿蔔，但是如果讓他們自己把蘿蔔切好放進沙拉裡，他們就會愛上這道菜。

另一個策略是不要在孩子面前節食。孩子很注意父母喜歡吃什麼，如果看到爸爸或媽媽吃某種食物，他們願意嘗試的可能性就高得多。既然影響這麼大，正在減肥的父母就應該留意，自己的節食習慣會怎麼影響孩子對食物和健康飲食的看法。在一項以 5 歲女孩為對象、關於節食的研究中，有個孩子說節食就是喝巧克力奶昔，因為她媽媽在喝 Slim-Fast 飲品。另一個孩子說，節食的意思是「你做了飯，可是不吃」。父母讓年幼的孩子接觸這些反覆無常的節食習慣，可能會讓孩子面臨飲食失調的風險。

title: 吼猴的行為與地域性（Howler Monkeys' Behavior and Territoriality）
paras: Howler monkeys are named for the long loud cries, or howls, that they make every day. They are the loudest land animal and their howls can be heard three miles away through dense forests. Male howler monkeys use their loud voices to fight for food, mates, or territory. Everyone starts and ends the day by howling to check out where their nearest competitors are.

Interestingly, when there are few howler monkeys in an area, the howling routine takes on a different pattern. In Belize, where howler monkeys were newly reintroduced into a wildlife sanctuary, the howler monkeys were heard only a few times a week rather than every day. Apparently, with plenty of space and no other howler monkeys around, there was no need to check on the whereabouts of their competitors. At the sanctuary, keepers now use recorded howler sounds from a distance so that the monkeys feel the need to make the territorial calls as they would do in the wild. In the future when the population grows, there will be no need for the recording because the howler monkeys will have more reason to check in with the neighbors to define their own territories.

outline: 介紹吼猴的名稱由來與其巨大聲量，說明公猴利用叫聲爭奪食物、配偶和地盤。
(Interestingly) 提出有趣現象：當吼猴數量稀少時，嚎叫模式會改變。
(Apparently) 解釋原因：在貝里斯的猴群因空間充足且無競爭者，無需頻繁嚎叫。
管理員現使用錄音來模擬吼叫聲，(so that) 以便猴子感受壓力而發出地域性叫聲。
(In the future) 展望未來：當猴群數量增長，將不再需要錄音，(because) 因為牠們會有更多理由與鄰居劃分地盤。

zh: 吼猴得名於牠們每天發出的長而響亮的叫聲，也就是吼聲。吼猴是陸地上叫聲最大的動物，吼聲穿過茂密的森林，三英里外都聽得到。公吼猴用宏亮的聲音爭奪食物、配偶或地盤。每一隻吼猴都用吼叫開始和結束一天，藉此查看離自己最近的競爭者在哪裡。

有趣的是，一個地區的吼猴很少的時候，每天吼叫的習慣會變成另一種模式。貝里斯有一處野生動物保護區最近重新引進吼猴，那裡的吼猴一週只吼叫幾次，而不是每天都叫。看來空間充足、附近又沒有其他吼猴，牠們就沒有必要查看競爭者在哪裡。現在保護區的管理員會從遠處播放吼猴叫聲的錄音，讓猴子覺得需要像在野外一樣，發出宣示地盤的叫聲。將來吼猴數量增加，就不需要錄音了，因為吼猴會有更多理由和鄰居互相確認，劃定自己的地盤。

title: 冰河國家公園道路的建設與公園合作（Glacier National Park Road Construction and Park Collaboration）
paras: After the creation of the Glacier National Park in Montana, the growing number of park visitors increased the need for roads. Eventually, the demand for a road across the mountains led to the building of the Going-to-the-Sun Road.

The construction of the Going-to-the-Sun Road was a huge task. After 11 years of work, the final section of the road was completed in 1932. The road is considered an engineering feat. Even today, visitors to the park marvel at how such a road could have been built. It is one of the most scenic roads in North America. The construction of the road has changed the way visitors experience the Glacier National Park. Visitors now can drive over sections of the park that previously took days of horseback riding to see.

Just across the border, in Canada, is the Waterton Lakes National Park. In 1931, members of the Rotary Clubs of Alberta and Montana suggested joining the two parks as a symbol of peace and friendship between the two countries. In 1932, the United States and Canadian governments renamed the parks the Waterton-Glacier International Peace Park, the world’s first. More recently, the parks have received several international honors. They were named as a World Heritage Site in 1995. This international recognition highlights the importance of this area, not just to the United States and Canada, but to the entire world.

zh: 蒙大拿州的冰河國家公園成立以後，遊客越來越多，對道路的需求也增加了。後來大家需要一條翻越山脈的道路，促成了「奔向太陽之路」的興建。
興建奔向太陽之路是一項浩大的工程。經過 11 年的施工，最後一段路在 1932 年完工。這條路公認是一項工程壯舉。直到今天，來公園的遊客仍然驚嘆這樣一條路是怎麼蓋起來的。這是北美洲風景最優美的道路之一。這條路改變了遊客體驗冰河國家公園的方式：公園裡有些地方，以前要騎好幾天的馬才看得到，現在遊客開車就能經過。
越過邊界，加拿大那一邊是華特頓湖國家公園。1931 年，亞伯達省和蒙大拿州的扶輪社成員提議把兩座公園結合起來，象徵兩國之間的和平與友誼。1932 年，美國和加拿大政府把這兩座公園重新命名為華特頓冰河國際和平公園，這是世界上第一座國際和平公園。近年來，這兩座公園獲得了幾項國際榮譽，1995 年列為世界遺產。這項國際肯定凸顯出這個地區不只對美國和加拿大重要，對全世界都很重要。

title: 冰雕藝術的挑戰與應用（Challenges and Applications of Ice Sculpting）
paras: Ice sculpting is a difficult process. First, ice must be carefully selected so that it is suitable for sculpting. Its ideal material is pure, clean water with high clarity. It should also have the minimum amount of air bubbles. Perfectly clear ice blocks weighing 140 kg and measuring 100 cm × 50 cm × 25 cm are available from the Clinebell Company in Colorado. Much larger clear blocks are produced in Europe and Canada or harvested from a frozen river in Sweden. These large ice blocks are used for large ice sculpting events and for building ice hotels.

Another difficulty in the process of ice sculpting is time control. The temperature of the environment affects how quickly the piece must be completed to avoid the effects of melting. If the sculpting does not take place in a cold environment, then the sculptor must work quickly to finish his piece. The tools used for sculpting also affect when the task can be accomplished. Some sculptures can be completed in as little as ten minutes if power tools are used. Ice sculptors also use razor-sharp chisels that are specifically designed for cutting ice. The best ice chisels are made in Japan, a country that, along with China, has a long tradition of magnificent ice sculptures.

Ice sculptures are used as decorations in some cuisines, especially in Asia. When holding a dinner party, some large restaurants or hotels will use an ice sculpture to decorate the table. For example, in a wedding banquet it is common to see a pair of ice-sculpted swans that represent the union of the new couple.

(Another difficulty) 闡述冰雕的第二個難點：時間控制，環境溫度影響融化速度，(If … then) 若不在寒冷環境，雕塑家必須快速完成作品。
(The tools used … also affect) 提及工具對完成時間的影響，(Some sculptures can be completed in as little as … if) 使用電動工具可快速完成，並介紹日本的冰雕鑿子與傳統。

zh: 冰雕是一個困難的過程。首先，冰塊必須仔細挑選，才適合雕刻。理想的材料是純淨、乾淨、透明度高的水，氣泡也要越少越好。科羅拉多州的 Clinebell 公司供應完全透明的冰塊，每塊重 140 公斤，尺寸是 100 公分 × 50 公分 × 25 公分。更大的透明冰塊則在歐洲和加拿大生產，或是從瑞典一條結冰的河上採集。這些大冰塊用在大型冰雕活動，也用來蓋冰旅館。
冰雕過程中的另一個困難是控制時間。環境的溫度會影響作品必須多快完成，才不會融化。如果不是在寒冷的環境裡雕刻，雕刻師就必須加快動作，才能完成作品。雕刻用的工具也會影響多久能完成。如果使用電動工具，有些作品只要十分鐘就能完成。冰雕師也會使用專門用來切冰、像剃刀一樣鋒利的鑿子。最好的冰鑿是日本製的；日本和中國一樣，都有製作壯觀冰雕的悠久傳統。
在某些料理中，冰雕用來當作裝飾，在亞洲尤其如此。舉辦晚宴時，有些大型餐廳或飯店會用冰雕裝飾餐桌。例如在婚宴上，常常可以看到一對冰雕的天鵝，代表新人的結合。

title: 疼痛的心理與生理元素（Physical and Psychological Elements of Pain）
paras: If you touch your finger to a hot stove, you know it’s going to hurt. However, if you convince yourself beforehand that the pain won’t be so bad, you might not suffer as much. According to a recent study, the part of your brain that reacts to severe pain is largely the same part that reacts to expectation of pain.

Researchers in this study worked with 10 volunteers, ages 24 to 46. Each volunteer wore a device that gave out 20-second-long pulses of heat to the right leg. There were three levels of heat, producing mild, moderate, or strong pain. During training, the volunteers would first hear a tone, followed by a period of silence, and then feel a heat pulse. They then learned to associate the length of the silent pause with the intensity of the upcoming heat pulse. The longer the pause, the stronger the heat pulse would be, causing more severe pain.

A day or two later, the real experiment began. The researchers found that the parts of the brain involved in learning, memory, emotion, and touch became more active as the volunteers expected higher levels of pain. These were mainly the same areas that became active when participants actually felt pain. Interestingly, when the volunteers expected only mild or moderate pain but experienced severe pain, they reported feeling 28 percent less pain than when they expected severe pain and actually got it.

The new study emphasizes that pain has both physical and psychological elements. Understanding how pain works in the mind and brain could eventually give doctors tools for helping people cope with painful medical treatments.
accuracyRateSource: 大考中心 97 學年度學科能力測驗統計圖表：英文科答對率及鑑別指數表

outline: 提出疼痛的普遍經驗，(However) 但指出若事先說服自己疼痛不那麼劇烈，感受可能減輕；(According to a recent study) 最新研究發現，大腦對預期疼痛的反應與實際疼痛的反應區域相似。
描述研究設計：10 位志願者參與實驗，透過不同長度的靜默期預期不同強度的熱脈衝。
(The researchers found that) 研究結果：預期越高疼痛，大腦中涉及學習、記憶、情感和觸摸的區域越活躍，且與實際疼痛區域重疊。
(Interestingly) 驚人發現：當預期輕度或中度疼痛卻遇到劇痛時，實際感受到的疼痛比預期劇痛時減少 28%。
(The new study emphasizes that) 總結疼痛同時有生理和心理的成分，(could eventually give doctors tools) 了解疼痛怎麼運作，未來可能幫助醫生讓病人更能面對會痛的治療。

zh: 如果你用手指碰到熱爐子，你知道會痛。然而，如果你事先說服自己不會那麼痛，你可能就不會那麼難受。根據最近的一項研究，大腦裡對劇痛起反應的部位，和對預期疼痛起反應的部位，大致是同一個。
這項研究的研究人員找了 10 位志願者，年齡從 24 到 46 歲。每位志願者都戴著一個裝置，裝置會對右腿發出每次 20 秒的熱脈衝。熱度分三個等級，分別造成輕微、中度或強烈的疼痛。訓練期間，志願者會先聽到一個聲音，接著是一段靜默，然後感覺到熱脈衝。他們因此學會把靜默停頓的長短，和接下來熱脈衝的強度聯想在一起：停頓越長，熱脈衝就越強，造成的疼痛也越劇烈。
一兩天後，正式的實驗開始了。研究人員發現，志願者預期的疼痛越強，大腦裡和學習、記憶、情緒、觸覺有關的部位就越活躍。這些部位和參與者真的感覺到疼痛時活躍的部位，大致相同。有意思的是，志願者如果預期的只是輕微或中度的疼痛，實際上卻感受到劇痛，他們說感覺到的疼痛，比預期劇痛而真的遇到劇痛時少了 28%。
這項新研究強調，疼痛同時有生理和心理的成分。了解疼痛在心智和大腦中怎麼運作，最後可能讓醫生有工具，幫助病人面對會痛的醫療處置。

title: 萬聖節糖果與牙齒健康（Halloween Candies and Dental Health）
paras: Most American kids love Halloween treats, but a bucket of Halloween candy can be a dentist’s nightmare. Some parents try to get rid of half of the candy after their children go to bed, but dentists say parents also need to separate the good kinds of treats from the bad.

It is not exactly what a child eats that truly matters, but how much time it stays in his mouth. According to pediatric dentist Dr. Kaneta Lott, the most damaging stuff is something that is sticky or very hard and thus stays in the mouth for a long time. This is because we all have bacteria in our mouths. When we eat, the bacteria take our food as their food and produce an acid that destroys the surface of the teeth, causing cavities to form. The longer the food stays in the mouth, the more likely cavities will develop. Therefore, potato chips are worse than candy because they get stuck between teeth. For the same reason, raisins and crackers are not the best choice. Hard candies take a long time to consume and are also a bad choice for Halloween treats.

If children really love candy, dentists recommend that they eat chocolate instead. Unlike hard candies, chocolate dissolves quickly in the mouth. Besides, chocolate contains tannins, which help to kill some of the bacteria in the mouth. But no matter what a child eats, brushing after each meal is still the best way to fight cavities.
accuracyRateSource: 大考中心 96 學年度學科能力測驗統計圖表：英文科答對率及鑑別指數表

outline: 提出問題：萬聖節糖果是牙醫的惡夢，即使家長處理掉部分糖果，仍需分辨好壞。
(According to) 說明最重要的是食物在口中停留的時間，(This is because) 因為細菌會產生酸性物質破壞牙齒，造成蛀牙。
(Therefore) 分析薯片比糖果更糟，(For the same reason) 葡萄乾和餅乾也不是好選擇，硬糖更是糟糕。
(Unlike) 建議巧克力是更好的選擇，因為它溶解快，(Besides) 且含有單寧酸有助於殺菌。
(But no matter what) 總結無論吃什麼，飯後刷牙仍是預防蛀牙的最佳方式。

zh: 大多數美國孩子都喜歡萬聖節的糖果，但是一整桶萬聖節糖果，可能是牙醫的惡夢。有些父母會在孩子上床以後，把一半的糖果處理掉；不過牙醫說，父母還要把好的零食和不好的零食分開。

真正要緊的不完全是孩子吃了什麼，而是食物在嘴裡停留多久。兒童牙醫 Kaneta Lott 醫師說，傷害最大的是黏黏的或很硬的東西，因為這些東西會在嘴裡停留很久。原因是每個人的嘴裡都有細菌。我們吃東西的時候，細菌也把我們的食物當成牠們的食物，並產生一種會破壞牙齒表面的酸，造成蛀牙。食物在嘴裡停留越久，就越可能蛀牙。所以洋芋片比糖果更糟，因為洋芋片會卡在牙縫裡。同樣的道理，葡萄乾和餅乾也不是最好的選擇。硬糖要吃很久，也不適合當萬聖節的零食。
如果孩子真的很愛吃糖，牙醫建議改吃巧克力。巧克力和硬糖不一樣，在嘴裡很快就會溶化。而且巧克力含有單寧酸，能幫忙殺死嘴裡的一些細菌。不過，不管孩子吃什麼，每餐飯後刷牙仍然是對抗蛀牙最好的方法。
