title: 語言學家的錄音詭計（The Linguist's Recording Trick）
paras: A linguist is always listening, never off-duty. Once I invited a group of friends round to my house, telling them that I was going to record their speech. I said I was interested in their regional accents, and that it would take only a few minutes. Thus, on one evening, three people turned up at my house and were shown into my front room. When they saw the room they were a bit alarmed, for it was laid out as a studio. In front of each easy chair there was a microphone at head height, with wires leading to a tape-recorder in the middle of the floor. They sat down, rather nervously, and I explained that all I wanted was for them to count from one to twenty. Then we could relax and have a drink.

I turned on the tape-recorder and each in turn solemnly counted from one to twenty in their best accent. When it was over, I turned the tape-recorder off and brought round the drinks. I was sternly criticized for having such an idiotic job, and for the rest of the evening there was general jolly conversation—spoilt only by the fact that I had to take a telephone call in another room, which unfortunately lasted some time.

Or at least that was how it would appear. For, of course, the microphones were not connected to the tape-recorder in the middle of the room at all but to another one, which was turning happily away in the kitchen. The participants, having seen the visible tape-recorder turned off, paid no more attention to the microphones which stayed in front of their chairs, only a few inches from their mouths, thus giving excellent sound quality. And my lengthy absence meant that I was able to obtain as natural a piece of conversation as it would be possible to find.

I should add, perhaps, that I did tell my friends what had happened to them, after the event was over, and gave them the option of destroying the tape. None of them wanted to—though for some years afterwards I was left in no doubt that I was morally obliged to them, in the sense that it always seemed to be my round when it came to the buying of drinks. Linguistic research can be a very expensive business.

outline: (A linguist is always listening, never off-duty) 語言學家隨時都在聽別人說話；(Once) 作者邀朋友來家裡錄音，謊稱只想錄他們的地方口音，幾分鐘就好。
(Thus, on one evening … When they saw the room) 朋友看到客廳佈置得像錄音室，有點不安；作者說只要他們從一數到二十，(Then we could relax) 之後就能放鬆喝酒。
(I turned on the tape-recorder) 朋友數完數，作者關掉錄音機、端出飲料，朋友笑他的工作很蠢；(I had to take a telephone call in another room) 後來作者去另一個房間接電話，離開了好一陣子。
(Or at least that was how it would appear. For, of course) 其實麥克風接的是廚房裡的另一台錄音機，朋友以為錄音結束，不再注意眼前的麥克風，(thus giving excellent sound quality) 錄音品質極佳；(my lengthy absence meant that) 作者藉故離開，錄到了最自然的對話。
(I should add) 作者事後說出真相，讓朋友選擇要不要銷毀錄音帶，結果沒有人要銷毀；(though for some years afterwards) 不過之後好幾年，每次輪到買酒的總是作者，(Linguistic research can be a very expensive business) 語言學研究的代價可不小。

zh: 語言學家隨時都在聽，從來不下班。有一次，我邀了一群朋友到家裡來，告訴他們我要錄下他們說話的聲音。我說我對他們各地的口音很有興趣，而且只要幾分鐘就好。就這樣，某天晚上有三個人來到我家，我帶他們進了客廳。他們看到客廳的樣子有點吃驚，因為客廳布置得像錄音室一樣。每張安樂椅前面都有一支麥克風，高度和頭部一樣，電線連到地板中間的一台錄音機。他們坐了下來，相當緊張；我向他們解釋，我只要他們從一數到二十，數完我們就可以放鬆一下，喝杯酒。
我打開錄音機，他們輪流拿出最標準的口音，一本正經地從一數到二十。數完以後，我關掉錄音機，端上飲料。他們狠狠地批評我，說我的工作真是蠢透了。那天晚上接下來的時間，大家愉快地閒聊，唯一掃興的是，我得到另一個房間接一通電話，可惜那通電話講了好一陣子。
至少表面上看起來是這樣。因為那些麥克風當然根本沒有接到房間中間那台錄音機，而是接到另一台錄音機，那台錄音機正在廚房裡愉快地轉個不停。參與的人看到那台看得見的錄音機已經關掉，就不再注意擺在椅子前面的麥克風了；麥克風離他們的嘴巴只有幾英寸，錄下來的音質好極了。而我離開了很長一段時間，錄到的對話也就自然得不能再自然了。
也許我應該補充一下：事後我確實告訴朋友們他們遇到了什麼事，也讓他們選擇要不要銷毀錄音帶。沒有人要銷毀；不過，接下來好幾年，朋友們讓我很清楚自己在道義上欠了他們一份情，具體來說，就是每次要買酒的時候，好像總是輪到我請客。語言學的研究可是很花錢的。

title: 蕭伯納與邱吉爾的機智對話（Shaw and Churchill's Witty Exchange）
paras: George Bernard Shaw and Winston Churchill apparently disliked each other. It is said that the playwright once sent Churchill two tickets for the opening night of one of his plays, together with a card, which said, “Bring a friend (if you have one).”

Churchill, however, managed to get the better of this exchange. He returned the tickets, enclosing a note, which said, “I shall be busy that evening. Please send me two tickets for the second night (if there is one).”
There is no record of whether Shaw ever sent the tickets.

title: 寫作目的與文章類型（Purposes of Writing and Text Types）
paras: Authors write for many reasons. Often they write about real or make-believe people, places, or events that may be funny, sad, or scary. Sometimes authors write about these things to entertain readers. Authors also write about these things to inform by giving facts or ideas.
The following two paragraphs are examples of these two kinds.

(1) When he finished with unpacking, Nelson carried all the empty boxes down the hallway. On his way to the dump, the bell rang. He needed to hurry. He had no time to go to the dump. Then, he stopped at Adam Joshua’s office, which happened to be unlocked, and walked away joyfully. Later in the afternoon, Nelson came to Adam’s office with Peter for their biology project. The empty boxes and many other things fell all over them the minute he opened the door. “Adam Joshua!” yelled Nelson, pushing away a basketball and shaking a toy frog off his foot. “This is no way to treat a friend!”

(2) Where the land meets the sea we find seashells. There are many different kinds of shells. They can be round like the moon, long like a jackknife, or shaped like boxes, fans, or tops. The shells we find are usually empty, but once there were soft bodies inside. Animals with hard shells outside and soft bodies inside are called mollusks.

(1) Nelson 拆完行李以後，把所有空箱子搬到走廊上。在他要把箱子拿去垃圾場的路上，鈴聲響了，他得趕快。他沒時間去垃圾場了，就在 Adam Joshua 的辦公室停了下來（那間辦公室剛好沒鎖），然後開開心心地走了。那天下午稍晚，Nelson 和 Peter 一起到 Adam 的辦公室做生物科的專題。Nelson 一打開門，空箱子和許多其他東西就掉下來，砸在他們身上。「Adam Joshua！」Nelson 一邊推開一顆籃球、把一隻玩具青蛙從腳上甩掉，一邊大叫：「怎麼可以這樣對待朋友！」
(2) 在陸地和海洋交界的地方，我們可以找到貝殼。貝殼有很多不同的種類：有的圓得像月亮，有的長得像摺疊刀，有的形狀像盒子、扇子或陀螺。我們找到的貝殼通常是空的，不過裡面曾經有柔軟的身體。外面有硬殼、裡面是柔軟身體的動物，稱為軟體動物。

title: 考艾島的自然風光與旅遊特色（Kauai Island's Natural Scenery and Tourism）
paras: Kauai, the oldest of the main Hawaiian Islands, has some of the state’s most stunning scenery. Rivers and streams flow slowly through jungles of shaded greens. The breathtaking 4,000-foot cliffs of Na Pali Coast rise grandly from the sea. Waimea Canyon, called the "Grand Canyon of the Pacific" by Mark Twain, cuts a deep gash through the rugged central mountains.

Rising more than 5,000 feet, Mt. Waialeale stands at the center of the nearly round island. This extinct volcano is considered the wettest spot on earth, with almost 500 inches of rainfall each year. Yet this amount of rain is surprisingly localized. Just a few miles west, there’s a dry region that receives a mere 6 inches of rain annually.
The island continues to recover from its 1992 visit from Iniki, the most powerful hurricane to hit Hawaii this century. A few hotels are still being rebuilt, but Kauai remains as beautiful as ever.

Kauai is not for people who thrive on crowds or nightlife. While it does have its share of resort hotels, shopping centers and good restaurants, and a smattering of museums, art galleries and night spots, its main attractions lie outdoors. Hiking, camping, and scuba diving are excellent on the island.

outline: 介紹考艾島是夏威夷群島中最古老的島嶼，擁有令人驚嘆的自然風光。
描述島上的河流、熱帶叢林、壯麗的納帕利海岸懸崖，以及有「太平洋大峽谷」之稱的威美亞峽谷。
考艾島中央的懷亞萊阿萊山是一座死火山，公認是地球上最潮濕的地方，(Yet this amount of rain is surprisingly localized) 不過雨量集中在局部，往西幾英里就是乾燥地區。
說明考艾島正從 1992 年颶風伊尼基的破壞中恢復，(but) 雖有飯店重建，但仍美麗如昔。
(While) 考艾島不適合喜歡喧囂或夜生活的人，(its main attractions lie outdoors) 主要吸引力在於戶外活動（如健行、露營、水肺潛水）。

zh: 考艾島是夏威夷各主要島嶼中最古老的一座，有夏威夷州幾處最令人驚嘆的景色。河流和溪水緩緩流過一片片綠蔭濃密的叢林。納帕利海岸高 4,000 英尺、令人屏息的懸崖，從海面雄偉地拔地而起。威美亞峽谷，馬克吐溫稱它為「太平洋大峽谷」，在崎嶇的中央山區劃出一道深深的切口。
懷亞萊阿萊山高 5,000 多英尺，矗立在這座近乎圓形的島嶼中央。一般認為這座死火山是地球上最潮濕的地方，每年降雨量將近 500 英寸。然而，這麼多的雨，卻出乎意料地集中在小範圍裡。往西才幾英里，就有一個乾燥地區，一年的雨量只有 6 英寸。
1992 年伊尼基颶風來襲，這是本世紀侵襲夏威夷最強的颶風，考艾島到現在還在復原。有幾家飯店仍在重建，不過考艾島依然和以前一樣美麗。
喜歡熱鬧人潮或夜生活的人，不適合來考艾島。島上雖然也有一些度假飯店、購物中心和好餐廳，還有零星幾間博物館、藝廊和夜間娛樂場所，但是主要的吸引力在戶外。在島上健行、露營和水肺潛水都非常棒。

ms.t: Kauai, the oldest of the main Hawaiian Islands, has some of the state’s most stunning scenery.
The island continues to recover from its 1992 visit from Iniki, the most powerful hurricane to hit Hawaii this century.
While it does have its share of resort hotels, shopping centers and good restaurants, and a smattering of museums, art galleries and night spots, its main attractions lie outdoors.

title: 分解者在生態循環中的作用（The Role of Decomposers in Ecological Cycles）
paras: All living things die eventually. In ecological terms, the chemicals of living things are borrowed from the Earth, and at death they return. All the material that every animal, from the smallest fly to the largest elephant, takes in as food also returns to the Earth, as waste matter. The dead material and waste matter form the diet of a group of living organisms called decomposers. They include a range of bacteria, fungi, and small animals that break down nature’s wastes into ever smaller pieces until all the chemicals are released into the air, the soil, and the water, making them available to other living things. Without the carbon dioxide released from the process, all plant life would die out. Without the oxygen that plants give out, and without the food that they supply, life would grind to a halt and all animals would starve. The decomposers are a vital link in the natural cycle of life and death.

死物質和廢物是分解者的食物，(They include) 分解者（細菌、真菌、小動物）將其分解成更小物質。
(until) 直到所有化學物質釋放到空氣、土壤和水中，供其他生物使用。
(Without) 沒有分解過程釋放的二氧化碳，植物將滅絕；沒有植物提供的氧氣和食物，所有生命將停滯，(The decomposers are a vital link) 分解者是生命與死亡自然循環中的關鍵環節。

zh: 所有生物最後都會死。用生態學的說法，生物身上的化學物質是向地球借來的，死的時候就還回去。每一種動物，從最小的蒼蠅到最大的大象，吃下去當作食物的東西，最後也都會變成排泄物，回到地球。死去的生物和排泄物，是一群叫做分解者的生物的食物。分解者包括各種細菌、真菌和小動物，它們把大自然的廢物分解成愈來愈小的碎片，直到所有化學物質都釋放到空氣、土壤和水中，讓其他生物可以利用。要是沒有這個過程釋放出來的二氧化碳，所有植物都會滅絕。要是沒有植物釋放的氧氣、沒有植物提供的食物，生命就會停擺，所有動物都會餓死。分解者是大自然生死循環中不可或缺的一環。

title: 約翰·葛倫的凱旋遊行與美國太空計畫的態度轉變（John Glenn's Ticker-Tape Parades and Changing Attitudes to Space Program）
paras: New York, Nov. 17--In a swirl of confetti and shredded paper, John Glenn made his second trip through New York’s "Canyon of Heroes" in a parade Monday, saluting his return to space 36 years after he became America’s first man in orbit.

Glenn’s first ticker-tape parade on March 1, 1962, after his Mercury flight, is considered the largest ever in New York. An estimated 3,474 tons of confetti and ticker-tape rained down along a seven-mile route.

For his second parade, despite lunchtime crowds from Wall Street, the turnout Monday was sparse by New York standards and spectators along a route less than a mile long were surprisingly restrained. Police said Glenn’s parade was attended by 500,000 -- a figure that appeared generously inflated.

The 1962 celebration "was more enthusiastic -- a lot more people," said one spectator, who as a young newlywed attended Glenn’s first parade and came from her Brooklyn home again for Glenn’s second parade.
Another spectator said that too many Americans take the achievements of the space program for granted. "It’s become so everyday, so ordinary, nobody cares," he said.

Glenn began the day with decorating the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree. After that event, Glenn recalled the 1962 parade, saying, "It was just so enormous. I remember just a blizzard of paper. You could hardly even look up without getting something in your eye."
Glenn, who retires from the U.S. Senate next month, joins a list of individuals and sports teams honored with more than one ticker-tape parade.

zh: 紐約 11 月 17 日電：五彩碎紙和紙屑漫天飛舞，John Glenn 週一第二次參加紐約「英雄谷」的遊行，慶祝他成為美國第一位環繞地球軌道飛行的太空人 36 年以後，重返太空。
Glenn 第一次的紙花遊行，是在 1962 年 3 月 1 日他完成水星計畫的太空飛行之後，一般認為那是紐約有史以來規模最大的一次。估計有 3,474 噸的五彩碎紙和紙帶，沿著七英里長的路線紛紛落下。
第二次遊行雖然有華爾街午餐時間的人潮，週一出來看遊行的人以紐約的標準來說還是稀稀落落；路線不到一英里長，沿路的觀眾也出乎意料地平靜。警方說有 50 萬人參加 Glenn 的遊行，這個數字看來誇大了不少。
「1962 年那次比較熱烈，人多得多。」一位觀眾說。她剛結婚的時候參加過 Glenn 的第一次遊行，這次又從布魯克林的家趕來參加第二次。
另一位觀眾說，太多美國人把太空計畫的成就視為理所當然。「這件事已經變得太平常、太普通，沒有人在乎了。」他說。
Glenn 這一天先替洛克斐勒中心的聖誕樹裝飾。之後他回憶 1962 年的遊行時說：「那次的規模實在太大了。我記得紙片多得像暴風雪一樣，一抬頭，眼睛幾乎就會有東西掉進去。」
Glenn 下個月就要從美國參議院退休，他也成為少數獲得不只一次紙花遊行表揚的個人和運動隊伍之一。

title: 機器人擔任畢業典禮演講者（Robot as a Commencement Speaker）
paras: One of the most unusual graduation speakers of the 1983 commencement season was not a person at all. The speaker was Robot Redford, a robot who delivered the commencement address at a community college in suburban Maryland.

The speaker, carefully programmed, arrived on the stage under its own power and proceeded to tell the audience of 658 graduates, their families, and friends that they would have to learn to work with robots and technology to solve society’s problems. The robot described itself as an extension of a person to help humans increase the workload. Although this particular robot can be programmed to speak, the voice heard wasn’t that of the robot, because it was feared that the robot’s voice was not loud enough to carry throughout the hall. An amplified voice of a human was used instead, while the listeners watched the robot.

Robot Redford was followed by a person, William Bakaleinikoff, who spoke about the need for cooperation between people and technology. Mr. Bakaleinikoff’s experience with his topic included the fact that he had created Robot Redford and had provided the voice for the robot’s words to the graduates.

There was quite a bit of controversy over the choice of a robot as a commencement speaker. Some students thought it was insensitive and degrading to use a robot. Others thought the idea was clever and innovative.
“I’ll never forget this speech,” said one graduate. “You forget a political leader, but you won’t forget a robot.”

zh: 1983 年畢業典禮季最特別的畢業演講者之一，根本不是人。這位演講者是 Robot Redford，一個機器人，它在馬里蘭州郊區一所社區大學的畢業典禮上致詞。
這位演講者經過精心設定程式，靠自己的動力走上講台，接著告訴在場的 658 位畢業生和他們的家人、朋友，他們必須學會和機器人、科技合作，來解決社會的問題。機器人把自己形容成人的延伸，能幫助人類完成更多工作。雖然這個機器人可以設定程式說話，但大家聽到的並不是機器人的聲音，因為有人擔心機器人的聲音不夠大，沒辦法傳遍整個禮堂。所以改用擴音的人聲，觀眾則看著機器人。
接在 Robot Redford 後面演講的是一個人：William Bakaleinikoff，他談到人和科技需要合作。Bakaleinikoff 先生對這個題目的經驗包括：Robot Redford 就是他製造的，機器人對畢業生說的話，也是他配的音。
選機器人當畢業典禮的演講者，引起不少爭議。有些學生認為用機器人既不體貼，又有貶低人的意味。也有人認為這個主意很聰明、很有創意。
「我永遠不會忘記這場演講。」一位畢業生說：「政治領袖你會忘記，但機器人你不會忘記。」

title: 父親的夏季家庭學校（Father's Summer Home School）
paras: Summers with father were always enjoyable. Swimming, hiking, boating, fishing--the days were not long enough to contain all of our activities. There never seemed to be enough time to go to church, which disturbed some friends and relatives. Accused of neglecting this part of our education, my father still instituted a summer school for my brother and me. His summer course included ancient history, which Papa felt our schools neglected, and navigation, in which we first had a formal examination in the dining room, part of which consisted of tying several knots in a given time limit. Then we were each separately sent on what was grandly referred to as a cruise in my father’s 18-foot boat, spending the night on board, and loaded down, according to my mother, with enough food for a week. I remember that on my cruise I was required to formally plot our course, using the tide table, even though our goal was an island I could see quite clearly across the water in the distance.

title: 巴黎千禧年木製艾菲爾鐵塔計畫（Paris Millennium Wooden Eiffel Tower Project）
paras: PARIS, Dec. 9 -- Paris will be given a new Eiffel Tower--but made of wood--for the millennium, city mayor Jean Tiberi said Tuesday, presenting a program of celebration for the year 2,000 which would transform the “city of light” into the “capital of light.”
The new structure will be 200 meters high, 100 meters shorter than the cast-iron Eiffel Tower built 100 years ago.

It will be made of timber as an ecological symbol of “the right to a dignified life on a protected Earth,” said architects Normier, Henni and Lelievre, who were also responsible for the Europe section at the Seville exhibition.
The tower, of pinewood, will be built on eight pillars and will be topped with a flower of five metal petals of 700 square meters each.
The structure, to be erected in the redeveloped areas of the capital’s 13th district, will cost 250 million francs (US$42 million).
Tiberi also said that Paris would be placed under the sign of the lights of “culture and life” and “intelligence.”
“If, in 1900, Paris was consecrated the ‘city of light’, it will become the ‘capital of light’ for the millennium,” Tiberi said.

The mayor said new buildings would be illuminated, notably along the banks of the Seine, which would become a luminous strip, while Notre Dame Cathedral would be lit from the inside to show off its stained glass windows.

A laser clock would be installed on top of the Arc de Triomphe at the top of the Champs Elysees and three laser beams would pick out the hands showing the hours, minutes and seconds in the millennium countdown, Tiberi said.
A giant egg-timer will be set up in the Place de la Concorde and its sand will begin running after a solar eclipse scheduled on April 11, 1999.

zh: 巴黎 12 月 9 日電：巴黎市長 Jean Tiberi 週二表示，巴黎將有一座新的艾菲爾鐵塔，不過是木造的，用來迎接千禧年。他同時提出 2000 年的慶祝計畫，要把這座「光之城」變成「光之首都」。
新的建築高 200 公尺，比 100 年前建造的鑄鐵艾菲爾鐵塔矮 100 公尺。
建築師 Normier、Henni 和 Lelievre 說，這座塔用木材建造，是要作為生態的象徵，代表「在保護良好的地球上，享有尊嚴生活的權利」。這三位建築師也負責過塞維亞博覽會的歐洲區。
這座松木塔將建在八根柱子上，塔頂是一朵有五片金屬花瓣的花，每片花瓣 700 平方公尺。
這座建築將豎立在巴黎第 13 區重新開發的地區，造價 2.5 億法郎（4,200 萬美元）。
Tiberi 也說，巴黎將以「文化與生活」和「智慧」之光為主題。
「如果說 1900 年巴黎獲尊為『光之城』，那麼到了千禧年，巴黎將成為『光之首都』。」Tiberi 說。
市長說，新建築會打上燈光，特別是塞納河兩岸，塞納河將成為一條發光的帶子；聖母院則會從內部點燈，展示它的彩繪玻璃窗。
Tiberi 說，香榭麗舍大道頂端的凱旋門上方會裝設一座雷射時鐘，三道雷射光分別標出時針、分針和秒針，為千禧年倒數計時。
協和廣場將設置一座巨型沙漏，沙子會在預定 1999 年 4 月 11 日發生的日蝕之後開始流動。

ms.t: PARIS, Dec. 9 -- Paris will be given a new Eiffel Tower--but made of wood--for the millennium, city mayor Jean Tiberi said Tuesday, presenting a program of celebration for the year 2,000 which would transform the “city of light” into the “capital of light.”
The new structure will be 200 meters high, 100 meters shorter than the cast-iron Eiffel Tower built 100 years ago.

It will be made of timber as an ecological symbol of “the right to a dignified life on a protected Earth,” said architects Normier, Henni and Lelievre, who were also responsible for the Europe section at the Seville exhibition.
The tower, of pinewood, will be built on eight pillars and will be topped with a flower of five metal petals of 700 square meters each.
The structure, to be erected in the redeveloped areas of the capital’s 13th district, will cost 250 million francs (US$42 million).
Tiberi also said that Paris would be placed under the sign of the lights of “culture and life” and “intelligence.”
“If, in 1900, Paris was consecrated the ‘city of light’, it will become the ‘capital of light’ for the millennium,” Tiberi said.

The mayor said new buildings would be illuminated, notably along the banks of the Seine, which would become a luminous strip, while Notre Dame Cathedral would be lit from the inside to show off its stained glass windows.

A laser clock would be installed on top of the Arc de Triomphe at the top of the Champs Elysees and three laser beams would pick out the hands showing the hours, minutes and seconds in the millennium countdown, Tiberi said.
A giant egg-timer will be set up in the Place de la Concorde and its sand will begin running after a solar eclipse scheduled on April 11, 1999.

title: 木匠店的回收再分配計畫（The Carpenters' Shop: Recycle and Redistribution Project）
paras: I wonder how often your family has bought new furniture, curtains or kitchen equipment and then wondered how to dispose of the old items that still have quite a lot of life left in them.

It was in response to this situation that The Carpenters’ Shop was opened in the town of Walsall, Staffordshire. Run by a team of church volunteers, the shop will collect any surplus, good-quality items and store them until they can be redistributed to the people who are needing those particular things.
Many have been helped through the scheme, including single parents, disabled people and the elderly, and those who have lost all their household possessions through a disaster such as a house fire.
It’s an admirable project, and it is worth finding out if a similar one operates in your hometown. Participation costs the donor nothing and can make such a difference to others.

正是為了解決這種情況，斯塔福德郡的沃爾索爾鎮開了一家 The Carpenters’ Shop。這家店由一群教會志工經營，會收集任何多餘、品質良好的物品，存放起來，直到可以重新分送給正好需要這些東西的人。

title: Jack 的磁碟醫生服務（Jack's Disk Doctor Service）
paras: What can you do if you ‘lose’ the data from your disks? To find an expert, who would recover the lost information for you, is probably the easiest solution. Jack Olson is one of these experts. Jack and a few of his friends set up a company called “Jack’s Disk Doctor Service” in 1984. They work from home and give all the money they earn to charity. The fees are always the same, no matter how precious the data on the disk is. Some people, however, are so grateful that they send extra money to Jack or to the charities his company supports. One oil company offered him $2000 for his help and an architect even sent him a blank check.

It would be difficult to put a value on the things rescued by the Disk Doctor. There have been disks containing medical research, television scripts, manuscripts of whole books, a lawyer’s papers for a court case, and even Margaret Thatcher’s travel plan for a visit to eastern Europe. For this last case, Jack had to go in person to Thatcher's office ‘for security reasons’!

Disks are usually sent to the Disk Doctor by post, but sometimes people are in such a hurry that they cannot wait for the mail to come. For example, some radio scripts had to be rushed by taxi to Jack’s house because they were needed for broadcasting the next day. When the material has been recovered, the disk is returned to the sender with a diagnosis and a prescription for avoiding the problem in the future. One grateful client, an author, put a “thank you” to Jack in the front of his book. “Jack saved me from a heart attack,” he wrote. “But,” says Jack, “most people don’t take any notice of the doctor’s advice!”

title: 人際關係的建立與維繫（Building and Maintaining Relationships）
paras: Do you know the meaning of the word “relationship”? Here is an easy way of understanding it. Whenever two people come together, even for a brief moment, they exchange looks, feelings, thoughts, ideas, and energy. Their relationship is how they interact with each other. Everything that happens in the world happens through relationships. We human beings need to love and be loved, and this will come from our relationship with others. Accordingly, anyone who wishes to love and be loved will want to establish lasting relationships.

Here are a few tips to help us create enduring relationships. First, know our steps. The relationship between two people is like the art of dancing. Before we can dance with a partner, we need to be able to dance by ourselves. We need to feel the rhythm of the music, hear how it inspires us to move and learn our unique style of movement and expression. Second, trust. As the key building block for enduring relationships, trust is a bond that evolves as two persons get to know each other and experience safety in opening their hearts. Trust develops when we respect each other’s needs and develop a history of common experience and caring. Third, be intimate. While intimacy is often limited to the sexual bond, we can be intimate with many people without sexuality. That is, by relating heart to heart. We need to be seen and known by another person. In this way, intimacy enables us to thrive and grow. Lastly, treat relationship as an organism. A new relationship is like an embryo that requires time, care and attention to grow into whatever may evolve. In our proper relationship with others, we will be known and seen for who we are, and love will come out of the seeing and the knowing.

outline: (Here is an easy way of understanding it) 解釋「關係」的意義：兩人互動時的交流，世上所有的事情都透過關係發生。
人都需要愛人也需要別人愛，(Accordingly) 這份需要來自和他人的關係，所以我們想建立長久的關係。
(Here are a few tips) 提供建立持久關係的建議：(First) 認識自己，像跳舞需先獨自舞動。
(Second) 信任是基石，透過了解和安全感建立，(Third) 親密關係是心與心的連結，而不只是性。
(Lastly) 把關係看成有生命的東西，需要時間和關懷才會成長；(In our proper relationship with others) 在對的關係裡，別人看見並了解我們，愛也就隨之而來。

zh: 你知道「關係」這個詞的意思嗎？這裡有個簡單的理解方法。每當兩個人碰在一起，即使只有短短一下子，他們也會交換眼神、感受、思緒、想法和能量。他們的關係，就是他們彼此互動的方式。世界上發生的每一件事，都是透過關係發生的。我們人類需要愛人，也需要別人愛，而這份愛來自我們和他人的關係。因此，想要愛人、也想要別人愛的人，都會想建立長久的關係。

下面有幾個建議，幫助我們建立持久的關係。第一，熟悉自己的舞步。兩個人之間的關係就像跳舞的藝術。在能和舞伴一起跳舞以前，我們得先能自己跳。我們要感受音樂的節奏，聽聽音樂怎麼激勵我們舞動，學會屬於自己的獨特動作和表達方式。第二，信任。信任是建立持久關係最關鍵的基石；兩個人逐漸了解彼此，敞開心胸時覺得安心，這份連結就會隨之發展。我們尊重彼此的需要，累積共同的經驗和關懷，信任就會慢慢建立起來。第三，親密。一般人常把親密只當成性方面的連結，但是不涉及性，我們也可以和許多人很親密，也就是心與心的交流。我們需要另一個人看見我們、了解我們。這樣一來，親密讓我們茁壯成長。最後，把關係看成一個有機體。新的關係就像胚胎，需要時間、照顧和關注，才能長成它可能長成的樣子。在和他人適當的關係裡，別人會看見、了解我們真正的樣子，而愛就從這份看見和了解中產生。

title: 俄羅斯父子澎湖獲救記（Russian Father and Son Rescued in Penghu）
paras: Penghu, Nov.24—Two Russians, a father and a son, were rescued Saturday near the Penghu Islands off southwestern Taiwan after their sailboat broke down and began drifting.
Medvedev Vladimir, 43, and his son, Maxsine, 14, sailed from an unnamed eastern Russian seaport on August 18, to begin an ambitious around-the-world cruise.

Their voyage, down the coastline of northeastern mainland China, through the East China Sea, then down the Taiwan Strait and into the South China Sea, had been smooth until four days ago when the mainsail of their twin-mast sailboat “Kawasaki” was smashed by strong winds on the high seas.
The father-and-son team started the inboard engine. However, after less than two days, the engine broke down.
Near the “black ditch” of Penghu, battered by winds of up to 70 knots, the rear sail was torn into shreds. The rudder also stopped responding.

Surprised by the father and son’s “pale faces” and their battered vessel, the Penghu police and fishers in Paisha rescued them. Speaking only limited English, the Vladimirs spent five hours trying to explain their presence.
It is not immediately known whether the “Kawasaki” can be repaired on the fishing island of Penghu, or when the Vladimirs will be able to set off again and continue their around-the-world voyage.

zh: 澎湖 11 月 24 日電：兩名俄羅斯人，一對父子，帆船故障、開始漂流以後，週六在台灣西南外海的澎湖群島附近獲救。
43 歲的 Medvedev Vladimir 和 14 歲的兒子 Maxsine，8 月 18 日從俄羅斯東部一個未透露名稱的港口出航，展開一趟雄心勃勃的環球航行。
他們的航程先沿著中國大陸東北部的海岸線南下，穿過東海，再南下台灣海峽，進入南海。一路都很順利，直到四天前，強風在公海上打碎了他們那艘雙桅帆船「Kawasaki」的主帆。
這對父子發動了船上的引擎。可是不到兩天，引擎就故障了。
在澎湖的「黑水溝」附近，風速高達 70 節的強風猛烈吹打著帆船，後帆撕成了碎片，舵也失靈了。
澎湖的警察和白沙的漁民看到這對父子「臉色蒼白」、船隻破損不堪，都嚇了一跳，於是救起了他們。Vladimir 父子只會說一點英文，花了五個小時，才解釋清楚他們為什麼會出現在這裡。
「Kawasaki」能不能在澎湖這個漁業島嶼上修好，Vladimir 父子什麼時候能再出發、繼續環球航行，目前都還不知道。

title: 家書：恭賀 Tom 大學入學（Family Letter: Congratulating Tom on College Acceptance）
paras: Dear Tom,
It seems only yesterday that Jack and I were helping you learn your ABC's—and now you have finished high school and been accepted at Taipei University.

We are both very proud of you, Tom. We have followed your high-school career with joy and pleasure and know that your four years at college will be even more rewarding. A word of congratulation just doesn't seem enough, so I am sending you a gift that I'm sure you will find useful—an unabridged dictionary. Jack says you'll not only find it handy in your studies, but a great argument-saver when playing Scrabble with your friends.
Mom and Dad are coming here for a weekend next month. Please try to take a few days off and come to join us. We are looking forward to seeing you.

Love,
Sally

Tom，我們兩個都非常以你為榮。我們一路看著你念高中，又開心又欣慰，也知道你大學四年會過得更充實。只說一聲恭喜好像不夠，所以我要送你一份禮物，相信你一定用得上：一本未刪節的大辭典。Jack 說，這本辭典不但讀書時很好用，和朋友玩 Scrabble 拼字遊戲的時候，也是避免爭吵的好幫手。
爸爸媽媽下個月要來我們這裡過週末。請盡量空出幾天來和我們聚一聚。我們很期待見到你。

title: 外國人入境台灣的簽證規定（Visa Regulations for Foreigners Entering Taiwan）
paras: Generally speaking, all foreigners coming to Taiwan should apply for entry visas through the embassies or consulates of the Republic of China, or agencies authorized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

As of May 1, 1995, all nationals of the following 15 countries are exempted from securing visas for entry into the Republic of China: U.S.A., Japan, Canada, Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Holland, New Zealand, Australia, Austria, Germany, Britain, France, Spain, and Portugal. The maximum duration of stay is 14 days. Requirements for a 14-day non-visa entry are: passport good for at least six months, confirmed onward ticket within 14 days, no violation of law recorded.

If it is necessary to stay more than 14 days and less than 30 days, nationals of the specific countries holding a 14-day non-visa entry should in the meantime apply for a landing-visa with the authorized office in the CKS airport from the Bureau of Consular Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The landing-visa fee is NT$1,500.

title: 大腦兩半球與語言學習（Brain Hemispheres and Language Learning）
paras: The brain, which weighs less than 2.2 pounds, is perhaps the most complicated organ in our bodies. Although scientists have not been able to solve all the mysteries of this amazing organ, they have made some progress. They have found that certain parts of the brain are responsible for learning, memory, and language.

Recent studies indicate that the two halves of the brain—the right hemisphere and the left hemisphere — play extremely important roles in learning and communicating. The left hemisphere deals with rules, lists of information, and short-term memory. In contrast, the right hemisphere deals with feelings, colors, and long-term memory. Scientists recognize the importance of both hemispheres in the learning of all sorts, including language learning.

Scientists now relate left and right hemispheres to the way different individuals learn languages. They believe that some learners use one half of their brains more than the other half. Left-brained learners usually concentrate on memorizing rules and lists. They use logic, definition, and repetition to learn. Right-brained learners look for a general picture and concentrate on relating new information to what they already know. They use associations and intuition to learn. Most people fall into one of these types. If teachers know whether their students are left-brained or right-brained, they can help them learn better.
accuracyRateSource: 該屆逐題數據未公開

outline: 介紹大腦是複雜器官，科學家雖未解所有謎團，但已發現特定區域負責學習、記憶和語言。
(Recent studies indicate that) 最新研究指出大腦兩半球（左右腦）在學習和溝通中扮演極重要角色。
左腦負責規則、資訊列表和短期記憶，(In contrast) 右腦負責情感、色彩和長期記憶，兩者在語言學習中都重要。
(Scientists now relate) 科學家把左右腦和每個人學語言的方式連在一起，認為有些學習者偏用其中一邊：(Left-brained learners) 左腦型背規則和清單，靠邏輯、定義和反覆練習，(Right-brained learners) 右腦型先看整體，把新資訊和已知的連結起來，靠聯想和直覺。
(If teachers know) 若教師了解學生是左腦型或右腦型，(they can help them learn better) 便能協助他們更好地學習。

zh: 大腦重不到 2.2 磅，也許是我們身體裡最複雜的器官。科學家雖然還沒能解開這個神奇器官的所有謎團，但已經有一些進展。他們發現，大腦的某些部位負責學習、記憶和語言。
最近的研究指出，大腦的兩半，也就是右半球和左半球，在學習和溝通上扮演極為重要的角色。左半球處理規則、一連串的資訊和短期記憶。相反地，右半球處理感受、色彩和長期記憶。科學家認為兩個半球對各種學習都很重要，語言學習也包括在內。
科學家現在把左右半球和每個人學語言的方式連在一起。他們認為，有些學習者用其中一半大腦用得比另一半多。左腦型的學習者通常專注於背規則和清單，用邏輯、定義和反覆練習來學習。右腦型的學習者會先看整體的樣貌，專注於把新資訊和已經知道的東西連結起來，靠聯想和直覺來學習。大多數人都屬於這兩型的其中一種。如果老師知道學生是左腦型還是右腦型，就能幫助他們學得更好。

Scientists now relate left and right hemispheres to the way different individuals learn languages.

title: 電腦駭客與網路犯罪（Computer Hacking and Cybercrime）
paras: Breaking into the computer codes (known as 'hacking') of banks, large companies or even government departments is the latest game for super-intelligent teenagers. One young hacker said, "Hacking is just intellectual. It's your brain against the computer. It's like climbing Mount Everest—it's something you have to do. You don't even need a very expensive computer—but you must understand everything about all kinds of computers."

At the moment most of these games are just fun for young people. But how long will it be before criminal gangs, like the Mafia, start to use computer experts to help them in their crimes? Future bank robbers will not need explosives to blow open bank safes—all they will need is someone who can break computer codes. Already in Britain people say that computer crimes are costing companies between 500 million pounds and 2.5 billion pounds a year.
accuracyRateSource: 該屆逐題數據未公開

title: 大型車輛導致交通事故與資源消耗（Large Cars Causing Accidents and Resource Depletion）
paras: There is increasing scientific evidence that large cars cause more highway accidents than small cars. In the news recently was the story of a woman who died of a heart attack while driving her station wagon. The car was moving so fast that it went through the highway-dividing fence, resulting in a collision in which five people died. Those unnecessary deaths are attributable in part to the woman's choice of a large automobile. A lighter and smaller car probably wouldn't have gone through the fence, its remaining energy would have been much less, and this would have reduced the chances of serious injury or death. Because of its small size, it might have missed the other car completely. The present design of the oversized automobile is largely responsible not only for increasing death toll on the highways but also for the rapid depletion of our resources of petroleum, for the pollution of our environment, and for the congestion and inconvenience of our cities.
accuracyRateSource: 該屆逐題數據未公開

zh: 愈來愈多科學證據顯示，大型車在公路上造成的事故比小型車多。最近新聞報導，一位女士開著她的旅行車，在途中心臟病發死亡。車子開得太快，衝破了公路的分隔護欄，造成一場五個人死亡的車禍。這些原本可以避免的死亡，部分要歸咎於這位女士選擇了大型車。換成輕一點、小一點的車，大概就不會衝破護欄，剩下的能量也會小得多，嚴重受傷或死亡的機會就會降低。而且小車體積小，說不定能完全避開另一輛車。目前這種超大型汽車的設計，不但是公路死亡人數增加的主要原因，石油資源迅速枯竭、環境汙染，以及城市的交通擁擠和不便，也大多是它造成的。

title: 受困鯨魚的救援與野放（Rescue and Release of Stranded Whales）
paras: Three pilot whales are believed to be swimming freely off the Atlantic Coast today. Their names are Tag, Notch, and Baby. These seagoing mammals are among the lucky survivors of a whale-stranding last December at Cape Cod.

As many as 60 pilot whales swam ashore. Scientists are still trying to find out why whales have this self-destructive behavior. Many of the whales died on the beach—crushed by their own weight. Whale experts found Tag, Notch, Baby alive. The three were believed to be too young to survive on their own or returned to sea.

The three whales were taken in a van to the New England Aquarium in Boston, Mass. They were kept in a 60,000-gallon tank for seven months. Only a few people worked with the whales so that they would not become too accustomed to human beings.

Early this past summer the three whales were pronounced fit enough to be returned to the Atlantic Ocean. A month after their release, the whales were spotted. They were found in a group of 50 whales about 60 miles from where they had been set free.

多達 60 隻領航鯨游上了岸。科學家還在設法找出鯨魚為什麼會有這種自我毀滅的行為。很多鯨魚死在海灘上，是自己的體重把自己壓死的。鯨魚專家發現 Tag、Notch 和 Baby 還活著。一般認為這三隻年紀太小，沒辦法自己活下去，也沒辦法直接送回海裡。

title: 卡內基獎章：表彰英雄事蹟（Carnegie Medal: Honoring Heroic Deeds）
paras: Most heroes are people like you. But what makes them heroes? They find special courage when they need it. They are brave enough to help in an emergency while others may stand by. A hero sees what needs to be done and does it.
Sometimes heroes are rewarded for their brave acts. One such reward is the Carnegie Medal. It is given to people who act bravely and face danger to save the lives of others.

The medal was named after Andrew Carnegie. In 1886, Carnegie heard about a young man by the name of William Hunter who lost his life trying to save two other boys from drowning. Carnegie became a very rich businessman and set aside money to honor heroes like William. Sometimes these heroes are in need or are hurt. If so, they receive money as well as the Carnegie Medal.

Over 6,000 people have received the Carnegie Medal. Some have saved people from drowning or from burning buildings. Others have pulled people in front of moving trains or saved them from attacks by wild animals. All these heroes have one thing in common, however. They put someone else's safety ahead of their own.

有時候，英雄的勇敢行為會得到獎勵。卡內基獎章就是其中一種。這個獎章頒給勇敢行動、冒著危險去救別人性命的人。

已經有 6,000 多人獲得卡內基獎章。有些人從水裡或失火的建築物裡救出別人；也有人把人從疾駛而來的火車前拉開，或從野生動物的攻擊中救人。不過，這些英雄都有一個共同點：他們把別人的安全放在自己的安全之前。

title: 徒手攀爬世貿中心的 George Willig（George Willig's World Trade Center Climb）
paras: On May 26, 1977, George Willig traveled to the top of the 1,350-foot-tall World Trade Center in New York City. He did not take the elevator, however. Instead, like a human fly, George Willig climbed the outside of the immense 110-story building. His climb, which began at 6:30 a.m., took three and a half hours to finish.

At the top, Willig was greeted by both police and reporters. Some of the police officers asked him for his autograph. Then they wanted to put him in jail and charged him with violation of law for climbing the building without a permit. Furthermore, the city also planned to sue him for a quarter of a million dollars. The amount, the police department reported, would pay the costs of rushing special equipment and eighty police officers in order to save him.

By the next day, city officials had reevaluated the situation. At City Hall, Mayor Abraham Beame hosted a news conference that turned into a ceremony in George Willig's honor. Beame announced that the city would not punish "The Human Fly." Instead, he would be fined a penny for each of the 110 floors he had climbed. Instead of punishing Willig, the city treated him as a hero who attempted the impossible and met the challenge.

zh: 1977 年 5 月 26 日，George Willig 登上了紐約市 1,350 英尺高的世界貿易中心頂端。不過，他不是搭電梯上去的，而是像蒼蠅一樣，貼著這棟 110 層樓的巨大建築外牆往上爬。他從早上 6 點 30 分開始爬，花了三個半小時才爬完。
到了頂樓，迎接 Willig 的有警察，也有記者。有些警察還向他要簽名。接著警方想把他關進監獄，控告他未經許可攀爬大樓，觸犯法律。不只這樣，市政府還打算向他求償 25 萬美元。警察局說，這筆錢是用來支付緊急調派特殊裝備和 80 名警察去救他的費用。
到了第二天，市府官員重新評估了整件事。市長 Abraham Beame 在市政廳舉行記者會，結果記者會變成了表揚 George Willig 的典禮。Beame 宣布市政府不會處罰這位「人蒼蠅」（The Human Fly），只會照他爬的 110 層樓，每一層罰他一美分。市政府沒有處罰 Willig，反而把他當成敢於挑戰不可能、而且成功完成挑戰的英雄。

title: 印刷術的發展歷程（The Development of Printing）
paras: Printing is one of the most important means of communication. Without it you would not now be reading this passage. Even the development of radio and television has not diminished the importance of printing.
The first printing was done from wood blocks one letter at a time by hand. This was a slow process, requiring much skill and patience, and every page of every book had to be cut separately.

A great step forward was the use of movable type. The Chinese discovered this in the 11th century, but it was not known in Europe until about 1440. In this method of printing, individual letters were made from separate pieces of metal. If these letters were inked over and pressed on to paper, they would print the words. When the printing was finished, the letters could be taken apart and rearranged to print something else.

One of the first European books to be printed in movable type was Johannes Gutenberg's 42-line Bible. The first book to be printed likewise in English was about the history of Troy. It was printed in Flanders in 1474 by an Englishman, William Caxton. In 1476 he returned to England and established a printing press at Westminster. Altogether he printed nearly 80 books, many being his own translations from the French.

outline: 印刷是重要溝通方式，(Without it) 若無印刷，讀者無法閱讀此文，廣播電視發展也未減其重要性。
(The first printing was done from) 最初印刷使用木刻版，(This was a slow process) 過程緩慢耗時，每頁需單獨刻製。
(A great step forward was) 活字印刷術是重大進步，(The Chinese discovered this in the 11th century) 中國在 11 世紀發現，(but it was not known in Europe until about) 歐洲約 1440 年才知曉。
(In this method of printing) 活字印刷術用獨立金屬字元，(If) 字母組合好壓在紙上就能印刷，印完後可拆解重排。
(One of the first European books) 最早的歐洲活字印刷書之一是古騰堡的四十二行聖經，第一本英文書是 William Caxton 1474 年在法蘭德斯印的特洛伊歷史，(In 1476 he returned to England) 他 1476 年回英國設立印刷廠，一共印了將近 80 本書。

zh: 印刷是最重要的溝通方式之一。要是沒有印刷，你現在就不會在讀這篇文章。即使有了廣播和電視，印刷的重要性也沒有減少。
最早的印刷是用木板，一次一個字母，全靠手工雕刻。這個過程很慢，需要很多技巧和耐心，而且每一本書的每一頁都得分開來刻。
一大進步是活字的使用。中國人在 11 世紀就發明了活字，但歐洲一直到 1440 年左右才知道。用這種方法印刷，每個字母都是用一塊塊分開的金屬做成的。字母塗上墨水、壓到紙上，就能印出字來。印完以後，這些字母可以拆開來重新排列，印別的東西。
歐洲最早用活字印刷的書籍之一，是古騰堡的《四十二行聖經》。第一本同樣用活字印刷的英文書，內容是特洛伊的歷史，1474 年由一位英國人 William Caxton 在法蘭德斯印製。1476 年他回到英國，在西敏設立了一家印刷廠。他總共印了將近 80 本書，其中很多是他自己從法文翻譯過來的。
